definition_zh: 床垫；（用作缓冲的）垫子
definition_en: a thick pad filled with soft material, often with springs, that forms the layer of a bed you lie on
core_image: 一张厚实的床垫摊在地上，手按下去陷出印子，松手又慢慢复原
scene: 搬进新宿舍时，她发现床垫太薄，只好在上面又铺了一条毯子。When she moved into the new dorm, she found the mattress too thin and put a blanket over it.
sceneCN: 这里 mattress 是「床垫」（第 1 个义项：铺在床上、供人躺卧的厚垫）；句意：搬进新宿舍时，她发现床垫太薄，就在上面又铺了一条毯子。

derivatives.zh: 装有床垫的（多用于复合词）
床垫垫层；褥垫
床垫保护罩

senses.title: The pad of a bed
senses.definition: the thick soft layer of a bed that a person lies on
senses.definitionCN: 床上供人躺卧的厚软垫层
senses.example: The hotel mattress was so soft that I sank into it.
senses.exampleCN: 酒店的床垫太软了，我一躺就陷了进去。
senses.why: Arabic matrah meant a place where something is thrown down, and the cushion thrown on the floor for sleeping became the bed pad.
senses.whyCN: 阿拉伯语 matrah 意为「把东西扔下去的地方」，铺在地上睡觉的垫子后来就成了床上垫层。

senses.title: Mattresses as objects
senses.definition: a mattress as a countable item of bedroom furniture in daily trade
senses.definitionCN: 日常买卖语境中作为可数家具品的床垫
senses.example: We bought two new mattresses for the spare room.
senses.exampleCN: 我们给客房买了两张新床垫。
senses.why: English treats furniture items as countable, and a household phrase such as two new mattresses became normal after the pad stopped being a loose floor cushion.
senses.whyCN: 英语把家具当作可数名词，当这种垫子不再只是松散的地铺垫之后，诸如「两张新床垫」之类的家庭说法就成了常例。

senses.title: With springs or foam
senses.definition: a mattress built with springs, foam, or latex as a separate manufactured product
senses.definitionCN: 以弹簧、泡沫或乳胶等制成的独立产品
senses.example: Pocket sprung mattresses support the spine better.
senses.exampleCN: 袋装弹簧床垫对脊柱的支撑更好。
senses.why: The industrial age put springs and foam inside the pad, and the type of construction became a way of naming kinds of mattress.
senses.whyCN: 工业时代把弹簧与泡沫塞进垫子里，构造方式于是成了给床垫分类命名的手段。

senses.title: A protective cushion
senses.definition: a thick padded layer used to soften a fall or protect a surface
senses.definitionCN: 用于减轻撞击或保护表面的厚垫层
senses.example: Gymnasts land on a thick mattress after the vault.
senses.exampleCN: 体操运动员跳马后落在厚垫上。
senses.why: The idea of something thrown down to soften a fall stays visible in sport, where the protective pad borrows the mattress word.
senses.whyCN: 「扔下去以缓冲」的想法在体育中仍看得见，防护垫就借用了 mattress 这个词。

senses.title: Placed directly on the floor
senses.definition: a floor pad for sleeping or sitting, typical of the word when it first came into English
senses.definitionCN: 用于睡觉或坐卧的地面铺垫，是该词初入英语时的典型用法
senses.example: In summer the children slept on a mattress on the roof.
senses.exampleCN: 夏天孩子们睡在屋顶的垫子上。
senses.why: When the word entered English it still named a pad laid straight on the floor, and that older use survives where a floor bed is natural.
senses.whyCN: 这个词初入英语时仍指直接铺在地上的垫子，在习惯睡地铺的场合，这一较早的用法依然存活。

senses.title: A makeshift bed
senses.definition: an improvised bed made from a mattress laid on the ground
senses.definitionCN: 用垫子铺在地上临时搭成的床
senses.example: He threw a mattress on the floor for his cousin.
senses.exampleCN: 他在地上丢了个床垫给表弟当床。
senses.why: The Arabic source meant a place where something is thrown down, so a mattress tossed on the floor still echoes the original picture.
senses.whyCN: 阿拉伯语词源意为把东西扔放下去的地方，所以随手丢在地上的床垫仍回响着最初的画面。

intro.en: Mattress comes through Old French and Italian from Arabic matrah, a place where something is thrown down, reinforced by the Arabic phrase al-matrah, the cushion or the place of throwing.
intro.cn: mattress 经古法语与意大利语来自阿拉伯语 matrah（扔放东西之处），并受阿拉伯语短语 al-matrah（垫子、扔放之处）的影响。

items.en: Matrah means a place where something is thrown or laid down, and al-matrah names the cushion laid on the floor.
items.cn: 阿拉伯语 matrah 意为扔下或铺下东西的地方，al-matrah 指铺在地上的垫子。

items.en: Materasso carries the Arabic word into Italian trade vocabulary for a bed cushion.
items.cn: 意大利语 materasso 把这个阿拉伯词带入意大利商贸用语，指床上垫子。

items.en: Materas names a quilted or stuffed bed covering, put on a bed base or the floor.
items.cn: 古法语 materas 指填充过的床上垫子，铺在床架或地板上。

items.en: Materas and materace appear, and the word names a stuffed pad for sleeping.
items.cn: 中古英语出现 matheras 一类拼写，指睡觉用的填充垫。

items.en: The spelling settles toward mattress, and the pad becomes part of the standard bed.
items.cn: 拼写逐渐固定为 mattress，垫子成为标准床铺的一部分。

items.en: Springs, foam, and latex make the mattress a manufactured product, and a protective cushion sense appears in sport.
items.cn: 弹簧、泡沫与乳胶使床垫成为工业产品，体育中又出现缓冲垫义。

note.en: Mattress is the stuffed bed pad whose name travels from Arabic through French, and it is easily confused with bedding terms and with similar-looking words.
note.cn: mattress 是填充的床上厚垫，名字经法语源自阿拉伯语，与床上用品词相邻，也容易与拼写相近的词混淆。

entries.definition: a woman in charge of a household
entries.definitionCN: 女主人；只是拼写相近，词源不同，来自 master

a removable cloth cover for a mattress

normalIntro.en: Mattress reaches English through Arabic al-matrah, the place where a cushion is thrown down for sleeping.
normalIntro.cn: mattress 经阿拉伯语 al-matrah 进入英语，指铺下垫子睡觉的地方。

normal.en: Mattress comes from Arabic matrah, a place where something is thrown down.
normal.cn: mattress 来自阿拉伯语 matrah，指把东西铺放下去的地方。

normal.en: A mattress pad is the thin layer you add over the mattress.
normal.cn: mattress pad 是加在床垫上面的薄垫层。

normal.en: The plural doubles the final s before it: mattresses.
normal.cn: 复数在 s 前双写，写作 mattresses。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with mistress, which comes from master.
normal.cn: 别和 mistress 混了，后者来自 master。

normal.en: Compare with quilt: the quilt is the cover, while the mattress is the layer you lie on.
normal.cn: 对比 quilt：quilt 是盖着的被子，mattress 则是躺着的垫层。

abstract.en: Picture pressing a hand into a thick mattress and watching it slowly rise back.
abstract.cn: 想象手掌按进厚床垫，再慢慢弹回原样。

abstract.en: Picture a mattress on a bare floor, with a pillow and one folded blanket.
abstract.cn: 想象光地板上铺着一张床垫，上面一个枕头和一条叠好的毯子。

abstract.en: Picture movers rolling a mattress up the stairs with their backs bent.
abstract.cn: 想象搬家工人弯着腰把床垫卷着抬上楼。

examples.en: The mattress was old and lumpy, so she saved for a new one.
examples.cn: 那张床垫又旧又硬，所以她攒钱买新的。

examples.en: Air the mattress every week during the summer.
examples.cn: 夏天每周都要晾晒床垫。

examples.en: A good mattress makes a big difference to sleep.
examples.cn: 一张好床垫对睡眠影响很大。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「麦特瑞斯」——一张铺在床上的厚垫子；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 阿拉伯语 matrah（扔放东西之处）→ 意大利语 materasso → 古法语 materas → 中古英语 matheras → 英语 mattress，核心义「铺下填充足量的厚垫」。

sensesIntro.en: Mattress starts with the pad of a bed, then counts as furniture, a product, a protective cushion, and an improvised floor bed of earlier English.
sensesIntro.cn: mattress 先从床上的垫层说起，再指可数的家具、产品、缓冲垫，以及英语早期使用的地铺垫。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thick pad laid down for a body to rest on.
core.cn: 核心意象：铺下来让人躺卧的厚垫。

branches.en: The bed pad is the central sense.
branches.cn: 床垫义是中心义。

branches.en: Countable items and spring or foam products widen the pad into goods.
branches.cn: 可数个体与弹簧泡沫产品把垫子扩展为商品。

branches.en: The protective cushion keeps the throwing-down image.
branches.cn: 缓冲垫义保留了「铺下去」的意象。

branches.en: The floor pad is the older sense in English.
branches.cn: 地铺垫是英语中较早的义项。

branches.en: A mattress on the floor makes the simplest spare bed.
branches.cn: 地上一张床垫就是最简单的临时床。

intro.en: Mattress has no productive English affix of its own; its family comes from compounds such as mattress pad and from the Arabic-derived base.
intro.cn: mattress 本身没有产出性的英语词缀，它的词族来自 mattress pad 这类复合词以及阿拉伯语来源的词根。

latinIntro.en: Mattress has no Latin source, so the Latin-derived list here is empty; the word travels from Arabic matrah through Italian and French.
latinIntro.cn: mattress 没有拉丁语来源，所以这里的拉丁同源词条目留空；这个词从阿拉伯语 matrah 经意大利语与法语而来。

items.example: Matrah is the ultimate source.
items.exampleCN: matrah 是最终来源。

items.example: The Arabic phrase strengthens the cushion sense.
items.exampleCN: 这一阿拉伯语短语强化了「垫子」义。

items.example: Italian materasso carries the word northward.
items.exampleCN: 意大利语 materasso 把词带向北方。

items.example: Old French materas reaches English.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 materas 抵达英语。

items.example: Mattress is the modern form.
items.exampleCN: mattress 是现代表。

items.meaningCN: 以 s 结尾时的复数后缀
items.example: The suffix -es gives mattresses.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -es 构成 mattresses。

items.meaning: a thin layer over a mattress
items.example: The compound adds pad.
items.exampleCN: 复合词加上 pad。

items.meaning: a cover that protects a mattress
items.example: The compound adds protector.
items.exampleCN: 复合词加上 protector。

definition_zh: 成熟；成熟过程；（疾病或症状的）完全形成、发作；陈化；成熟期
definition_en: the process of becoming fully developed or ripe, whether of a person, a living thing, a product, or an illness
core_image: 青涩的果子在枝头一天天变红，摸上去越来越软，最后熟透落地
scene: 夏末的果园里，农人每天到树下查看果实的成色。By late summer, the farmer walks among the trees each day to judge the slow maturation of the fruit before picking.
sceneCN: 这里 maturation 是「成熟过程」（第 1 个义项：生物或事物逐渐发育完全的过程）；句意：到了夏末，农人每天在果树间走动，判断果实是否已缓慢成熟，准备采摘。

pos.zh: （疾病的）完全形成与发作；陈化；熟化

forms.label: 形容词比较级（由 maturer 改写）
形容词最高级（由 maturest 改写）

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁词干加英语 -e 构成，形容词义为「成熟的」，动词义为「使成熟；成熟」
词干 matur- + -ity，表示成熟的状态或时期，比 maturation 更强调结果与状态
maturation + -al，指「与成熟过程有关的」，常见于发育学与医学文献
否定前缀 im- + mature，指「未成熟的；幼稚的」
前缀 pre-（在……之前）+ mature，指「过早的；未到期的」，如早产
词干 matur- + -ate，医学上表示「化脓；（伤口）成熟」，日常少用

senses.title: Becoming fully developed
senses.definition: the natural process by which a living thing grows and becomes fully developed
senses.definitionCN: 生物自然生长发育、逐步达到完全成熟的过程
senses.example: The maturation of the brain continues well into the teens.
senses.exampleCN: 大脑的成熟会一直持续到青少年时期。
senses.why: Latin maturus means ripe, and -ation names the process, so maturation is literally the ripening.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 maturus 意为「成熟的」，后缀 -ation 表示过程，所以 maturation 字面就是「变熟的过程」，核心画面是果子一天天熟透。

senses.title: Personal growth
senses.definition: the process of becoming mature in character, judgment, or skill
senses.definitionCN: 性格、判断力或技能逐渐走向成熟的过程
senses.example: Years of travel contributed to her emotional maturation.
senses.exampleCN: 多年的旅行促成了她情感上的成熟。
senses.why: The ripening image is applied to the mind: ideas and judgment need time before they are fully formed.
senses.whyCN: 「变熟」的画面被移用到心智上：想法和判断需要时间才能长成，就像果子需要日晒，所以这个义项强调人格与判断力的成长。

senses.title: Ripening or ageing of a product
senses.definition: the process by which food, wine, or a material improves as it ages
senses.definitionCN: 食品、酒或材料随时间存放而变得更好的过程
senses.example: The cheese needs six months of maturation in the cellar.
senses.exampleCN: 这种奶酪需要在地窖里陈化六个月。
senses.why: The same ripening turn is given to things that are not alive: cheese, wine, and timber mature in storage.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「熟成」转向了非生命的东西：奶酪、葡萄酒、木材放在仓里也会「变熟」，所以 maturation 又指带有改善意味的存放与陈化。

senses.title: Full development of an illness
senses.definition: the stage at which symptoms of a disease become fully present
senses.definitionCN: 疾病的症状完全显现出来的阶段
senses.example: Doctors watched for the maturation of the disease before treating it.
senses.exampleCN: 医生在治疗之前先观察这种疾病是否已完全发作。
senses.why: Because ripening can end in bursting, medical English borrowed the word for a condition that has fully ripened into an outbreak.
senses.whyCN: 果实熟到最后会绽开，医学英语借用这一画面，把完全发作的病情说成已经「长熟」，于是有了这个略带警告意味的用法。

senses.title: The mature period
senses.definition: the period in which a thing is fully grown or at its best
senses.definitionCN: 事物完全长成或处于最佳状态的时期
senses.example: Their best work came during the maturation of the program.
senses.exampleCN: 他们最好的作品出现在这个项目走向成熟的那段时期。
senses.why: Every ripening has a moment of fullness, and that moment can be named as a period rather than a process.
senses.whyCN: 每一次熟成都有一刻到达饱满，把那一刻拉长成一段时间，过程义便转成了「成熟期」这个时期义。

intro.en: Maturation comes through French, from Latin maturatio, a ripening, built on maturus, ripe, and the verb maturare.
intro.cn: maturation 经法语进入英语，源于拉丁语 maturatio（成熟、变熟），由形容词 maturus（成熟的）与动词 maturare 构成。

items.en: Maturus means ripe or timely, probably linked to mane, the early morning.
items.cn: maturus 意为「成熟的；及时的」，一般认为与 mane（清晨）有关，因为一早就是时候到了。

items.en: Maturare means to ripen or to hurry something to its right time.
items.cn: maturare 意为「使成熟；赶在合适的时候做成」。

items.en: The noun maturatio names the act or process of ripening.
items.cn: 名词 maturatio 指「变熟」这一动作或过程。

items.en: Maturation carries the ripening noun into French and then towards English.
items.cn: maturation 把「变熟」这一名词带入法语，再传向英语。

items.en: English borrows maturation, first for plants and produce.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 maturation，早期多用于植物与农产品。

items.en: Biology, medicine, and industry extend it to organs, illnesses, and stored goods.
items.cn: 现代英语把它的使用面扩展到器官、疾病以及存放的货物。

note.en: Maturation sits with mature, maturity, and premature, and is close in meaning to words for growth, development, and ageing.
note.cn: maturation 与 mature、maturity、premature 同属一词族，意义上与表示生长、发展、老成的词相邻，区别在于它侧重「正在变熟的过程」。

the state of being mature
happening or born before the proper time
the process of increasing in size or amount
the process of becoming larger, stronger, or more advanced
the process of becoming ripe

normalIntro.en: Maturation is the noun of ripening: maturus means ripe, and the suffix names the process rather than the state.
normalIntro.cn: maturation 是「变熟」的名词：词根 maturus 意为成熟，后缀 -ation 表示过程，所以它强调的是「正在成熟」而不是「已经成熟」。

normal.en: The suffix -ation turns a verb or stem into the name of a process, as mature becomes maturation.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ation 把动词或词干变成「过程」的名词，mature 因此变成 maturation。

normal.en: Compare maturity: maturity is the state of being mature, maturation is the journey towards it.
normal.cn: 对比 maturity：maturity 是成熟的状态，maturation 是走向成熟的路程。

normal.en: Premature means before the time is ripe, the same matur- stem with a pre- in front.
normal.cn: premature 意为「在成熟之前」，正是同一词干 matur- 前面加了 pre-。

normal.en: In dictionaries maturation of an illness means the stage when its symptoms are fully formed.
normal.cn: 词典里 maturation of an illness 指症状完全形成的阶段，是医学上的固定说法。

normal.en: Use the phrase the maturation of with abstract nouns, as in the maturation of ideas.
normal.cn: 常用搭配「the maturation of」接抽象名词，如思想的成熟，比单纯说成熟更强调过程。

abstract.en: Picture a green apple turning red, softening day by day under the sun.
abstract.cn: 想象一只青苹果在太阳下一天天变红、变软，直到熟透。

abstract.en: Imagine a teenager whose ideas slowly harden into clear judgments.
abstract.cn: 想象一个少年，想法慢慢沉淀成清晰的判断，这就是心智的成熟。

abstract.en: Think of a cellar where bottles lie in the dark while everything inside quietly improves.
abstract.cn: 想象一个地窖，酒瓶躺在黑暗里，瓶中的东西却在悄悄变好，这就是陈化。

examples.en: Scientists link the maturation of the brain to better self-control.
examples.cn: 科学家把大脑的成熟与更好的自控力联系起来。

examples.en: The wine benefits from several years of maturation in oak barrels.
examples.cn: 这种葡萄酒在橡木桶里陈化几年会更好。

examples.en: Early experiences can shape mental maturation later in life.
examples.cn: 童年的经历会影响日后心智的成熟。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马 丘 雷 神」——想象一匹马在田丘上被雷声催熟，果子一下子全红了；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 maturus（成熟的）→ maturare（使成熟）→ maturatio（变熟）→ 古法语 maturation → 英语 maturation，核心义「由生到熟」。

sensesIntro.en: Maturation starts as the ripening of a living thing, stretches to a persons growth and to stored goods, and finally names the moment a disease has fully ripened.
sensesIntro.cn: maturation 从生物的发育成熟出发，扩展到人的心智成长与物品的陈化，最后还用来指疾病完全发作的那一刻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a green fruit slowly ripening on the branch.
core.cn: 核心意象：枝头一只青果慢慢熟透。

branches.en: The natural ripening of a living thing is the base sense.
branches.cn: 生物的发育成熟是基础义项。

branches.en: Growth of judgment is the human sense.
branches.cn: 心智判断力的成长是人间义项。

branches.en: Storing wine or cheese transfers the word to goods.
branches.cn: 酒与奶酪的存放把词义转到货物上，即陈化。

branches.en: Sickness that ripens into an outbreak borrows from the fruit.
branches.cn: 病情「长熟」后完全发作，是从果子借来的说法。

branches.en: The process of maturing and the period of maturity are the same ripening seen as a journey or a place.
branches.cn: 成熟的过程与成熟期，是同一场「变熟」被看成旅程或看成站点。

intro.en: Maturation is a Latin process noun built on matur-, the stem of maturus, with the suffix -ation; English also has mature, maturity, and premature around it.
intro.cn: maturation 是由拉丁词干 matur-（源自 maturus，成熟）加上后缀 -ation 构成的过程名词，英语中围绕它还有 mature、maturity、premature。

latinIntro.en: Latin maturus means ripe, maturare means to ripen, and maturatio names the ripening.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 maturus 意为「成熟的」，maturare 意为「使成熟」，maturatio 则指「变熟」这一过程。

items.example: The stem matur- appears in mature, maturity, and maturation.
items.exampleCN: 词干 matur- 出现在 mature、maturity、maturation 里。

items.example: Maturus describes fruit that is ready to pick.
items.exampleCN: maturus 形容可以采摘的果子。

items.meaning: to ripen, to bring to maturity
items.example: Maturare gives the verb sense of the family.
items.exampleCN: maturare 提供这个词族的动词义。

items.example: Maturatio is the direct model for the English noun.
items.exampleCN: maturatio 是这个英语名词的直接原型。

items.meaning: the act or process of doing something
items.meaningCN: 表示动作或过程的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ation turns verbs into process nouns.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 把动词变成表示过程的名词。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ity forms maturity from the same stem.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 用同一词干构成 maturity，指成熟的状态。

items.example: The prefix im- creates immature.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 im- 构成 immature，表示未成熟。

items.example: The prefix pre- creates premature.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 pre- 构成 premature，表示过早的。

items.example: The rare verb maturate keeps the suffix -ate.
items.exampleCN: 少用的动词 maturate 保留了这个词尾。

items.example: Maturational changes appear in child development studies.
items.exampleCN: 发育研究里会出现「与成熟有关的变化」这一说法。

definition_zh: 使最大化；使增至最大；充分利用；把……开到最大；（计算机中）将窗口放到最大
definition_en: to make something as large, as great, or as useful as it can possibly be
core_image: 一只手把旋钮拧到最右端，仪表指针顶到最大刻度
scene: 工厂里，班长想把每条生产线的产量都提到极限，于是把排班表排得满满当当。The foreman rearranged the shifts to maximise output from every line without adding a single worker.
sceneCN: 这里 maximise 是「使最大化」（第 1 个义项：使某物尽可能大或尽可能多）；句意：班长重新安排了班次，在不多加一名工人的情况下，让每条生产线的产量都达到最大。

pos.zh: 使最大化；使增至最大；充分利用
使窗口最大化；取值达到最大

derivatives.zh: maximise + -ation，义为「最大化；最大限度利用」
由拉丁词干 maxim- 直接构成，义为「最大值；最大的」
maxim- + -al，义为「最大的；极度的」，常用于数学与逻辑
同一动词的美式拼写，词尾 -ize 与英式 -ise 对应
maximise + -er，义为「使最大化的人或事物」，也可指只追求最优结果的人

senses.title: To make as large as possible
senses.definition: to increase something to its greatest possible size, amount, or value
senses.definitionCN: 把某物的规模、数量或价值提高到尽可能大的程度
senses.example: The company aims to maximise profits this year.
senses.exampleCN: 公司今年的目标是让利润最大化。
senses.why: Latin maximus means greatest, and the suffix -ise means to make, so the word literally means to make greatest.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 maximus 意为「最大的」，后缀 -ise 表示「使……」，所以这个词字面就是「使成为最大」，核心画面是旋钮拧到尽头。

senses.title: To use fully
senses.definition: to make the best possible use of something such as time, space, or a chance
senses.definitionCN: 把时间、空间或机会利用到最好
senses.example: She rearranged her day to maximise study time.
senses.exampleCN: 她重新安排了日程，以便充分利用学习时间。
senses.why: When the thing being increased is not a number but a resource, the same turning-up gesture becomes making full use of it.
senses.whyCN: 要变大的东西从数字换成了资源时，同样是「拧到头」的动作，含义就变成把资源用足用尽，所以这个义项侧重「别浪费」。

senses.title: To set to the highest level
senses.definition: to set a control, sound, or setting to its highest level
senses.definitionCN: 把控制、音量或设置调到最高档
senses.example: He maximised the volume to drown out the traffic.
senses.exampleCN: 他把音量开到最大，好盖过车流声。
senses.why: A dial that has been turned fully clockwise shows the maximum as a visible position, so the word also names that final click.
senses.whyCN: 把旋钮顺时针拧到底时，「最大」成了一个看得见的位置，于是这个词也用来指「调到最大」这一最后一步。

senses.title: To enlarge a window
senses.definition: to make a computer window fill the whole screen
senses.definitionCN: 让电脑窗口铺满整个屏幕
senses.example: Use the top right corner to maximise the window.
senses.exampleCN: 使用右上角的按钮可以把窗口最大化。
senses.why: On a screen, the fullest possible size is the full screen, so software makes the old image of the extreme setting its most literal use.
senses.whyCN: 在屏幕上，能占的最大面积就是整块屏幕，所以软件把这个词原本「达到极限」的画面用得最为字面。

intro.en: Maximise is a modern verbal form built from Latin maximus, greatest, the superlative of magnus, and the suffix -ise.
intro.cn: maximise 是现代英语用拉丁语 maximus（最大的，magnus「大」的最高级）加后缀 -ise 构成的动词。

items.en: Magnus means great or large, and maximus is its superlative, greatest.
items.cn: magnus 意为「大的」，maximus 是它的最高级，意为「最大的」。

items.en: Maxima is used in mathematics as the name for the greatest value.
items.cn: 数学中已有 maxima 一词，用来指「最大值」。

items.en: Maximum enters English in the eighteenth century as a technical and scientific term.
items.cn: maximum 在十八世纪以科技术语的身份进入英语。

items.en: The verb form maximise appears, first in mathematics and economics.
items.cn: 动词形式 maximise 出现，最初用于数学和经济学。

items.en: Maximise spreads to management, computing, and everyday settings such as volume.
items.cn: 现代英语把它扩展到管理、计算机以及音量等日常设置上。

note.en: Maximise belongs to the Latin maximum family, with maximum, maximal, and maximise, and it stands near words for increasing and using things well.
note.cn: maximise 属于拉丁「最大」词族，与 maximum、maximal 同源；在意义上与表示增加、提高、充分利用的词相邻，但强调「推到极限」这一终点。

entries.definition: the largest amount that is possible
as large as possible
the same verb spelled with -ize
entries.definitionCN: 同一动词的美式拼写，词尾写作 -ize

entries.definition: to become or make larger in amount
to increase or improve something quickly
to make something as effective as possible

normalIntro.en: Maximise pairs the Latin root maxim-, meaning greatest, with the suffix -ise, which means to make.
normalIntro.cn: maximise 由拉丁词根 maxim-（最大的）加上后缀 -ise（使……）组成，所以它天生就是「使它变成最大」的意思。

normal.en: Latin magnus gives great, and maximus is its superlative, so maxim- carries the idea of greatest.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 magnus 意为「大的」，maximus 是最高级，所以词根 maxim- 带着「最大」的意味。

normal.en: The suffix -ise turns adjectives and nouns into verbs meaning to make or cause.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ise 把形容词或名词变成「使……；造成……」的动词，如 maximise、modernise。

normal.en: Compare maximum and maximise: maximum is the top point, maximise is the act of getting there.
normal.cn: 对比 maximum 与 maximise：maximum 是顶点的值，maximise 是爬到顶点的动作。

normal.en: British writing uses -ise, American writing uses -ize, so maximisation and maximization are the same noun.
normal.cn: 英式写 -ise，美式写 -ize，所以 maximisation 与 maximization 是同一个名词。

normal.en: Business English has ready pairs such as maximise profits and maximise efficiency.
normal.cn: 商务英语里有现成的搭配，如使利润最大化、最大限度地提高效率。

abstract.en: Picture one finger turning a dial all the way to the right until it clicks.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指把旋钮一直拧到最右边，直到咔嗒一声停住。

abstract.en: Imagine packing a suitcase so full that the zip barely closes, using every gap.
abstract.cn: 想象把行李箱塞到几乎拉不上拉链，每个缝隙都塞满，这就是充分利用。

abstract.en: Think of a phone with the volume bar filled to the very last square.
abstract.cn: 想象手机音量条被填满到最后一格，这就是把声音开到最大。

examples.en: Firms use software to maximise the value of their data.
examples.cn: 各公司用软件让数据的价值最大化。

examples.en: Resting before an exam maximises your chance of remembering things.
examples.cn: 考前休息能最大化你记住内容的机会。

examples.en: Please maximise the window so we can all see the chart.
examples.cn: 请把窗口最大化，让大家都能看到图表。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马 克 西 买 子」——想买马可西家的「最大号」鞋子，非最大号不要；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 magnus（大的）→ 最高级 maximus（最大的）→ 英语 maximum（最大值）→ maximise（使达到最大），核心义「拉到尽头」。

sensesIntro.en: Maximise begins with numbers and amounts, widens to resources that can be used fully, then moves to controls such as volume and finally to a window filling the screen.
sensesIntro.cn: maximise 先从数字与数量起步，扩展到可以「用足」的资源，再指音量等控制项调到最大，最后用于让窗口铺满屏幕。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dial turned all the way to its highest mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：旋钮被拧到刻度的尽头。

branches.en: Numbers pushed to their ceiling give the base sense.
branches.cn: 把数字推到上限，是这个词的基础义项。

branches.en: Resources used to the last drop are the practical sense.
branches.cn: 把资源用到一滴不剩，是实用层面的义项。

branches.en: A volume control at its top position is the physical sense.
branches.cn: 音量控制处在最高档，是这个词的物理义项。

branches.en: A window filling the screen is the most literal modern use.
branches.cn: 窗口铺满整个屏幕，是它在当代最字面的用法。

branches.en: Profits and study time are both increased to the point where nothing more can be gained.
branches.cn: 利润与学习时间都是增加到再无可增的地步，二者同源。

intro.en: Maximise is built on the Latin superlative stem maxim-, to which English adds the verb suffix -ise, as it does in modernise and optimise.
intro.cn: maximise 由拉丁最高级词干 maxim- 加英语动词后缀 -ise 构成，和 modernise、optimise 的构词方式一样。

latinIntro.en: Latin magnus means great, maximus means greatest, and the noun maximum means the greatest thing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 magnus 意为「大的」，maximus 意为「最大的」，名词 maximum 意为「最大的东西」。

items.example: The stem maxim- appears in maximum, maximal, and maximise.
items.exampleCN: 词干 maxim- 出现在 maximum、maximal 与 maximise 里。

items.example: Magnus is the root behind maximus and magnitude.
items.exampleCN: magnus 是 maximus 与 magnitude 背后的词根。

items.example: Maximus is the superlative of magnus.
items.exampleCN: maximus 是 magnus 的最高级。

items.example: Maximum is the noun from which the verb was built.
items.exampleCN: maximum 是这个动词所依托的名词。

items.meaning: to make, to cause to be
items.example: The suffix -ise turns maximum into an action.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ise 把 maximum 变成动作。

items.example: Maximize is the American spelling of the same verb.
items.exampleCN: maximize 是同一动词的美式拼写。

items.meaning: the act or process of doing something
items.meaningCN: 表示动作或过程的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ation forms maximisation.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 构成 maximisation，表示最大化的过程。

items.example: The suffix -al forms maximal.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -al 构成 maximal。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does
items.meaningCN: 表示做某事的人或物的词尾
items.example: The suffix -er forms maximizer.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 maximizer。

items.meaning: to make as effective as possible
items.example: Optimise uses the same -ise pattern as maximise.
items.exampleCN: optimise 与 maximise 使用同样的 -ise 构词法。

definition_zh: 草地；牧场； meadow（供收割牧草的田野）；水边低洼的草甸
definition_en: a field of grass and wild flowers, often one that is cut for hay or kept for grazing
core_image: 一片开阔的绿草地，草长到膝盖高，其间点缀着野花，边缘是石墙
scene: 春天一到，村外那块地就开满了黄花，风一吹像水面一样起伏。Every spring the wide river meadow beyond the village turns golden and rolls in the wind like the surface of a lake.
sceneCN: 这里 meadow 是「河边草甸」（第 3 个义项：河边低洼、常被水淹的草地）；句意：每逢春天，村外那片宽阔的河边草甸就变成金黄色，像湖面一样随风起伏。

forms.label: 复合词（草地甜草；山芥草）

derivatives.zh: meadow + land（地）构成的复合词，义为「草地；牧草地」
meadow + -y（具有……特性的），义为「多草的；像草地的」
meadow + lark（云雀）构成的复合词，北美草原云雀，叫声响亮
meadow + sweet（甜的）构成的复合词，指草地上的绣线菊类植物

senses.title: A field of grass and flowers
senses.definition: an open field covered with grass and wild flowers
senses.definitionCN: 长满青草与野花的开阔田野
senses.example: Bees buzzed across the wide meadow.
senses.exampleCN: 蜜蜂在宽阔的草地上嗡嗡飞过。
senses.why: Old English maedwe came from the root magon, meaning to mow, so a meadow was first a field meant for cutting.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 maedwe 来自词根 magon（割草），所以草地最初就是「准备割草的那块地」，画面是满地长草、等人来割。

senses.title: A place for hay
senses.definition: a field where grass is grown and cut to make hay
senses.definitionCN: 专门种草、割草制干草的田地
senses.example: Farmers scythe the meadow in late June.
senses.exampleCN: 农夫在六月底割草地里的草做干草。
senses.why: The mowing root lives on here: this sense keeps the meadow at the moment when it is cut and dried for winter feed.
senses.whyCN: 「割草」的词根在这一义项里最直接：这块地存在的意义就是被割下、晒干，留到冬天喂牲口，所以它是牧场而不是风景。

senses.title: Low ground by a river
senses.definition: low grassy ground beside a river, often flooded in winter
senses.definitionCN: 河边低洼、冬季常被水淹的草地
senses.example: The river meadow floods every winter and sings with frogs in spring.
senses.exampleCN: 河边草甸每到冬天就被淹，春天则到处是蛙鸣。
senses.why: Riverside meadows depended on seasonal water to grow well, so meadow also names the wet lowland by a stream.
senses.whyCN: 河边的草要靠冬天漫上来的水才长得旺，于是草地一词也用来指水边那块易淹的低地，带上了水的意味。

intro.en: Meadow is a native Old English word from maedwe, which is generally believed to come from a Germanic root meaning to mow.
intro.cn: meadow 是古英语固有词，来自 maedwe，一般认为源于日耳曼语词根 magon（割草）。

items.en: A reconstructed root magon, meaning a mowing, is generally taken as the base.
items.cn: 一般认为其根源是重构形式 magon，意为「割草」。

items.en: Maedwe names a grassland that is mown for hay.
items.cn: maedwe 指专门割草制干草的草地。

items.en: Related forms such as mawe, a mowing, sit beside it in the same family.
items.cn: 同族的 mawe（割草）等相关形式也出现在这一家族里。

items.en: Medwe is respelled towards the modern shape and widens to any grassy field.
items.cn: 中古英语 medwe 的拼写逐渐接近现代形式，含义扩展到一般意义上的草地。

items.en: Meadow keeps a gentle, literary and pastoral tone, often in place names.
items.cn: 现代英语中 meadow 保持温和、文学化的田园色彩，也常出现在地名里。

note.en: Meadow shares the mowing family with mow and the compound meadowlark, and it stands near field, pasture, and grassland.
note.cn: meadow 与 mow、meadowlark 同属「割草」词族，意义上与 field、pasture、grassland 相邻，区别在于它自带「长着野花、可割草」的田园气息。

entries.definition: to cut grass or crops with a blade
a North American songbird of open fields
a tall plant with clusters of small flowers
entries.definitionCN: 绣线菊；草地上的小花植物

entries.definition: an area of open land used for crops or animals
land covered with grass for grazing animals
large areas of land covered with grass

normalIntro.en: Meadow is an old farming word whose core is the mowing of grass.
normalIntro.cn: meadow 是一个古老的农事词，核心始终是「割草」这件事。

normal.en: The root links meadow to mow, because a meadow is a field kept for cutting grass.
normal.cn: 词根把 meadow 与 mow（割草）连在一起：草地本质上是留着割草的田。

normal.en: A water meadow is fed by a river every winter so the grass grows thick.
normal.cn: water meadow（水草地）靠每年冬天的河水漫灌，草才长得特别厚。

normal.en: Wildflower meadows hold many small plants that are lost in mown grass.
normal.cn: 野花草甸保住了许多小植物，而这些植物在常年割短的草里活不下来。

normal.en: Compare field: a field may grow wheat, a meadow is mainly grass and flowers.
normal.cn: 对比 field：field 可以种麦子，meadow 则以草和野花为主，更接近牧场。

normal.en: The compound word meadowlark names a bird that sings over open grass.
normal.cn: 复合词 meadowlark 指一种在开阔草地上歌唱的鸟，可见 meadow 的画面感。

abstract.en: Picture a low green strip of grass by a river, dotted with yellow and white flowers.
abstract.cn: 想象河畔一条低低的绿草带，点缀着黄白相间的野花。

abstract.en: Imagine a long row of cut grass drying in the sun, then being gathered into hay.
abstract.cn: 想象割下的草被摊成长长的一条在阳光下晒干，然后堆成干草，这就是牧场。

abstract.en: Think of spring water rising over the river field, then falling back as the grass grows greener.
abstract.cn: 想象春水漫过河边的低地，退去之后草却更绿了，这就是水边草甸。

examples.en: Cows graze in the meadow behind the old farmhouse.
examples.cn: 奶牛在旧农舍后面的草地上吃草。

examples.en: The wildflower meadow attracts butterflies all summer.
examples.cn: 这片野花草甸整个夏天都吸引着蝴蝶。

examples.en: They spread the cut grass across the meadow to dry.
examples.cn: 他们把割下的草铺在草地上晾干。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「没 到」——夏天一过，草地就「没到」膝盖了，草深得看不见脚；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 maedwe（草地）→ 一般认为来自日耳曼语词根 magon（割草）→ 中古英语 medwe → 现代英语 meadow，核心义「长着草、等着割的田」。

sensesIntro.en: Meadow opens with the grassy field itself, sharpens into the hay field that was mown, and then points to the wet lowland by a river.
sensesIntro.cn: meadow 先从「长满草和花的田野」说起，再聚焦到准备割草做干草的那块田，最后指向河边易淹的低洼草甸。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wide green field of tall grass and wild flowers.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片长着高草与野花的开阔绿野。

branches.en: The basic grassy field is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 长草的开阔田野是日常义项。

branches.en: The field set aside for hay is the farming sense.
branches.cn: 专门割草制干草的田是农事义项。

branches.en: The lowland fed by a river is the landscape sense.
branches.cn: 靠河水滋养的低地是地貌义项。

branches.en: Both senses are open grass, one seen as ground, one seen as wet ground.
branches.cn: 两种义项都是开阔的草，一个看成土地，一个看成湿润的土地。

branches.en: Flowers and hay belong to the same summer meadow before it is cut.
branches.cn: 野花与干草属于同一片夏日草地，割草前后是同一条命脉。

intro.en: Meadow is a native English noun, not a Latin borrowing; English turns it into compounds such as meadowland and meadowlark.
intro.cn: meadow 是英语固有名词，并非拉丁借词；英语把它组合成 meadowland、meadowlark 等复合词。

latinIntro.en: Meadow has no Latin source, though the Latin pratum for meadow is a common parallel in European languages.
latinIntro.cn: meadow 没有拉丁语来源，但拉丁语的 pratum（草地）在欧洲语言里是一个常见的对照词。

items.example: Meadow is the base word of the family.
items.exampleCN: meadow 是这个词族的基础词。

items.example: Mow shares the old mowing root with meadow.
items.exampleCN: mow 与 meadow 共用一个古老词根「割草」。

items.example: The plural meadows names several fields at once.
items.exampleCN: 复数 meadows 一下子指好几片草地。

items.example: Meadow plus land gives meadowland.
items.exampleCN: meadow 加 land 构成 meadowland，指草地、牧草地。

items.example: The suffix -y forms meadowy.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 构成 meadowy，指多草的。

items.example: Meadow plus lark gives meadowlark.
items.exampleCN: meadow 加 lark 构成 meadowlark，指草地鹨。

items.example: Meadow plus sweet gives meadowsweet.
items.exampleCN: meadow 加 sweet 构成 meadowsweet，指绣线菊。

items.example: Wildflower names the flowers that grow in a meadow.
items.exampleCN: wildflower 指草地上长出的野花。

items.example: Hay meadow names a field grown for cutting.
items.exampleCN: hay meadow 指专门供割草制干草的田地。

items.example: Latin pratum means much the same as meadow.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 pratum 与 meadow 意思相近，但并非其来源。

definition_zh: 贫乏的；微薄的；瘦的；贫瘠的
definition_en: small in amount or quality, and clearly not enough
core_image: 一只几乎见底的米缸，刮出的米只够下锅一顿
scene: 旱季的河滩上，村民挖出小得可怜的一捧水。Along the dry riverbed, the villagers dug out a meagre handful of water.
sceneCN: 这里 meagre 是「贫乏的、微薄的」（第 1 个义项：数量少得可怜）；句意：沿着干涸的河床，村民挖出小得可怜的一捧水。

pos.zh: 贫乏的；微薄的；质量差的
瘦弱者；瘦小的动物（多见于口语）

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加 -ness 构成，义为「贫乏；微薄」
由形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「微薄地；贫乏地」
美式拼写，与英式拼写意思完全相同

senses.title: Falling short in amount
senses.definition: existing in a small amount that is not enough
senses.definitionCN: 数量很少，不足以满足需要
senses.example: The family lived on a meagre income from selling fish.
senses.exampleCN: 一家人靠卖鱼的微薄收入生活。
senses.why: The oldest recorded senses of French maigre mean thin, so scarcity is bound up with the word from the start.
senses.whyCN: 法语 maigre 最早记录的义项就有「瘦」，所以「稀少」从这个词诞生起就与之相连。

senses.title: Poor in quality
senses.definition: low in quality or variety, so that it fails to satisfy
senses.definitionCN: 质量或种类低劣，无法令人满意
senses.example: The town offers a meagre choice of courses for adults.
senses.exampleCN: 这个小镇为成年人提供的课程选择很少。
senses.why: If food is thin and watery it is also poor, so the idea of being lean extends from quantity to quality.
senses.whyCN: 食物若又稀又水，品质自然也差，所以「瘦」从数量义延伸到质量义。

senses.title: Of a person or animal: lean
senses.definition: having little fat on the body
senses.definitionCN: 身上脂肪很少的
senses.example: The meagre cat slept in the doorway of the shop.
senses.exampleCN: 那只瘦猫睡在店门口。
senses.why: The French source maigre means physically lean, and English kept that fleshly sense alongside the figurative ones.
senses.whyCN: 法语来源 maigre 本义就是身体瘦，英语把这个关于肉的义项与比喻义一并保留下来。

senses.title: Of land or soil: barren
senses.definition: producing few crops because the earth is poor
senses.definitionCN: 土壤肥力差，收成很少
senses.example: Nothing much grows on this meagre soil.
senses.exampleCN: 这种贫瘠的土壤上长不出什么。
senses.why: A lean body produces little, and lean soil produces little too, so the bodily sense passes over to land.
senses.whyCN: 瘦弱的身体产出少，贫瘠的土地产出也少，于是身体义延伸到土地。

senses.title: Of style or writing: thin
senses.definition: lacking detail, warmth, or substance in expression
senses.definitionCN: 表达上缺少细节、温度或实质内容
senses.example: His meagre prose gave no sense of the place.
senses.exampleCN: 他简薄的文笔没能写出那个地方的感觉。
senses.why: Writing that lacks flesh is literally thin, which is why critics call bare prose meagre.
senses.whyCN: 缺乏血肉的文章字面上就是「瘦」，所以批评家称空洞干瘪的文风为 meagre。

senses.title: Of an allowance or ration: scanty
senses.definition: very limited in size, compared with what is expected
senses.definitionCN: 与预期相比非常有限
senses.example: Workers received a meagre ration of bread each day.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们每天领取一份很少的面包配给。
senses.why: Rations are weighed out by hand, and a handful that barely covers the palm is the image behind this use.
senses.whyCN: 配给要用手称量，刚能盖住掌心的一小把，正是这个用法背后的画面。

senses.title: Used of praise or credit: grudging
senses.definition: given or expressed only with reluctance and in small measure
senses.definitionCN: 勉强给出且分量很小
senses.example: The reviewer gave the film meagre praise.
senses.exampleCN: 评论者对这部电影吝于称赞。
senses.why: Praise that is stingy in amount behaves exactly like a lean meal, so the metaphor carries over to words of approval.
senses.whyCN: 分量吝啬的称赞就像一顿清汤寡水的饭，比喻因此延伸到表示赞许的词语上。

senses.title: The noun: a lean animal or person
senses.definition: a person or animal that is very thin
senses.definitionCN: 非常瘦的人或动物
senses.example: In the dialect the cow was called a meagre.
senses.exampleCN: 在方言里，那头母牛被称为一只瘦小的牲口。
senses.why: English once used the word as a noun for a lean creature, a use that survives mostly in dialect and in mackerel names.
senses.whyCN: 英语曾把这个词用作名词指瘦弱的生灵，这一用法如今多见于方言，也保留在鲭鱼的名称里。

intro.en: Meagre goes back through French maigre to Latin macer, meaning thin or lean.
intro.cn: meagre 经法语 maigre 上溯至拉丁语 macer，意为「瘦的、消瘦的」。

items.en: Macer describes a body that is thin or lean.
items.cn: macer 形容身体瘦削。

items.en: Maigre carries the sense of lean into Old French.
items.cn: maigre 把「瘦」的意思带入古法语。

items.en: Legal documents of medieval England weigh maigre in matters of flesh and fish.
items.cn: 中世纪英格兰的法律文书在有关肉类与鱼的条文中掂量 maigre 的分量。

items.en: Magre appears in English for a thin body or scarce provision.
items.cn: 英语中的 magre 指消瘦的身体或短缺的供给。

items.en: The modern spelling meagre settles down.
items.cn: 现代拼写 meagre 逐渐固定。

items.en: Abstract uses spread to income, evidence, and praise, while American spelling prefers meager.
items.cn: 抽象用法扩展到收入、证据与称赞，而美式拼写更常用 meager。

note.en: Meagre is the French route to Latin macer, so it sits beside other words for thinness, and beside ordinary words for shortage.
note.cn: meagre 是经法语到达拉丁语 macer 的一条路径，所以它与表示「瘦」的其他词相邻，也与表示短缺的常用词相邻。

entries.definition: the American spelling of the same word
entries.definitionCN: 与 meagre 同词，只是美式拼写，意思完全相同

entries.definition: a Latin adjective meaning thin or lean
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语形容词，意为「瘦的」，是 meagre 的源头

entries.definition: extremely thin, a rare word from the same Latin family
entries.definitionCN: 极度消瘦的，是同一拉丁词族的罕用词

entries.definition: barely enough, often of clothing or supply
entries.definitionCN: 勉强够的；匮乏的，常用于衣物或供给

entries.definition: thinly spread out over an area
too small in size or amount

normalIntro.en: Meagre is the word for what is thin, scarce, and never quite enough.
normalIntro.cn: meagre 专门形容又瘦又少、总也不够用的事物。

normal.en: A meagre income buys only the plainest food.
normal.cn: 微薄的收入只买得起最朴素的食物。

normal.en: Meagre resources force the team to plan carefully.
normal.cn: 贫乏的资源迫使团队小心规划。

normal.en: A meagre diet leaves children weak.
normal.cn: 粗劣的饮食让孩子们体弱。

normal.en: Compare the American spelling meager: same word, one letter fewer.
normal.cn: 对比美式拼写 meager：同一个词，少一个字母。

normal.en: Remember that meagre and meager both hang on the Latin root macer, thin.
normal.cn: 记住 meagre 与 meager 都附着在拉丁词根 macer（瘦）上。

abstract.en: Picture a bowl scraped until only a few grains remain.
abstract.cn: 想象一只被刮干净的碗，只剩几粒米。

abstract.en: Imagine a thin soup with nothing but water in it.
abstract.cn: 想象一碗清得只有水的稀汤。

abstract.en: See a stray cat with ribs showing at every step.
abstract.cn: 想象一只流浪猫每走一步都露出肋骨。

examples.en: The charity survives on a meagre budget.
examples.cn: 这家慈善机构靠微薄的预算维持。

examples.en: Wildlife is sparse in this meagre soil.
examples.cn: 在这片贫瘠的土壤上，野生动物稀少。

examples.en: The manager offered only meagre praise for her work.
examples.cn: 经理对她的工作只是吝啬地称赞了几句。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米哥儿」——穷人家的哥哥把米刮得只剩一点儿，日子过得微薄；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 macer（瘦的；消瘦的）→ 古法语 maigre → 英语 meagre，核心义「瘦而少」，由身体的瘦引申为数量与质量的贫乏。

sensesIntro.en: Meagre starts with the body of a lean creature and grows outward to soil, writing, rations, and finally to grudging praise.
sensesIntro.cn: meagre 从瘦弱生灵的身体出发，向外长到土地、文笔、配给，最后到吝啬的称赞。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a nearly empty rice bowl that yields one thin meal.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只几乎见底的米缸。

branches.en: Too small in amount is the everyday sense that grew from leanness.
branches.cn: 数量太少是日常义项，由瘦引申而来。

branches.en: Poor quality follows once the amount cannot satisfy anyone.
branches.cn: 一旦数量无法满足需要，质量义随之而来。

branches.en: The bodily sense of a lean person or animal is the oldest physical layer, and the dialect noun keeps it.
branches.cn: 人和动物的瘦是较古老的身体义层，方言名词保留了它。

branches.en: Barren ground stretches the bodily sense outward to landscape.
branches.cn: 贫瘠的土地把身体义延伸到自然景观。

branches.en: Thin prose, scanty rations, and grudging praise are all ways of measuring what is doled out.
branches.cn: 简薄的文风、少量的配给与吝啬的称赞，都是对「分给多少」的度量。

intro.en: Meagre is a borrowed adjective with a Latin root macer, and the family is built out with -ness, -ly, and the American spelling meager.
intro.cn: meagre 是借入的形容词，词根为拉丁语 macer，同族词由 -ness、-ly 与美式拼写 meager 扩展而成。

latinIntro.en: Latin macer means thin or lean, and its comparative macrior and the rare macilentus all circle the same image.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 macer 意为瘦的，比较级 macrior 与罕用的 macilentus 都围绕同一意象。

items.example: Macer is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: macer 是整个词族的词根。

items.meaning: thin, slim; also of days without meat
items.meaningCN: 瘦的；也指不食肉的斋日
items.example: Maigre is the direct French source.
items.exampleCN: maigre 是直接的法语来源。

items.example: Meagre keeps the figurative sense.
items.exampleCN: meagre 保留了比喻义。

items.meaning: the same adjective under American conventions
items.meaningCN: 美式拼写，同一个形容词
items.example: American texts write meager.
items.exampleCN: 美式文本写作 meager。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms meagreness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 meagreness。

items.meaning: the state of being scarce or poor
items.example: Meagreness names the shortage itself.
items.exampleCN: meagreness 指短缺本身。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms meagrely.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 meagrely。

items.example: Meagrely describes how little is given.
items.exampleCN: meagrely 描述给出的分量之少。

items.example: Macilent is a rare cousin from the same root.
items.exampleCN: macilent 是同一词根的罕用近亲。

items.example: Emaciate points back to Latin macer.
items.exampleCN: emaciate 指回拉丁语 macer。

definition_zh: 蜿蜒；迂回地走；漫谈；曲折的河道
definition_en: to follow a slow and twisting path, or to wander without a fixed direction
core_image: 一条河在平原上绕出一个个大弯，像被拉长的省略号
scene: 下午的街道上，游客们不着急，在巷子里慢慢转来转去。Without a map, the visitors meander through the narrow streets of the old town.
sceneCN: 这里 meander 是「迂回地走、闲逛」（第 2 个义项：不沿直线行走）；句意：没有地图，游客们在老城的窄巷里蜿蜒前行。

pos.zh: 蜿蜒而流；迂回行进；漫步；漫谈
使蜿蜒；沿曲折路线穿越
蜿蜒的弯曲；曲折的河道

derivatives.zh: 由现在分词形容词化，义为「蜿蜒的；迂回的」
由拉丁词干加 -ous 构成，义为「曲折的」，多见于文学与地理文字
由动词加 -er 构成，指漫步者、闲逛的人

senses.title: Of a river: to wind in broad curves
senses.definition: to flow in a series of wide bends across a plain
senses.definitionCN: 在平原上流出一连串宽阔的弯道
senses.example: The river meanders across the valley floor.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河在谷底蜿蜒流过。
senses.why: The word began as the name of a specific twisting river in Asia Minor, so bending water is its oldest meaning.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是小亚细亚一条弯曲河流的名字，所以「弯曲的水」是它最古老的含义。

senses.title: To walk without a straight course
senses.definition: to move about slowly and by a winding route, without hurrying
senses.definitionCN: 缓慢地沿曲折路线移动，不慌不忙
senses.example: We meandered through the market for an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在市场里逛了一个小时。
senses.why: A person who walks like a river does not choose the shortest way, so the water image transfers to the legs.
senses.whyCN: 像河流那样走路的人不走最短的路，于是水的意象转移到双腿上。

senses.title: The noun: a bend in a river
senses.definition: a single wide curve in a river or road
senses.definitionCN: 河流或道路上一处宽阔的弯道
senses.example: The old mill stood at a meander of the stream.
senses.exampleCN: 老磨坊坐落在小溪的一个河曲边。
senses.why: Geographers named the loop itself after the winding river, giving English a countable noun.
senses.whyCN: 地理学家以这条弯曲的河来命名弯道本身，英语由此得到一个可数名词。

senses.title: Of abstract things: to wander without aim
senses.definition: to move from topic to topic without a clear direction
senses.definitionCN: 从一个话题漫无目的地转到另一个话题
senses.example: His talk meandered from cricket to cooking.
senses.exampleCN: 他讲了从板球到烹饪的各种话题，漫无边际。
senses.why: Conversation that does not go straight is like water that cannot, so the image stretches to speech and thought.
senses.whyCN: 不走直线的谈话就像无法直行的水，意象因此延伸到言语与思绪。

senses.title: To follow a winding route through a place
senses.definition: to go along a route that curves back and forth across an area
senses.definitionCN: 沿着来回弯曲的路线穿越一个区域
senses.example: A path meanders across the marsh to the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 一条小路在沼泽上蜿蜒通向海边。
senses.why: Here the verb keeps the full picture of the river, naming the whole curved course rather than a single step.
senses.whyCN: 这里动词保留了河流的完整画面，指整条弯曲的路线，而不只是一步。

senses.title: Of a line or shape: to wind
senses.definition: to consist of curves that twist in and out
senses.definitionCN: 由来回扭动的曲线构成
senses.example: Golden lines meander across the edge of the plate.
senses.exampleCN: 金色的线条在盘子边缘蜿蜒。
senses.why: Artists borrowed the river word for ornament because the greek key pattern curls exactly like a bend of water.
senses.whyCN: 艺术家借用这条河的名字来表示装饰纹样，因为回纹的卷曲正像一段弯曲的水流。

senses.title: The verb for roads: to twist and turn
senses.definition: to change direction many times while advancing
senses.definitionCN: 在前进过程中多次改变方向
senses.example: The road meanders up the hillside for miles.
senses.exampleCN: 这条路沿着山坡蜿蜒数英里。
senses.why: Roads on a slope can only climb in zigzags, so the winding river becomes the model for every twist and turn of travel.
senses.whyCN: 斜坡上的路只能以之字形攀升，于是弯曲的河流成了所有曲折行程的范本。

intro.en: Meander comes from Latin Maeander, the Greek name of a river in Asia Minor famous for its winding course.
intro.cn: meander 来自拉丁语 Maeander，即小亚细亚一条以弯曲著称的河流的希腊语名称。

items.en: Maiandros is the name of a winding river in what is now Turkey.
items.cn: Maiandros 是今土耳其境内一条弯曲河流的名称。

items.en: Maeander names the same river and also a winding pattern.
items.cn: Maeander 既指这条河，也指一种蜿蜒的纹样。

items.en: English adopts the river name and uses it for anything that winds.
items.cn: 英语借入这条河的名字，用它指任何蜿蜒的事物。

items.en: Meander becomes a verb for streams and for people walking.
items.cn: meander 成为动词，用于溪流，也用于走路的人。

items.en: Geographers adopt meander as a technical term, and speakers apply it to speech and thought.
items.cn: 地理学家把 meander 用作术语，说话者也把它用于言语与思绪。

note.en: Meander belongs to the family of winding words, and it is also close to plain words for walking slowly.
note.cn: meander 属于表示「弯曲」的词群，也与表示慢慢行走的常用词相邻。

entries.definition: winding or aimless, used as an adjective
entries.definitionCN: 蜿蜒的；漫无目的的，作形容词用

entries.definition: full of curves and windings
entries.definitionCN: 曲折蜿蜒的，与 meander 同源

entries.definition: the river name that gave English the word
entries.definitionCN: 给英语这个词的河名，比 meander 更古老

entries.definition: to move about without a fixed course, often without a goal
entries.definitionCN: 漫游；游荡，强调没有目标

entries.definition: to follow a curving course
entries.definitionCN: 蜿蜒；缠绕，强调路线弯曲

entries.definition: to walk slowly and in a relaxed way
entries.definitionCN: 悠闲地散步，强调从容而不强调路线

normalIntro.en: Meander is a river name that became a verb for anything that refuses to go straight.
normalIntro.cn: meander 是一个河名，后来变成动词，指任何不肯走直的事物。

normal.en: The stream meanders through the meadow before it joins the river.
normal.cn: 小溪蜿蜒穿过草地，然后汇入大河。

normal.en: Meander through a town means walking without a route.
normal.cn: meander through 一座城，就是没有路线地闲逛。

normal.en: The meandering of a discussion means it keeps turning aside.
normal.cn: 讨论的 meandering 指它不断岔开。

normal.en: Compare wander: wander cares about having no goal, meander about the curving path.
normal.cn: 对比 wander：wander 关注没有目标，meander 关注路线弯曲。

normal.en: In geography this is a technical term: a meander is a single loop of a slow river.
normal.cn: 在地理学中它是术语：meander 指慢河里一个独立的弯道。

abstract.en: Draw an S on paper and follow it with a finger.
abstract.cn: 在纸上画一个弯曲的 S，用手指沿着它走一遍。

abstract.en: Picture water with all the time in the world taking the long way round.
abstract.cn: 想象时间无比充裕的水，偏要绕远路走。

abstract.en: Think of a road that knows the destination but forgets the direction.
abstract.cn: 想象一条知道终点却忘了方向的路。

examples.en: The small river meanders for miles before reaching the lake.
examples.cn: 这条小河蜿蜒数英里后才抵达湖泊。

examples.en: We meandered along the harbour wall at sunset.
examples.cn: 日落时我们沿着海港的堤岸慢慢漫步。

examples.en: Her story meandered, but everyone stayed to listen.
examples.cn: 她的故事讲得漫无边际，但大家都留下来听。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「漫的」——走路漫无方向、弯来绕去就是漫的；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 Maiandros（小亚细亚一条弯曲的河）→ 拉丁语 Maeander → 英语 meander，核心义「像那条河一样弯」。

sensesIntro.en: Meander begins with the bend of a river, moves to the legs of a walker, then to the loop itself, and finally to words and lines that will not stay straight.
sensesIntro.cn: meander 从河水的弯曲出发，转到行人的双腿，再到弯道本身，最后到不肯走直的话语与线条。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a river drawing wide loops across a flat plain.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条河在平原上绕出一个又一个大弯。

branches.en: A river or path that winds across land is the original picture.
branches.cn: 横过大地蜿蜒的河流或小路是最初的画面。

branches.en: Walking without the shortest route is the river image moved onto feet.
branches.cn: 不走最短路线地走路，是河流意象挪到了脚上。

branches.en: The countable noun names one loop of the winding course.
branches.cn: 可数名词指蜿蜒河道中的一个弯。

branches.en: Speech that keeps turning comes from the same failure to go straight.
branches.cn: 不断拐弯的谈话来自同样的「不肯走直」。

branches.en: Lines in art and roads in geography both borrow the river shape.
branches.cn: 艺术中的线条与地理中的道路都借用了河流的形状。

intro.en: Meander is a whole borrowed name rather than a built word, but English grows a family around it with -ing, -er, and -ous.
intro.cn: meander 是整体借入的名字，不是拼装出的词，但英语用 -ing、-er、-ous 围绕它长出一个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin Maeander is a Greek place name carried over, and it gave the adjective meandrous through the Latin stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 Maeander 是由希腊语传下来的地名，并经由拉丁词干产生了形容词 meandrous。

items.meaning: a winding river of Asia Minor
items.meaningCN: 小亚细亚的一条弯曲河流
items.example: Maiandros is the starting point.
items.exampleCN: Maiandros 是整个词的起点。

items.meaning: the same river, and a winding ornament
items.meaningCN: 同一条河，也指一种蜿蜒纹样
items.example: Maeander passes the name into Latin.
items.exampleCN: Maeander 把名字传入拉丁语。

items.example: Meander becomes a common word.
items.exampleCN: meander 成为常用词。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词与形容词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ing forms meandering.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 meandering。

items.example: Meandering describes a river or a speech.
items.exampleCN: meandering 形容河流或讲话。

items.example: The suffix -er forms meanderer.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 meanderer。

items.example: The suffix -ous forms meandrous.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ous 构成 meandrous。

items.example: Meandrous is a literary adjective.
items.exampleCN: meandrous 是文学色彩较浓的形容词。

items.example: Anfractuous covers the same winding idea.
items.exampleCN: anfractuous 覆盖同样的弯曲概念。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 小亚细亚的一条弯曲河流

definition_zh: 有意义的；意味深长的；有重要价值的
definition_en: having real meaning, importance, or a clear point
core_image: 一张纸上写满别人看不懂的符号，直到有人把每个字都读懂
scene: 老义工在社区中心待了很久，觉得这件事让她的人生有了分量。For the retired volunteer, teaching children to read is a meaningful experience.
sceneCN: 这里 meaningful 是「有重要价值的」（第 1 个义项：具有真实的分量与意义）；句意：对这位退休志愿者来说，教孩子读书是一段有意义的经历。

pos.zh: 有意义的；意味深长的；重要的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「有意义地；意味深长地」
由形容词加 -ness 构成，义为「有意义；具有意义的状态」
meaningful 的基础名词，义为「意思；意义」
由 -less 构成，与 meaningful 相反，义为「无意义的」

senses.title: Having real value or importance
senses.titleCN: 有重要价值的；有意义的
senses.definition: serious, important, and worth doing or caring about
senses.definitionCN: 严肃、重要、值得去做或在意的
senses.example: Volunteering gave him a meaningful role in the town.
senses.exampleCN: 做志愿者让他在小镇里有了一个重要的角色。
senses.why: Meaning here is weight, so calling something meaningful says it carries real consequence in a life.
senses.whyCN: 这里的意义指分量，说某事 meaningful 就是说它对人生有真实的影响。

senses.title: Full of a message that is understood
senses.definition: carrying a message that is felt clearly, often through small signs
senses.definitionCN: 通过细微的信号清晰传达信息
senses.example: She gave her son a meaningful look across the table.
senses.exampleCN: 她在桌子对面意味深长地看了儿子一眼。
senses.why: The base noun meaning is what a sign carries, and meaningful describes a sign that carries plenty of it.
senses.whyCN: 基础名词 meaning 是符号承载的东西，meaningful 形容承载得很多的符号。

senses.title: Clear and understandable
senses.definition: presented so that the sense can be grasped, not just received
senses.definitionCN: 呈现得能让人抓住其含义，而不只是接收
senses.example: The survey must produce meaningful results for the council.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查必须为议会提供有意义的结果。
senses.why: In research a number that nobody can interpret is useless, so meaningful means the figures actually say something.
senses.whyCN: 在研究中，没人能解读的数字毫无用处，所以 meaningful 指数据真的说明了问题。

senses.title: Following from cause and effect
senses.titleCN: 有意义的（因果关系上可检验）
senses.definition: showing a real relationship rather than chance, in statistics or science
senses.definitionCN: 在统计或科学中显示真实关系而非偶然
senses.example: The two groups differed in a meaningful way.
senses.exampleCN: 两组之间存在具有意义的差异。
senses.why: Proof needs differences that mean something, so a measurable, real effect becomes the meaningful one.
senses.whyCN: 论证需要有意涵的差异，于是可测量、真实的效应被称作 meaningful。

senses.title: Having a purpose
senses.definition: done for a deliberate purpose rather than by accident
senses.definitionCN: 为了明确目的而做，而非偶然
senses.example: The talks led to meaningful progress on the treaty.
senses.exampleCN: 会谈在条约问题上带来了有实质意义的进展。
senses.why: Change that means something is change that was aimed at, so the word slides from meaning to purpose.
senses.whyCN: 真正的改变是有意争取来的，于是这个词从「有意义」滑向「有目的」。

senses.title: Emotionally significant
senses.definition: carrying personal significance for the feelings
senses.definitionCN: 对个人情感具有特殊重要性
senses.example: Their wedding song is deeply meaningful to them.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的婚礼歌曲对他们来说意义深远。
senses.why: Personal memory loads an object with meaning, so the word comes to describe moments that matter to the heart.
senses.whyCN: 个人记忆给物件加载意义，于是这个词也形容对人心重要的时刻。

senses.title: Of a look or silence: loaded with intent
senses.definition: expressing a reaction or intention without words
senses.definitionCN: 不用言语而表达某种反应或意图
senses.example: A meaningful silence followed his remark.
senses.exampleCN: 他的话之后是一阵意味深长的沉默。
senses.why: Even a pause can carry a message, so meaningful extends from words to the small gestures around them.
senses.whyCN: 连停顿也能传递信息，于是 meaningful 从言语延伸到言语周围的小动作。

intro.en: Meaningful is an English construction, made from the noun meaning plus the full form of the suffix -ful.
intro.cn: meaningful 是英语自身构造的词，由名词 meaning 加上后缀 -ful 的完整形式构成。

items.en: Munan means to think of or intend, and gives the verb mean.
items.cn: 古英语 munan 意为想到、打算，由此产生动词 mean。

items.en: Meanning names the sense or intention a word or act carries.
items.cn: 中古英语 meanning 指词语或行为所带的意思或意图。

items.en: The suffix -ful, from a word for full, attaches to nouns.
items.cn: 后缀 -ful 源自意为「满」的形容词，附着在名词上。

items.en: Meaningful is recorded in the sense of full of sense or consequence.
items.cn: meaningful 被记录，义为「充满含义或后果的」。

items.en: Psychology and statistics adopt the word for effects that matter, including significant results.
items.cn: 心理学与统计学把这个词用于重要的效应，包括显著的结果。

items.en: It becomes a mild and polite way to praise work, love, or a long conversation.
items.cn: 它成为温和而礼貌地称赞工作、爱或谈话的说法。

note.en: Meaningful is one of the words built on meaning, so the look-alike group is a family of English derivations, and the near-meaning group gathers words for what matters.
note.cn: meaningful 是由 meaning 构成的一批词之一，所以形近组是一族英语派生词，近义组则汇集表示「重要」的词。

entries.definition: the idea that something expresses
entries.definitionCN: 某事物所表达的意思，是 meaningful 的基础名词

entries.definition: in a way that carries meaning
the quality of having meaning
entries.definitionCN: 有意义；具有意义的性质

entries.definition: having no meaning or purpose
entries.definitionCN: 无意义的，与 meaningful 后缀相反

entries.definition: important enough to be noticed or counted
entries.definitionCN: 重要的；显著的，比 meaningful 更正式

entries.definition: done for a deliberate aim
expressing much with few words
entries.definitionCN: 意味深长的；有说服力的

normalIntro.en: Meaningful simply says that something carries meaning, so pull it apart into meaning plus full.
normalIntro.cn: meaningful 只是说某事物充满了含义，把它拆成 meaning 与 full 就懂了。

normal.en: Meaning plus full equals loaded with meaning.
normal.cn: meaning 加 full，就是充满了含义。

normal.en: A meaningful job is one whose point you can see.
normal.cn: 有意义的工作，就是你能看见其意义的工作。

normal.en: A meaningful look says as much as a sentence.
normal.cn: 意味深长的一瞥，等于说了一句话。

normal.en: Swap the suffix: meaningless is the opposite, meaningfully is the adverb.
normal.cn: 换个词尾：meaningless 相反，meaningfully 是副词。

normal.en: In research writing, meaningful results are results that are not just noise.
normal.cn: 在学术写作中，meaningful results 指不是噪声的数据结果。

abstract.en: See a key that opens a door everybody thought was a wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙打开了一扇被所有人当成墙的门。

abstract.en: Imagine a letter written in a language you finally learn to read.
abstract.cn: 想象一封用一种语言写的信，你终于学会了读它。

abstract.en: Picture a nearly blank page that still carries one clear line.
abstract.cn: 想象一页几乎空白的纸，却仍写着一行清晰的字。

examples.en: She left her job to find more meaningful work.
examples.cn: 她辞去工作，去寻找更有意义的工作。

examples.en: His meaningful smile said more than any speech.
examples.cn: 他意味深长的微笑胜过任何演讲。

examples.en: The new data made the debate more meaningful.
examples.cn: 新数据让这场辩论更有意义。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「命您服」——一件事有价值，才值得你花上性命去服；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 munan（想着、打算）→ mean（意思是）→ 名词 meaning（意义）+ 后缀 -ful（充满）→ meaningful，核心义「充满意义」。

sensesIntro.en: Meaningful starts from carrying a message that can be read, then spreads to value, purpose, and effects that actually matter.
sensesIntro.cn: meaningful 从「承载可读出的信息」出发，再扩展到价值、目的与真正起作用的效应。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a page of symbols that suddenly makes sense.
core.cn: 核心意象：一页忽然读得懂的符号。

branches.en: Worth doing is the everyday sense of the word.
branches.cn: 值得做是这个词的日常义项。

branches.en: A sign that carries a clear message is the most literal modern sense.
branches.cn: 承载清晰信息的信号是最字面的现代义项。

branches.en: Clear and understandable is meaning in the plainest sense.
branches.cn: 清晰可懂是最朴素意义上的意义。

branches.en: Real effects and deliberate aims show meaning turning into purpose.
branches.cn: 真实的效应与有意的目标显示意义转化为目的。

branches.en: Personal memory and wordless signals load ordinary things with meaning.
branches.cn: 个人记忆与无言信号为寻常事物加载意义。

intro.en: Meaningful is built inside English, from mean and meaning plus the suffix -ful, with -less, -ly, and -ness as siblings.
intro.cn: meaningful 是在英语内部构造的，由 mean、meaning 加上后缀 -ful 构成，-less、-ly、-ness 是同门词尾。

latinIntro.en: This word owes nothing to Latin. Its root is native English munan, to think of or intend.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词与拉丁语无关，其词根是本土英语的 munan，意为想到、打算。

items.example: Munan is the native ancestor of mean.
items.exampleCN: munan 是 mean 的本土祖先。

items.example: Mean supplies the verbal core.
items.exampleCN: mean 提供动词核心。

items.example: Meaning is the noun the adjective grows from.
items.exampleCN: meaning 是这个形容词所由生长的名词。

items.example: The suffix -ful forms meaningful.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ful 构成 meaningful。

items.example: The suffix -less forms meaningless.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -less 构成 meaningless。

items.example: Meaningless is the direct opposite.
items.exampleCN: meaningless 是直接的反义词。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms meaningfully.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 meaningfully。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms meaningfulness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 meaningfulness。

items.example: Signify carries a Latin sign root instead.
items.exampleCN: signify 则带有拉丁语「符号」词根。

items.example: Significant is the Latin route to the same idea.
items.exampleCN: significant 是通往同一概念的拉丁路径。

definition_zh: 力学；机械学；机械结构；运作方式；运转细节；技巧；机械部分
definition_en: the branch of science that studies the behaviour of moving bodies and forces, or the way a machine, system, or process actually works inside
core_image: 一张拆开的机械表：齿轮、发条与杠杆一一咬合，各司其职
scene: 修表匠把怀表放在放大镜下，逐层拆出齿轮，向学徒解释每一道咬合的道理。The apprentice asked how the tiny gears worked, and the old watchmaker said, patience is half of mechanics.
sceneCN: 这里 mechanics 是「力学；机械学」（第 1 个义项：研究运动与力的学科）；句意为学徒问那些微小齿轮为何能运转，老修表匠说耐心是力学的一半。图中可辨识物件：怀表、齿轮、镊子、放大镜。

pos.zh: 机械结构；机械部分（作复数用）
运作方式；运作机制（作复数用）

collocations.zh: 汽车机械结构；汽车机械原理

forms.label: 单复数同形（作学科时常视为单数）

derivatives.zh: 由 mechane 加名词后缀构成，义为「机修工；机械师」
由 mechanics 加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「机械的；呆板的」
与 mechanics 同出一源，义为「机械装置；机制」
由 mechanism 加动词后缀 -ize 构成，义为「使机械化」
复合词，义为「机械工程师」

senses.title: The science of motion and forces
senses.definition: the branch of physics that studies how bodies move and how forces act on them
senses.definitionCN: 研究物体如何运动、力如何作用于物体的物理学分支
senses.example: Newton laid the foundations of classical mechanics.
senses.exampleCN: 牛顿奠定了经典力学的基础。
senses.why: The Greek root mekhane means a machine or a contrivance, so the study of how machines move became the name of a science.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根 mekhane 意为「机械、巧器」，研究机械如何运动的知识最终成为一门学科的名字。

senses.title: The working parts of a machine
senses.definition: the moving parts of a machine and the way they are arranged to work together
senses.definitionCN: 机器中会动的部件以及它们互相配合的构造方式
senses.example: The mechanics of the clock were surprisingly simple.
senses.exampleCN: 这座钟的机械结构出奇地简单。
senses.why: Because the science grew out of watching machines, the plural form could name the machine parts themselves.
senses.whyCN: 这门学问本就源于观察机械，所以复数形式也用来直接指机器上那些零件与结构。

senses.title: The way something works inside
senses.definition: the way that a system, process, or organization works internally
senses.definitionCN: 某个系统、过程或组织内部运转的方式
senses.example: Few voters understand the mechanics of tax reform.
senses.exampleCN: 很少有选民真正了解税制改革的运作方式。
senses.why: The machine became a metaphor, so any system can be described by the gears of its mechanics.
senses.whyCN: 机器变成了比喻，于是任何系统都可以用它的齿轮运作来描述。

senses.title: Practical mechanical skill
senses.titleCN: 机械修造技能；机械原理
senses.definition: the practical knowledge or skill needed to build or repair machines
senses.definitionCN: 建造或修理机器所需的实际知识或技能
senses.example: He learned the mechanics of car repair in his fathers workshop.
senses.exampleCN: 他在父亲的工场里学会了汽车修理的机械原理。
senses.why: The abstract science narrowed into hands-on craft knowledge among engineers and repairers.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的学科在工程师与修理工手中收窄为动手操作的技艺知识。

senses.title: Technique in doing something
senses.definition: the basic techniques and working methods used in an activity such as writing or sport
senses.definitionCN: 写作、体育等活动中使用的基本技法与操作方法
senses.example: Good mechanics matter more than style in a fast serve.
senses.exampleCN: 在高速发球中，扎实的技巧比风格更重要。
senses.why: From the workings of a machine came the idea of the correct workings of a skill.
senses.whyCN: 由机器的运转方式引申出技能应有正确的运作方式这层意思。

senses.title: Mechanical parts as a plural noun
senses.definition: the mechanical parts of a vehicle or device considered together
senses.definitionCN: 把车辆或装置的机械部件作为整体来看
senses.example: The mechanics of the aircraft were checked before every flight.
senses.exampleCN: 每次飞行前都会检查飞机的机械部件。
senses.why: A collective plural names all the moving components of one device at once.
senses.whyCN: 集合复数把同一装置上所有会动的组件一次性统指。

senses.title: The small but decisive inner rules
senses.definition: the small inner rules that decide whether a system or game works well
senses.definitionCN: 决定一个系统或游戏能否顺利运转的细小内在规则
senses.example: Once you learn the mechanics of the app, it saves hours.
senses.exampleCN: 一旦摸清这个应用的运作诀窍，它能省下好几个小时。
senses.why: Modern technical use reduces the whole subject to the hidden rules that make something run.
senses.whyCN: 现代技术用法把整门学问缩小为让事物跑起来的那套隐藏规则。

senses.title: The human labor force of machines
senses.titleCN: 机械师队伍；机械类岗位
senses.definition: the people who operate and maintain machines, viewed as a group
senses.definitionCN: 操作与维护机器的人员作为整体来看
senses.example: The pit mechanics worked all night on the damaged car.
senses.exampleCN: 维修区里的机械师们整夜都在修那辆受损的车。
senses.why: People who live by machines can be named by the machines they serve.
senses.whyCN: 靠机器为生的人，可以直接用他们所照管的机器来称呼。

intro.en: Mechanics goes back through Latin to the Greek word for a machine, and the science was first named for the workings of machines.
intro.cn: mechanics 经拉丁语追溯到希腊语中表示「机械」的词；这门学科最初就是按机械的运转来命名的。

items.en: Mekhane meant a machine, a contrivance, or a device for lifting.
items.cn: mekhane 意为机械、巧器，或用于起重吊运的装置。

items.en: The adjective mekhanikos described what is done by a machine.
items.cn: 形容词 mekhanikos 描述由机械完成的事物。

items.en: Latin mechanicus and mechanica carried the idea of things done by art and engine.
items.cn: 拉丁语 mechanicus 与 mechanica 承接了「借技艺与器械完成」的观念。

items.en: Mechanics first named the mechanical arts and the skill of building engines.
items.cn: 英语 mechanics 最早指机械技艺与建造器械的技能。

items.en: With Galileo and Newton the word became the science of motion and force.
items.cn: 到伽利略与牛顿时代，这个词成为研究运动与力的学科。

items.en: Today mechanics also names the inner workings of systems, games, and software.
items.cn: 现代英语中 mechanics 也指系统、游戏与软件的内部运作方式。

note.en: Mechanics is the science and the workings; its family reaches outward to mechanic, mechanism, and mechanical.
note.cn: mechanics 既是学科，也指运作方式；它的词族向外延伸到 mechanic、mechanism 与 mechanical。

relating to machines

to replace human work with machines

entries.definition: the branch of mechanics that studies forces and motion
entries.definitionCN: 动力学（研究力与运动的分支）

entries.definition: the science of matter, energy, and motion
the way something operates inside

normalIntro.en: Mechanics is the name of a science, but it is built on the plain noun mechanic plus the plural ending -s that old science names share.
normalIntro.cn: mechanics 是一门学科的名称，由普通名词 mechanic 加学科常用的复数结尾 -s 构成。

normal.en: Kinematics studies motion, while dynamics studies force; both sit under mechanics.
normal.cn: 运动学研究运动，动力学研究力，两者都归于力学之下。

normal.en: The suffix -ics names a field of study, just as in physics and ethics.
normal.cn: 结尾 -ics 表示一门学科，和 physics、ethics 同理。

normal.en: Mechanic is the person, mechanical is the adjective, mechanics is the science.
normal.cn: mechanic 是人，mechanical 是形容词，mechanics 是学科。

normal.en: The mechanics of something are the hidden gears, not the visible surface.
normal.cn: the mechanics of 某物指的是隐藏的齿轮，而不是表面。

normal.en: Quantum mechanics is particle science; classical mechanics covers cars and swings.
normal.cn: quantum mechanics 是研究粒子的学问；classical mechanics 覆盖汽车与秋千。

abstract.en: Picture a watch opened up, all gears laid out in order.
abstract.cn: 想象一只被拆开的手表，齿轮按顺序摆开。

abstract.en: Imagine the first machine ever built, a rope lifting a stone.
abstract.cn: 想象人类最早的机械，用绳索吊起石头。

abstract.en: See a board game lifted up, revealing the rules printed underneath.
abstract.cn: 想象掀开一块棋盘，露出印在底下的规则。

examples.en: Students of classical mechanics study how forces change motion.
examples.cn: 学习经典力学的学生研究力如何改变运动。

examples.en: Before blaming the players, study the mechanics of the game.
examples.cn: 在责怪球员之前，先研究这项运动的规则和运作方式。

examples.en: The mechanic explained the mechanics of the engine in simple words.
examples.cn: 机修工用简单的说法解释引擎的机械原理。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「没卡你死」——机械齿轮卡死了，就得拆开研究它的力学；这不是真实词源，只是把 mecha 与机械运转连起来记。

root: 希腊语 mekhane（机械、巧器）→ mekhanikos（机械的）→ 拉丁语 mechanicus 与 mechanica（机械之术）→ 英语 mechanic 与 mechanics，核心义「机器如何动起来」。

sensesIntro.en: From the science of machines, mechanics widens to the parts of a machine, then to the way any system works, and finally to the small rules behind everyday activities.
sensesIntro.cn: mechanics 从研究机器的学问出发，扩展到机器的部件，再扩展到任何系统的运作方式，最后落脚到日常活动背后的细小规则。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an opened watch with gears laid out in order.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只被拆开、齿轮按序摆开的手表。

branches.en: The plainest branch is the science itself, named after machines.
branches.cn: 最直接的分支就是这门以机器命名的学科。

branches.en: The parts branch names the gears rather than the study.
branches.cn: 部件分支指向齿轮本身，而不是研究它的学问。

branches.en: The workings branch turns every system into a machine.
branches.cn: 运作分支把任何系统都看成一台机器。

branches.en: The technique branch treats a skill as a well-oiled mechanism.
branches.cn: 技巧分支把一项技能看作上过油的装置。

branches.en: The human branch names the craftsmen and crews who serve machines.
branches.cn: 人的分支指伺弄机器的工匠与维修人员。

intro.en: Mechanics is a Greek machine word dressed in a Latin plural; English builds mechanic, mechanism, and mechanical around the same stem.
intro.cn: mechanics 是一个披着拉丁语复数外衣的希腊语机械词；英语围绕同一词干构成 mechanic、mechanism 与 mechanical。

latinIntro.en: Latin mechanicus and mechanica keep the Greek sense of a machine and of the arts done by engines.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mechanicus 与 mechanica 保留了希腊语中机械以及借器械完成的技艺之义。

items.example: The root mekhane gives the machine image.
items.exampleCN: 词根 mekhane 提供机械意象。

items.example: Mechanics names the science as a whole.
items.exampleCN: mechanics 整体指这门学科。

items.example: The suffix -ics forms science names such as physics.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ics 构成 physics 之类的学科名。

items.example: Mechanic is the person one letter away from the science.
items.exampleCN: mechanic 是比学科名少一个字母的人。

items.example: The suffix -ical forms mechanical.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ical 构成 mechanical。

items.example: The suffix -ism forms mechanism.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ism 构成 mechanism。

items.example: The suffix -ize forms mechanize.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ize 构成 mechanize。

items.example: Mechanism names one internal device.
items.exampleCN: mechanism 指一个内部装置。

items.example: Mechanical describes what machines do.
items.exampleCN: mechanical 描述机械所为。

items.example: Mechanize is the verb of the family.
items.exampleCN: mechanize 是这个词族的动词。

definition_zh: 调解人；仲裁者；中间人；居间媒介；中间物；介质
definition_en: a person who tries to help two sides reach an agreement, or something that stands between two things and serves as a link
core_image: 一个人站两排对峙的人中间，两手各接过一支伸来的手
scene: 两户人家为地界争吵，族里的长辈被请来坐在中间，听双方把话说完。The neighbours finally shook hands after an experienced mediator listened to both families.
sceneCN: 这里 mediator 是「调解人」（第 1 个义项：帮助双方达成协议的中间人）；句意为一位有经验的调解人听完两家的话后，邻居们终于握手。图中可辨识物件：木桌、对峙的两户人家、中间的长者。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 mediare 构成，义为「调解；居间调停」
由 mediate 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「调解；调停」
由 mediator 加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「调解的」
同出拉丁语 medius，前缀 in- 否定中间，义为「立即的；直接的」
同出拉丁语 medius，义为「媒介；中间物；介质」

senses.title: A person who helps two sides agree
senses.definition: a person who talks with two opposing sides and helps them reach an agreement
senses.definitionCN: 与对立双方沟通、帮助他们达成协议的人
senses.example: A union mediator ended the three-week strike.
senses.exampleCN: 一位工会调解人终结了这场持续三周的罢工。
senses.why: The Latin verb mediare means to be in the middle, so the person who stands in the middle of an argument became the mediator.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 mediare 意为「居于中间」，于是站在争吵中间的人就成了调解人。

senses.title: A go-between in business
senses.definition: a person who carries messages or deals between two parties who do not meet directly
senses.definitionCN: 在彼此不直接见面的两方之间传递消息或做成交易的人
senses.example: The mediator found a buyer without revealing the seller.
senses.exampleCN: 中间人在不透露卖方身份的情况下找到了买家。
senses.why: Commerce keeps the same middle position but drops the argument, so the mediator becomes a broker.
senses.whyCN: 商业活动保留了同样的「中间位置」，只是不再有争吵，于是调解人变成居间人。

senses.title: An agent that joins two things
senses.definition: something that connects two separate things or carries an effect from one to the other
senses.definitionCN: 连接两个分隔事物，或把作用从一处传到另一处的东西
senses.example: In the experiment, water acted as a mediator of heat.
senses.exampleCN: 在实验中，水充当热的介质。
senses.why: When the middle thing is not a person but a substance, the middle image turns into a medium.
senses.whyCN: 当处于中间的不是人而是物质时，居中的意象就转成了媒介或介质。

senses.title: An indirect cause or channel
senses.definition: a person or thing through which an effect reaches its final point without direct contact
senses.definitionCN: 使某效果不经直接接触而抵达最终对象的人或物
senses.example: The doctor was the mediator between the new drug and the patients.
senses.exampleCN: 医生是新药与病人之间的渠道。
senses.why: The same middle role now describes a cause acting at a distance.
senses.whyCN: 同样的居中角色此时描述的是隔着距离起作用的原因。

senses.title: A chemical messenger in the body
senses.definition: a substance that carries a signal from one cell or organ to another
senses.definitionCN: 把信号从一个细胞或器官传递到另一个的物质
senses.example: Histamine is a mediator of the allergic response.
senses.exampleCN: 组胺是过敏反应的一种递质。
senses.why: Science narrows the middle role to the molecules that pass a message along.
senses.whyCN: 科学把居中的角色收窄为传递信息的分子。

senses.title: A legal or diplomatic peacemaker
senses.definition: an official or envoy who works between states or parties to settle a dispute
senses.definitionCN: 在国家或团体之间斡旋、以求解决争端的官员或使者
senses.example: The small country offered itself as a mediator between the two powers.
senses.exampleCN: 这个小国自荐充当两个大国之间的调停者。
senses.why: Diplomacy formalizes the middle position as a recognized role with mandates and powers.
senses.whyCN: 外交把居中的位置制度化为一个拥有授权与权力的公认角色。

senses.title: A go-between in a dispute at home
senses.definition: a family member or colleague who tries to settle a quarrel informally
senses.definitionCN: 在家庭或同事之间非正式地说和、平息争吵的人
senses.example: Their aunt was the mediator whenever the family argued at dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 家里吃饭时一吵架，阿姨就是那个说和的人。
senses.why: Even without any institution, anyone who stands between two quarrels earns the name.
senses.whyCN: 即使没有制度背景，任何站在两场争吵之间的人都能被这样称呼。

senses.title: A device that relays a signal
senses.definition: a device or material that passes a signal or energy from one point to another
senses.definitionCN: 把信号或能量从一点传到另一点的装置或材料
senses.example: The engineers used the cable as a mediator of the signal.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师用这根电缆作为信号的传导介质。
senses.why: Technology takes the substance sense and turns it into hardware in the middle of a circuit.
senses.whyCN: 技术把「介质」那层意思变成电路中间的具体硬件。

intro.en: Mediator comes from the Latin verb mediare, to be in the middle, built on the adjective medius, middle.
intro.cn: mediator 来自拉丁语动词 mediare（居于中间），其词干是形容词 medius（中间的）。

items.en: A reconstructed root medhyo meant middle, giving Latin medius.
items.cn: 重构词根 medhyo 意为中间，演化出拉丁语 medius。

items.en: Medius means middle, and mediare means to stand or act in the middle.
items.cn: medius 意为中间的；mediare 意为居于或行于中间。

items.en: Mediator named one who goes between two parties.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 mediator 指在双方之间往来的人。

items.en: Mediateur carried the sense of a peacemaker into French.
items.cn: mediateur 把「说和者」的意思带入法语。

items.en: Mediator entered English as a middleman or peacemaker.
items.cn: mediator 进入英语时指中间人或调停者。

items.en: Modern English widens it to chemical, physical, and diplomatic agents.
items.cn: 现代英语把它扩展到化学、物理与外交上的居间者。

note.en: Mediator is the person in the middle; the family around it runs from mediate and mediation to medium and immediate.
note.cn: mediator 是站在中间的那个人；围绕它的词族从 mediate、mediation 一直到 medium 与 immediate。

entries.definition: to act between two sides to settle a dispute
the process of settling a dispute through a third party
a means of communication or a substance something passes through
happening or acting without anything in between
entries.definitionCN: 立即的；直接的（中间没有别的东西）

entries.definition: an independent person who settles a dispute with a binding decision
entries.definitionCN: 仲裁员（作出有约束力的裁决）

entries.definition: a person who discusses terms on behalf of one side
entries.definitionCN: 谈判者（代表一方谈条件）

entries.definition: a person who ends a quarrel
a person who carries messages between two parties

normalIntro.en: Mediator is built from the Latin middle: medius plus the agent ending -or, so it literally names the one who stands in the middle.
normalIntro.cn: mediator 由拉丁语「中间」构建而成：medius 加施动者词尾 -or，字面就是「站在中间的人」。

normal.en: Medium, immediate, and mediation all keep the middle sense of medius.
normal.cn: medium、immediate 与 mediation 都保留着 medius 的「中间」义。

normal.en: Immediate means no one stands in the middle, so nothing delays.
normal.cn: immediate 表示中间没有别人，所以没有耽搁。

normal.en: Mediate is the verb, mediator is the person, mediation is the act.
normal.cn: mediate 是动词，mediator 是人，mediation 是行为。

normal.en: An arbitrator decides, a mediator helps; only one of them imposes.
normal.cn: 仲裁者作决定，调解人帮忙；只有前者强加结果。

normal.en: Act as a mediator is the standard phrase, not make a mediator.
normal.cn: 固定说法是 act as a mediator，而不是 make a mediator。

abstract.en: Picture two hands reaching toward each other with one palm in between.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手相向伸出，中间隔着一只手掌。

abstract.en: Imagine a bridge pillar standing in the middle of a river.
abstract.cn: 想象一根桥柱立在河中间。

abstract.en: Think of a radio repeater passing a signal from hill to hill.
abstract.cn: 想象一座中继台把信号从一个山头传到另一个山头。

examples.en: They hired a mediator to settle the dispute out of court.
examples.cn: 他们聘请了一位调解人在庭外解决纠纷。

examples.en: The teacher acted as a mediator between the two students.
examples.cn: 老师充当了两名学生之间的调解人。

examples.en: In the body, histamine is an important mediator of inflammation.
examples.cn: 在体内，组胺是炎症的重要递质。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米底阿特」——把 mediator 记成「米袋一放，两边坐下来」，音近而意通于「居中调和」；这只是谐音联想，与真实词源无关。

root: 重构词根 medhyo（中间）→ 拉丁语 medius（中间的）→ mediare（居于中间）→ 晚期拉丁语 mediator（居间者）→ 古法语 mediateur → 英语 mediator，核心义「站在中间的人」。

sensesIntro.en: Mediator starts with a person between two quarrelling sides, widens to any go-between, and then loses the human element to name media, indirect causes, and chemical messengers.
sensesIntro.cn: mediator 先指站在争吵双方之间的人，扩展到任何居间者，再丢掉人的因素，用来指媒介、间接原因与化学信使。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one person standing between two outstretched hands.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在两只伸出的手之间。

branches.en: The plainest branch is the person who settles a quarrel.
branches.cn: 最直接的分支就是平息争吵的那个人。

branches.en: Commerce turns the peacemaker into a professional go-between.
branches.cn: 商业把说和者变成职业化的居间人。

branches.en: Diplomacy formalizes the role as a mandate from states.
branches.cn: 外交把这个角色制度化为国家授予的使命。

branches.en: The middle thing becomes a substance or a device.
branches.cn: 处于中间的事物变成了物质或装置。

branches.en: The middle becomes an indirect cause or a chemical messenger.
branches.cn: 中间者变成间接的原因或化学信使。

intro.en: Mediator is medius plus the agent ending -or; English builds mediate, mediation, and medium on the same middle stem.
intro.cn: mediator 是 medius 加施动者词尾 -or；英语围绕同一「中间」词干构成 mediate、mediation 与 medium。

latinIntro.en: Latin medius means middle; mediare means to be in the middle; mediator means one who goes between.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 medius 意为中间；mediare 意为居于中间；mediator 意为在双方之间往来的人。

items.example: Medius supplies the whole family of middle words.
items.exampleCN: medius 提供整个「中间」词族的源头。

items.example: Mediare is the verb behind the English word.
items.exampleCN: mediare 是英语词的动词来源。

items.example: The Latin noun is taken over almost unchanged.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语名词几乎原样被借入英语。

items.example: The suffix -or marks the person, not the act.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -or 标记的是人，而不是行为。

items.example: Mediate drops the person ending.
items.exampleCN: mediate 去掉了施动者词尾。

items.example: The suffix -ion forms mediation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 构成 mediation。

items.meaning: a means or substance in between
items.example: Medium keeps the middle sense as a thing.
items.exampleCN: medium 把「中间」义保留为物。

items.example: The prefix im- negates the middle in immediate.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 im- 在 immediate 中否定「中间」。

items.example: Immediate shows the negative side of the root.
items.exampleCN: immediate 显示词根的否定面。

items.example: Mediation names the whole process.
items.exampleCN: mediation 指整个调解过程。

definition_zh: 平庸的；中等的；普通的；不突出的；不出色的；马马虎虎的
definition_en: not very good and not very bad either, only about average and of no special quality
core_image: 操场跑道正中：跑在前面的人已到终点，后面的人刚出发，他只停在半山腰
scene: 质检员把一批杯子的成色分为三档，中间那档既没瑕疵也说不上精致，被单独放在一旁。The manager glanced at the fading label on the box and sighed, the hotel was clean but its breakfast was completely mediocre.
sceneCN: 这里 mediocre 是「平庸的；中等的」（第 1 个义项：既不好也不坏，平平无奇）；句意为经理看了眼盒子上褪色的标签叹了口气，酒店很干净，但早餐平平无奇。图中可辨识物件：三档杯子、质检台、纸盒标签。

derivatives.zh: 由 mediocre 去词尾加 -ity 构成，义为「平庸；平庸之才」
由 mediocre 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「平庸地」
mediocrity 的复数，义为「平庸者；平庸之举」
由 mediocre 加 -ness 构成，义为「平庸的状态」

senses.title: Exactly in the middle
senses.definition: sitting in the middle of a range, neither high nor low
senses.definitionCN: 处在某个范围的中间，既不高也不低
