senses.example: The hotel is mediocre: clean rooms, plain food.
senses.exampleCN: 这家酒店是中等的：房间干净，饭菜普通。
senses.why: Latin mediocris is medius plus ocris, a mountain of middle height, so the word began as the middle in a scale.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 mediocris 由 medius（中间）与 ocris（山）合成，原指「中等高度的山」，因此最初表示尺度上的中间。

senses.title: Not very good
senses.definition: of a quality just short of good, disappointing without being bad
senses.definitionCN: 质量略逊于好、令人失望但并不算坏
senses.example: His mediocre exam results closed the door to scholarships.
senses.exampleCN: 他平庸的考试成绩断送了拿奖学金的机会。
senses.why: Once the middle became the standard, average came to be heard as a mild failure.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「中间」成为评判标准，平均就被听成了轻微的失败。

senses.title: Of an ordinary person without distinction
senses.definition: describing a person who has average ability and no special gift
senses.definitionCN: 形容能力中等、没有特殊天赋的人
senses.example: She refused to be a mediocre student and joined the debate team.
senses.exampleCN: 她不愿做一个普通的学生，于是加入了辩论队。
senses.why: The middle height of a hill becomes a metaphor for a mind that never rose above the plain.
senses.whyCN: 「中等的山高」被比喻为从未高出平地的头脑。

senses.title: Second rate in comparison
senses.definition: clearly weaker than something else of the same type
senses.definitionCN: 与同类的另一事物相比明显较弱
senses.example: The sequel felt mediocre beside the original film.
senses.exampleCN: 与第一部相比，这部续集显得平庸。
senses.why: Comparison fixes the middle relative to another thing, so the word can rank downward.
senses.whyCN: 比较把「中间」相对化，于是这个词也可以用来判定偏低。

senses.title: Acceptable but unremarkable work
senses.definition: work that gets the job done but leaves no impression
senses.definitionCN: 能完成任务却不留印象的工作成果
senses.example: The report was mediocre but it met the deadline.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告平平，但赶上了截止日期。
senses.why: In workplaces the middle position is judged by impact, so passable work gets the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 在职场中「中间位置」以影响力评判，因此勉强过关的成果就用这个词。

senses.title: Blaming the average taste
senses.titleCN: （批评）流于平庸的；通俗无趣的
senses.definition: used in criticism of art or taste that plays safe and avoids risk
senses.definitionCN: 用于批评艺术或品味只求稳妥、不敢冒险
senses.example: Critics called the exhibition mediocre and safe.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家说这场展览平庸而保守。
senses.why: Criticism adds disapproval: choosing the middle is itself taken as a lack of ambition.
senses.whyCN: 批评语境增添了不赞同：选择中间本身就被视为缺乏抱负。

intro.en: Mediocre goes back to the Latin compound mediocris, a mountain of middle height, made of medius, middle, and ocris, a mountain.
intro.cn: mediocre 追溯到拉丁语复合词 mediocris，意为「中等高度的山」，由 medius（中间）与 ocris（山）合成。

items.en: Ocris is an old Latin word for a rugged mountain.
items.cn: ocris 是古拉丁语中表示崎岖山丘的词。

items.en: Mediocris joins medius, middle, to that mountain word.
items.cn: mediocris 把 medius（中间）与这个「山」字结合。

items.en: It describes a hill of middling height, half way up a peak.
items.cn: 它形容中等高度的山丘，只有峰顶的一半高。

items.en: Mediocre arrives through French with the sense of middling quality.
items.cn: mediocre 经法语进入英语，义为「中等质量的」。

items.en: In English it soon carries the sense of something second rate.
items.cn: 在英语中它很快就带上了「次一等」的意味。

note.en: Mediocre is a middle-height adjective; its noun mediocrity and the plainer words average and ordinary sit around it.
note.cn: mediocre 是一个表示「中等高度」的形容词；名词 mediocrity 以及更朴素的 average、ordinary 围绕在它周围。

entries.definition: the state of being average or the person who is
in an average or unimpressive way
a middle position or a means
entries.definitionCN: 中等的；媒介（只是共享 medius，不是直接派生）

entries.definition: the middle value of a set of numbers
typical and not special
not unusual in any way
of lower quality than might be expected
of very high quality

normalIntro.en: Mediocre is a mountain phrase hidden in an adjective: medius plus ocris, a hill that never reached the top.
normalIntro.cn: mediocre 是一个藏在形容词里的山岳短语：medius 加 ocris，就是一座从未登顶的山。

normal.en: Mediocrity is the noun, mediocrely the adverb, and mediocre the adjective.
normal.cn: mediocrity 是名词，mediocrely 是副词，mediocre 是形容词。

normal.en: Average is neutral, but mediocre often carries a small complaint.
normal.cn: average 是中性的，而 mediocre 常带一点不满。

normal.en: The opposite of mediocre is excellent, not bad.
normal.cn: mediocre 的反义词是 excellent，而不是 bad。

normal.en: Median and medium share the middle root but are not its derivatives.
normal.cn: median 与 medium 共享「中间」词根，但并非它的派生词。

normal.en: We say mediocre performance and mediocre quality, never a mediocre of something.
normal.cn: 常见搭配是 mediocre performance 与 mediocre quality，不能说 a mediocre of 某物。

abstract.en: Picture a hill standing exactly halfway up a tall mountain.
abstract.cn: 想象一座山丘正立在高山的一半高处。

abstract.en: Imagine a gauge where the needle stops dead centre.
abstract.cn: 想象一根指针停在刻度正中央。

abstract.en: See a report card full of B grades and no marks above that.
abstract.cn: 想象一张全是 B 等成绩的学籍单，没有更高的分数。

examples.en: The film was mediocre, with a thin plot and weak acting.
examples.cn: 这部电影很平庸，情节单薄，表演无力。

examples.en: Even a mediocre effort can win if the rivals are worse.
examples.cn: 如果对手更差，即使是平庸的努力也能赢。

examples.en: Mediocrity inside a team often comes from unclear goals.
examples.cn: 团队内部的平庸往往源于目标不清。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米地奥克」——把 mediocre 记成「平庸的人，米地都拿不到奥克」，音近而意通于「中游水平」；这只是谐音联想，与真实词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 medius（中间）+ ocris（崎岖山地）→ mediocris（中等高度的山）→ 法语 médiocre → 英语 mediocre，核心义「不高不低、停在山腰」。

sensesIntro.en: Mediocre starts at the exact middle of a scale, turns into mild disappointment, then into a judgment on people, results, and culture.
sensesIntro.cn: mediocre 从尺度上的正中间出发，转为轻微的失望，再成为对人、成绩与文化的评判。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hill standing halfway up a mountain.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座立在高山半腰的山丘。

branches.en: The literal branch is the middle position itself.
branches.cn: 字面分支就是「中间位置」本身。

branches.en: Average becomes a quiet complaint about quality.
branches.cn: 「平均」变成对质量的低声抱怨。

branches.en: The middle height describes a person without gifts.
branches.cn: 中等高度形容一个没有突出天赋的人。

branches.en: Comparison ranks the middle below its neighbour.
branches.cn: 比较使中间者在同类之下。

branches.en: Criticism adds design: playing safe is itself a fault.
branches.cn: 批评加上意图：只求稳妥本身就成了缺点。

intro.en: Mediocre is a compound from two Latin pieces, medius and ocris, with the noun mediocrity and the adverb mediocrely built in English.
intro.cn: mediocre 是两个拉丁语要素 medius 与 ocris 的复合词；英语在此基础上构成名词 mediocrity 与副词 mediocrely。

latinIntro.en: Latin medius means middle and the rare ocris means a mountain, so mediocris names a hill of middle height.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 medius 意为中间，生僻的 ocris 意为山，所以 mediocris 指中等高度的山丘。

items.example: Medius is the first half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: medius 是复合词的前半。

items.example: Ocris is the rare second half.
items.exampleCN: ocris 是生僻的后半部分。

items.example: Mediocris is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: mediocris 是直接来源。

items.example: Mediocre enters English through French.
items.exampleCN: mediocre 经法语进入英语。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms mediocrity.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 构成 mediocrity。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms mediocrely.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 mediocrely。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms mediocreness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 mediocreness。

items.example: Mediocrity names the state or the person.
items.exampleCN: mediocrity 指状态或人。

items.example: Mediocrely describes how something is done.
items.exampleCN: mediocrely 描述做事的方式。

definition_zh: 冥想；静坐沉思；深思；考虑；盘算
definition_en: to sit quietly and empty or focus the mind, or to think deeply and carefully about something
core_image: 一个人盘腿静坐，屋里很安静，呼吸放慢，把所有念头一点点收拢
scene: 清晨的院子里没有别的声音，她闭上眼，把呼吸放慢，让杂念一个个退开。Every morning she sits by the window and meditates for twenty minutes before work.
sceneCN: 这里 meditate 是「冥想、静坐安神」（第 1 个义项：坐下让心静下来）；句意为她每天早上坐在窗边冥想二十分钟再去上班。画面可联想：清晨的窗、闭上的眼睛、慢慢放长的呼吸，以及脑中逐渐退开的杂念。

derivatives.zh: 由 meditate 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「冥想；沉思」
由拉丁语 meditativus 构成的形容词，义为「冥想的；沉思的」
由 meditate 加表示「人」的后缀 -or 构成，义为「冥想者」
拉丁语前缀 prae-（在前）加 meditare，义为「预谋」
由 premeditate 加 -ion 构成，义为「预谋」

senses.title: To sit quietly to calm the mind
senses.definition: to sit quietly and keep the mind still or focused, often as a practice
senses.definitionCN: 安静地坐着，让心保持平静或专注，常作为一种练习
senses.example: He meditates for ten minutes after lunch to clear his head.
senses.exampleCN: 他午饭后冥想十分钟，好让脑子清醒。
senses.why: The core image is a mind weighed and turned over in stillness, so meditation first meant thinking carefully and only later came to mean quiet mental training.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是静下来反复衡量一件事的心；所以「冥想」先从安静地思考长出来，后来才专门指一种让心安静的训练。

senses.title: To think deeply about something
senses.definition: to think long and carefully about a subject
senses.definitionCN: 对某个题目长时间细细地思考
senses.example: She sat by the river and meditated on the choices ahead of her.
senses.exampleCN: 她坐在河边，沉思眼前的选择。
senses.why: Meditation in the Latin tradition was deliberate reflection, so the verb keeps the image of the mind working slowly over one idea.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁传统里的静观就是有意识地反复思考，所以这个动词一直保留着「心在一件事上慢慢打转」的画面。

senses.title: To consider doing something
senses.definition: to think seriously about doing something, often something difficult
senses.definitionCN: 认真考虑做某事，常指不太容易做到的事
senses.example: The directors meditated a change of plan but said nothing yet.
senses.exampleCN: 董事们在盘算改变方案，却还没有对外说什么。
senses.why: Once the mind turns a plan over again and again, the verb slides into weighing an action before taking it.
senses.whyCN: 当心把计划翻来覆去掂量时，这个动词就从「沉思」滑到「考虑要不要采取行动」。

senses.title: To weigh something in the mind
senses.definition: to go over a matter again and again in the mind
senses.definitionCN: 在心里把一件事翻来覆去地想
senses.example: She meditated the matter in silence until a plan took shape.
senses.exampleCN: 她把这件事在沉默中反复琢磨，直到计划成形。
senses.why: The Latin source carries the measured image of weighing, and that image survives whenever we say we are turning something over in the mind.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁来源里带着「称量」的画面，所以每当我们说在心里反复翻检一件事，这个画面就还在。

senses.title: To reflect on life in a solemn way
senses.definition: to think quietly and seriously about life, death, or what matters
senses.definitionCN: 安静而严肃地思考生命、死亡或真正重要的事
senses.example: In the churchyard the visitors meditated on how short life is.
senses.exampleCN: 墓园里，来访者静思人生何其短暂。
senses.why: Because the image is a still and solemn mind, the verb also covers the thoughtful mood of religion and philosophy.
senses.whyCN: 画面的基调安静而庄重，所以这个词也覆盖宗教与哲思里那种沉静的情怀。

senses.title: To plan something in secret
senses.definition: to work out a plan quietly, often before acting on it
senses.definitionCN: 安静地把计划想清楚，常在行动之前进行
senses.example: For weeks he meditated revenge while smiling at his rival.
senses.exampleCN: 他笑着面对对手，暗地里盘算了好几个星期的报复。
senses.why: A plan weighed in silence easily turns into a plan kept out of sight, which is why premeditated means planned beforehand.
senses.whyCN: 在沉默中掂量的计划很容易变成藏在心里的计划，这也是 premeditated 表示「事先想好的」的原因。

senses.title: To focus the mind on a spiritual aim
senses.definition: to give the mind firmly to a spiritual idea or practice
senses.definitionCN: 把心安住在某个精神层面的观念或修炼上
senses.example: Each evening the monks meditate on the meaning of change.
senses.exampleCN: 僧人们每晚凝神观照变化的含义。
senses.why: When the object of the deep thought is sacred, the same verb names a spiritual discipline rather than ordinary reflection.
senses.whyCN: 当深思的对象变成神圣之物，同一个动词指的就成了一种修行，而不只是普通的思虑。

intro.en: Meditate comes from Latin meditari, to think about or practise, probably from the same root as mederi, to heal; the link is an image of a mind that measures and cares for what it turns over.
intro.cn: meditate 来自拉丁语 meditari（思考、练习），一般认为与 mederi（医治）同源；这条线索的画面是：一颗心既在衡量，也在照看它所思之事。

items.en: A reconstructed root med- suggests measuring, taking thought, or caring for.
items.cn: 一般认为可重构为「衡量、思虑或照看」一类的词根形式。

items.en: Meditari means to think over, reflect on, or practise a thing.
items.cn: meditari 意为反复思考、沉思或练习某事。

items.en: Mederi, to heal or look after, is probably kin and gives the image of care.
items.cn: mederi 意为医治、照看，一般认为与之同源，带来「照看」的意象。

items.en: Roman writers use meditari for rehearsing speeches and preparing the mind.
items.cn: 罗马作家用 meditari 表示演练演说、让心做好准备。

items.en: English meditacion names religious reflection before the verb meditate settles.
items.cn: 英语先出现 meditacion，指宗教性的省思，之后才有动词 meditate。

items.en: Meditate now covers calm mental training, careful thought, and planning.
items.cn: 现代英语里，meditate 兼指静心训练、细心深思与计划。

note.en: Meditate belongs to the meditation family and to a circle of quiet thinking words, from ponder to contemplate.
note.cn: meditate 属于 meditation 一词的家族，也落在表示安静思考的词群里，如 ponder 与 contemplate。

entries.definition: the practice of calming the mind or the act of deep thought
showing calm and deep thought
a person who practises meditation
to think about something carefully over a period of time
to think deeply about something for a long time
to think quietly and carefully about something

normalIntro.en: The word carries a measured, still mind, and the premeditated family shows what happens when that mind works on a plan.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词的画面是一颗在静默中衡量的心；premeditated 这一家族正好说明，当这颗心去盘算计划时会发生什么。

normal.en: Meditate on a question means to think it over slowly.
normal.cn: meditate on 一个问题，就是把它慢慢地反复想。

normal.en: Meditation is the noun, meditator is the person, meditative is the mood.
normal.cn: 名词是 meditation，冥想者是 meditator，沉思的神态是 meditative。

normal.en: Premeditated means planned in advance, a plan thought over before the act.
normal.cn: premeditated 表示事先盘算，即在行动之前就把计划想好了。

normal.en: Meditate often takes on or upon before its object.
normal.cn: meditate 接宾语时常用 on 或 upon。

normal.en: The same verb covers calming the mind and weighing an idea.
normal.cn: 同一个动词既指让心静下来，也指把想法反复掂量。

abstract.en: Think of a pond going still until the ripples disappear.
abstract.cn: 想象一池水慢慢静下来，涟漪一圈圈消失。

abstract.en: Picture a speaker rehearsing every sentence in an empty hall.
abstract.cn: 想象演说者在空荡的大厅里把每一句都排练一遍。

abstract.en: Imagine a monk watching one candle flame for an hour.
abstract.cn: 想象一位僧人对着一点烛火看上一小时。

examples.en: She meditates for twenty minutes every morning before work.
examples.cn: 她每天早上上班前冥想二十分钟。

examples.en: He meditated on the offer for two days before replying.
examples.cn: 他对这个提议琢磨了两天才回复。

examples.en: The plan was meditated for months before anyone spoke of it.
examples.cn: 这个计划在无人提起之前已被反复盘算了数月。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「没地退」——心里没地方可退，只好坐下来静静冥想；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为源自拉丁语 meditari（反复思考、练习），与 mederi（医治、照看）为同源近邻，可追溯至重构词根 med-（衡量、思虑）→ 经法语进入英语 meditate，核心义「在心里反复衡量」。

sensesIntro.en: Meditate starts from a mind that is still and weighed, giving the sense of quiet practice, then deep thought, and finally planning or thinking over an action.
sensesIntro.cn: meditate 从一颗安静而反复衡量的心出发，先长出静心练习义，再延伸为深思，最后落到盘算与考虑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person sitting still with the mind turned over like a weighed stone.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人静静坐着，把心事像石头一样反复掂量。

branches.en: Quiet sitting is the body of the practice sense.
branches.cn: 安静地坐着，是冥想这一义项的身体动作。

branches.en: Slow thought about a subject grows straight out of weighing.
branches.cn: 对某个题目慢慢思考，直接由「掂量」长出来。

branches.en: A plan under consideration is a further reach of the same turning over.
branches.cn: 被考虑的方案，是同一个「翻检」动作再向前一步。

branches.en: Practice, thought, and spiritual focus all share a still mind.
branches.cn: 练习、思考与凝神都共享一颗安静的心。

branches.en: A thought kept out of sight turns into a plan, even a revenge.
branches.cn: 藏在心里的想法会变成计划，甚至变成报复的盘算。

intro.en: Meditate grows a small English family of nouns, adjectives, and agents, plus the premeditation words built with Latin prae-.
intro.cn: meditate 在英语里长出一个不大的家族，包括名词、形容词与施事者，还有借助拉丁前缀 prae- 的 premeditation 一组词。

latinIntro.en: Latin meditari carries the thought, and mederi, to heal, is its probable relative; the Latin noun meditatio is the direct source of the English noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 meditari 承载「思虑」义，mederi（医治）被认为是它的近亲；拉丁名词 meditatio 是英语名词的直接来源。

items.example: Meditari is the direct source of the English verb.
items.exampleCN: meditari 是英语动词的直接来源。

items.example: The ending -ate shapes meditate from Latin forms.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 把拉丁词形收拢成 meditate。

items.example: He meditated on the plan all night.
items.exampleCN: 他整夜都在思量这个计划。

items.example: Meditating each day helps her stay calm.
items.exampleCN: 每天冥想让她保持平静。

items.example: The suffix -ion gives meditation.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ion 构成 meditation。

items.meaning: the act or practice of reflecting
items.example: Meditation can be a simple breathing exercise.
items.exampleCN: 冥想可以只是一种简单的呼吸练习。

items.example: The suffix -ive gives meditative.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ive 构成 meditative。

items.example: The suffix -or gives meditator.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -or 构成 meditator。

items.example: The prefix prae- gives premeditate.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 prae- 构成 premeditate。

items.example: Premeditate extends the planning sense.
items.exampleCN: premeditate 把「盘算」义推到行动之前。

definition_zh: 冥想；静坐；沉思；深思；静观
definition_en: the practice of sitting quietly to calm or focus the mind, or long serious thought about something
core_image: 一个人盘腿坐着，闭眼垂肩，屋里只听得见自己的呼吸声
scene: 考试前的那个晚上，学生关了灯，靠着枕头什么都不想，只数着自己的呼吸。Guided meditation helps many students stay calm before an exam.
sceneCN: 这里 meditation 是「冥想、静坐安神」（第 1 个义项：坐下来让心静下来）；句意为引导式冥想帮助许多学生在考试前保持平静。画面可联想到：关掉的灯、靠着的枕头、数着呼吸的夜晚，以及慢慢稳下来的心跳。

derivatives.zh: meditation 的动词形式，义为「冥想；沉思」
由拉丁语 meditativus 构成，义为「冥想的；沉思的」
由 meditate 加表示「人」的后缀 -or 构成，义为「冥想者」
拉丁语前缀 prae-（在前）加 meditatio，义为「预谋」

senses.title: The practice of calming the mind
senses.definition: the practice of sitting quietly and training the mind to be calm or focused
senses.definitionCN: 安静地坐着，训练心平静或专注的练习
senses.example: Meditation for ten minutes a day can ease stress.
senses.exampleCN: 每天冥想十分钟可以缓解压力。
senses.why: Because the core image is a mind made still on purpose, meditation names the whole training of that stillness as a noun.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一颗被有意安顿下来的心，于是 meditation 作为名词，指的就是对这种安静状态的整体训练。

senses.title: Deep thought about something
senses.definition: long and careful thought about a subject
senses.definitionCN: 对某个题目长时间而仔细的思考
senses.example: In meditation she went over the letter word by word.
senses.exampleCN: 她在沉思中把那封信逐字过了一遍。
senses.why: Before it named a seated practice, meditation meant serious reflection, and that older sense still runs under the calm image.
senses.whyCN: 在指坐下来练习之前，meditation 本来指的是严肃的思考，这个较早的含义至今仍在这幅安静的画面之下延续。

senses.title: A written reflection
senses.definition: a written text of serious reflection on a religious or moral theme
senses.definitionCN: 就宗教或道德主题写下的严肃反思文字
senses.example: His meditations on mortality were published after his death.
senses.exampleCN: 他关于生死的冥想文字在他去世后才出版。
senses.why: Once deep thought takes a written form, the noun can name the book as well as the act.
senses.whyCN: 一旦深思落成文字，这个名词既可以指动作，也可以指那本书。

senses.title: Spiritual contemplation
senses.definition: concentrated attention on a sacred idea as a spiritual exercise
senses.definitionCN: 把注意力集中在神圣观念上的精神修炼
senses.example: The monks spent the afternoon in silent meditation.
senses.exampleCN: 僧人们整个下午都在静默中观照。
senses.why: Religious use keeps the still mind of the image and points it at something sacred.
senses.whyCN: 宗教用法保留了画面里的那颗静心，只是把它对准了神圣之物。

senses.title: A state of being absorbed in thought
senses.definition: a condition in which the mind is wholly absorbed in one thought
senses.definitionCN: 心思完全沉浸在某个念头里的状态
senses.example: She was so lost in meditation that she did not hear the door.
senses.exampleCN: 她沉思得太入神，连门声都没听见。
senses.why: When the practice is intense, the noun stops naming the activity and names the absorbed state instead.
senses.whyCN: 当练习足够投入时，这个名词就不再指活动本身，而指那种全神贯注的状态。

senses.title: A plan weighed in the mind
senses.definition: the quiet working out of a plan, sometimes before acting
senses.definitionCN: 安静地把计划想清楚，有时是在行动之前
senses.example: The killing was the fruit of long meditation and careful timing.
senses.exampleCN: 这场凶案是长期盘算与精心择时的结果。
senses.why: The weighing image underneath the word lets it reach out to plans that are thought through before they happen.
senses.whyCN: 词底下的「称量」画面让它可以延伸到事先想透的计划。

senses.title: The training of attention by quiet sitting
senses.definition: the systematic training of attention through sitting quietly
senses.definitionCN: 通过静坐对注意力进行系统训练
senses.example: Mindfulness meditation trains people to notice thoughts without holding on to them.
senses.exampleCN: 正念冥想训练人们察觉念头而不去抓住它。
senses.why: Modern psychology took the calm image and built a measurable exercise around it, giving more meditation styles their names.
senses.whyCN: 现代心理学接过了这幅安静的画面，围绕它建立起可测量的练习，于是各种冥想流派也都有了名字。

intro.en: Meditation comes from Latin meditatio, reflection, from the verb meditari, to think over, which is probably related to mederi, to heal.
intro.cn: meditation 来自拉丁语 meditatio（省思），源于动词 meditari（反复思考）；一般认为与 mederi（医治）同源。

items.en: The reconstructed root med- carries the sense of measuring or giving thought.
items.cn: 一般认为重构词根 med- 带有「衡量、思虑」之意。

items.en: Meditari means to think over or practise a thing.
items.cn: meditari 意为反复思考或练习某事。

items.en: Meditatio names the act of such thought, and writers also used it for exercises of the mind.
items.cn: meditatio 指这种思考的行为，文人也用它指精神操练。

items.en: Meditacion carries the word into French use.
items.cn: meditacion 把这个词带入法语。

items.en: Meditacioun appears in English religious writing for devout reflection.
items.cn: 英语宗教写作里出现 meditacioun，指虔诚的省思。

items.en: Meditation later takes on secular training of attention and calm sitting.
items.cn: 现代英语里，meditation 又兼指世俗化的注意力训练与静坐。

note.en: Meditation is the noun behind meditate, close to contemplation and reflection and to its own verb family.
note.cn: meditation 是 meditate 背后的名词，与 contemplation、reflection 意义相近，也自成动词家族。

entries.definition: to sit quietly or think deeply
calm and thoughtful in manner
someone who meditates regularly
deep and steady thought
careful thinking about the past or about oneself
the practice of paying calm attention to the present

normalIntro.en: The noun wraps the verb meditate in the suffix -ion, and the whole family shares one still, weighed mind.
normalIntro.cn: 名词 meditation 就是动词 meditate 套上后缀 -ion，整个家族共享一颗安静而反复衡量的心。

normal.en: Meditation is the noun of meditate; the -ion turns the act into a thing you can practise.
normal.cn: meditation 是 meditate 的名词，后缀 -ion 把动作变成一个可以练习的东西。

normal.en: Guided meditation means someone talks you through it.
normal.cn: guided meditation 指有人在旁边引导你完成。

normal.en: In meditation can mean while thinking deeply.
normal.cn: in meditation 可以表示正处于深思之中。

normal.en: The plural meditations often means a book of reflections.
normal.cn: 复数形式 meditations 常指一本反思录。

normal.en: Premeditation is planning in advance, built on the same weighing image.
normal.cn: premeditation 指事先谋划，建立在同一个「掂量」的画面上。

abstract.en: Picture a phone lying face down while a person breathes slowly nearby.
abstract.cn: 想象一部手机屏幕朝下放着，而旁边的人正在慢慢呼吸。

abstract.en: See a cushion on the floor and one candle burning steadily.
abstract.cn: 想象地上的一个坐垫，和一支静静燃烧的蜡烛。

abstract.en: Imagine a diary filled with one short thought on every page.
abstract.cn: 想象一本日记，每一页只写着一句短思。

examples.en: She begins the day with twenty minutes of meditation.
examples.cn: 她以二十分钟的冥想开始新的一天。

examples.en: His book is a series of meditations on friendship.
examples.cn: 他的书是一系列关于友谊的思考。

examples.en: After years of meditation, he found it easier to stay calm.
examples.cn: 经过多年的冥想，他发现自己更容易保持平静。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「没地推」——心里没地方推托，只好坐下来慢慢冥想；只是谐音联想，与真实词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 meditari（反复思考、练习）→ 晚期拉丁语 meditatio（省思）→ 古法语 meditacion → 英语 meditation，一般认为与 mederi（医治）同源，核心义「在心里反复衡量」。

sensesIntro.en: Meditation begins as deliberate reflection, then becomes the named practice of a calm mind, and from there extends to written reflections, spiritual contemplation, and absorbed thought.
sensesIntro.cn: meditation 起初指有意识的省思，后来成为「让心安静」这一练习的名称，再从此延伸出反思文字、宗教观照与全神沉思。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one person seated still with the breathing as the only sound.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人静坐不动，屋子里只剩呼吸声。

branches.en: Sitting still to calm the mind is the practice sense.
branches.cn: 静坐安神是冥想这一义项的主体。

branches.en: Deep thinking is the older sense that still lives under the calm.
branches.cn: 深思是更早的含义，至今仍藏在这份安静之下。

branches.en: Written reflection and spiritual contemplation put the still mind into words and prayer.
branches.cn: 静思录与宗教观照把静心放进文字与祈祷。

branches.en: Practice and attention training are the same exercise named by different schools.
branches.cn: 静坐练习与注意力训练，是不同流派对同一练习的两种命名。

branches.en: Absorbed thought and quiet planning are what the calm mind does with its time.
branches.cn: 全神沉思与盘算筹谋，是静下来的心用时间做的事。

intro.en: Meditation is the -ion noun of meditate, and the family spreads to meditate, meditative, meditator, and premeditation.
intro.cn: meditation 是 meditate 加后缀 -ion 得到的名词，家族延伸到 meditate、meditative、meditator 与 premeditation。

latinIntro.en: Latin meditatio, from meditari, supplies both the noun and the reflection image behind English meditation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 meditatio 出自 meditari，为英语 meditation 提供了名词形式与「反思」的意象。

items.example: Meditari is the verb beneath the noun.
items.exampleCN: meditari 是这组名词底下的动词。

items.example: Meditatio is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: meditatio 是直接来源。

items.example: Meditate is the action form.
items.exampleCN: meditate 是动作形式。

items.example: Meditate is the everyday verb.
items.exampleCN: meditate 是日常使用的动词。

items.example: The suffix -ion gives meditation.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ion 构成 meditation。

items.example: The suffix -ive gives meditative.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ive 构成 meditative。

items.example: Meditative music suits the practice.
items.exampleCN: 冥想音乐适合这种练习。

items.example: The suffix -or gives meditator.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -or 构成 meditator。

items.example: The prefix prae- gives premeditation.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 prae- 构成 premeditation。

items.example: Premeditation extends the planning sense.
items.exampleCN: premeditation 把「盘算」义推到行动之前。

definition_zh: 褪黑素；褪黑激素
definition_en: a hormone made in the brain that rises in darkness and helps the body know when it is night and time to sleep
core_image: 天色变黑，脑子里的一个小腺体悄悄放出激素，人开始发困
scene: 旅行者跨过好几个时区，明明是大白天却困得睁不开眼，晚上又睡不着。Jet lag happens because the body releases melatonin on the old schedule for several days.
sceneCN: 这里 melatonin 是「褪黑素、褪黑激素」（第 1 个义项：夜里分泌、帮助人入睡的激素）；句意为时差反应之所以出现，是因为身体连续几天仍按原来的作息时间分泌褪黑素。画面可联想：大白天里发困的旅客、酒店厚窗帘遮出的暗房，以及慢慢调回正常的睡眠节律。

derivatives.zh: 由 melatonin 加后缀 -ergic 构成，指与褪黑素神经传递相关的（少数专业用法）
由 melatonin 加 receptor 构成的复合名词，义为「褪黑素受体」

senses.title: The sleep hormone
senses.definition: a hormone that the pineal gland releases during darkness and that helps set the bodys sleep rhythm
senses.definitionCN: 松果体在黑暗时释放、帮助设定睡眠节律的激素
senses.example: Melatonin levels rise after dark and fall again at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 天黑之后褪黑素水平上升，黎明时又回落。
senses.why: The core image is a gland that answers to darkness, so the word first names one natural chemical messenger of sleep.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一个对黑暗作出反应的腺体，所以这个词首先指一种天然的、传递睡意的化学信使。

senses.title: The supplement in a bottle
senses.definition: a tablet or capsule containing this hormone, which people take for sleep problems
senses.definitionCN: 人们为睡眠问题服用的、含同种激素的片剂或胶囊
senses.example: Some travellers take melatonin to adjust their sleep after a long flight.
senses.exampleCN: 有些旅行者长途飞行后服用褪黑素来调整睡眠。
senses.why: Once the hormone is put into a bottle, the same word names the product on the shelf.
senses.whyCN: 当这种激素被装进瓶子，同一个词也就指货架上的那件产品。

senses.title: A marker of body clock
senses.titleCN: 生物钟指标；褪黑素节律
senses.definition: the daily pattern of this hormone, taken as a marker of the internal body clock
senses.definitionCN: 以这种激素的起伏作为人体内在生物钟的日常标志
senses.example: Researchers use melatonin as a marker of the internal clock.
senses.exampleCN: 研究人员把褪黑素用作体内生物钟的标志。
senses.why: Because the hormone tracks light and dark so faithfully, it also serves as a clock reading for scientists.
senses.whyCN: 因为这种激素如此忠实地反映昼夜，它也就成了科学家读取生物钟的一张时间表。

intro.en: Melatonin is a modern coined word: it names a substance first isolated by Aaron Lerner in 1958, built from related chemistry words rather than an ancient root.
intro.cn: melatonin 是现代新造词，指阿龙·勒纳于一九五八年首次分离出的物质，由相关的化学片段拼成，而不是来自古代词根。

items.en: The opening m points back to mustard, melanin, and dark-coloured compounds that chemists had in view.
items.cn: 词首的 m 呼应芥菜、黑色素以及化学家当时关注的深色化合物。

items.en: Chemists rarely take whole Latin words; they build names from fragments that point at related compounds.
items.cn: 化学家很少整词借用拉丁语，而是用指向相关化合物的片段拼出名称。

items.en: The ending follows amine naming, as in serotonin, with tone standing for the tightening action of such amines.
items.cn: 词尾沿用胺类的命名方式，如 serotonin 中 tone 表示这类胺的收缩作用。

items.en: Aaron Lerner and his colleagues isolated the substance from the pineal gland, found that it lightened skin, and named it melatonin.
items.cn: 一九五八年，阿龙·勒纳与同事从松果体中分离出这种物质，发现它能使皮肤变浅，于是命名为 melatonin。

items.en: Melatonin passes quickly into medical and popular English as both a hormone and a supplement.
items.cn: melatonin 很快作为激素名与保健品名进入专业与大众英语。

items.en: Today the word mostly appears in sleep research, travel advice, and product labels.
items.cn: 如今这个词多见于睡眠研究、出行建议与产品标签。

note.en: Melatonin is built like other hormone names and sits beside light, sleep, and the pineal gland; its near words are from biology rather than etymological kin.
note.cn: melatonin 的构词方式与其他激素名相同，常常和光、睡眠、松果体放在一起；它的近邻多来自生物学，而不是同源词。

entries.definition: a brain chemical linked to mood and wellbeing
a brain chemical involved in reward and movement
the dark pigment in skin, hair, and eyes
a chemical made in the body that controls a process
the daily cycle of the body clock
the habit of being unable to sleep

normalIntro.en: Melatonin is a chemistry word, so the pieces to hold on to are the words built from the same naming pattern and what the hormone does at night.
normalIntro.cn: melatonin 是化学命名造出来的词，所以真正该记住的，是与它同式构词的伙伴名，以及这种激素夜里做的事。

normal.en: Melatonin is a hormone, so it is uncountable when the general idea is meant.
normal.cn: melatonin 是激素名，泛指这种物质时不用数。

normal.en: Serotonin and melatonin share the ending -tonin, and both are hormones of the brain.
normal.cn: serotonin 与 melatonin 共享词尾 -tonin，都是脑中的激素。

normal.en: Melatonin supplements are sold in many countries, often for sleep problems.
normal.cn: 许多国家都售卖褪黑素补充剂，多用于睡眠问题。

normal.en: Light controls melatonin, so bright screens at night delay it.
normal.cn: 光会影响褪黑素，所以夜里面对亮屏幕会推迟它分泌。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with melanin, the pigment, though the names look alike.
normal.cn: 不要把它和表示色素的 melanin 混淆，虽然拼写很像。

abstract.en: Picture a small dark room where the body starts to feel sleepy.
abstract.cn: 想象一间暗下来的小屋，身体开始发困。

abstract.en: See travellers in a bright hotel room pulling the curtains shut so they can sleep.
abstract.cn: 想象旅行者在明亮的酒店房间里拉上窗帘，好让自己睡着。

abstract.en: Think of a clock whose hands move only when the lights go out.
abstract.cn: 想象一只只有在灯灭后才走动的钟。

examples.en: Bright light at night can lower melatonin levels.
examples.cn: 夜里的强光会降低褪黑素水平。

examples.en: Melatonin is often used to help people sleep after long flights.
examples.cn: 褪黑素常被用来帮助人们长途飞行后入睡。

examples.en: The body naturally releases melatonin as darkness falls.
examples.cn: 天黑时身体会自然释放褪黑素。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「没了他特困」——没了它便特别困，音与意都能钩住 melatonin；这只是谐音联想，非词源。

root: 现代化学造词：词首 m 呼应黑色素一类的变色化合物（邻词如 melanin），词尾 -tonin 仿血清素 serotonin 一类胺类物质的命名习惯；一九五八年由勒纳等人命名，无古典词根可循。

sensesIntro.en: Melatonin starts as the natural hormone of darkness, then as the supplement version of that hormone, and finally as a scientific marker of the internal clock.
sensesIntro.cn: melatonin 先指黑暗中分泌的天然激素，再指瓶中出售的同种补充剂，最后成为科研中读取生物钟的指标。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small gland in the brain answering darkness by sending out a sleepy signal.
core.cn: 核心意象：脑中一个小腺体对黑暗作出反应，放出让人发困的信号。

branches.en: The natural hormone of darkness is the first sense.
branches.cn: 黑暗中分泌的天然激素，是第一个义项。

branches.en: The pill on the shelf is the hormone in a bottle.
branches.cn: 货架上的药片，就是装进瓶子的这种激素。

branches.en: As a marker of the body clock, the hormone becomes data for scientists.
branches.cn: 作为生物钟的指标，这种激素成了供科学家读取的数据。

branches.en: The daily rise and fall of the hormone is what makes it a clock reading.
branches.cn: 这种激素每日的起伏，正是它成为生物钟读数之处。

branches.en: Travellers and researchers both use melatonin to follow the internal clock.
branches.cn: 旅行者与研究者都用褪黑素来对照内在的生物钟。

intro.en: Melatonin has no Latin affixes of the old kind; it is a modern chemistry coinage whose pieces echo related compound names.
intro.cn: melatonin 没有传统意义上的拉丁词缀，它是现代化学造词，各片段呼应着相关化合物的名字。

latinIntro.en: The word borrows chemistry convention, not Latin grammar: the opening fragment points to dark colouring and the ending follows amine naming.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词借用的是化学命名惯例，而不是拉丁语语法：开头一段指向深色，结尾沿用了胺类的命名法。

items.meaningCN: 取自相关色素化合物名的首字母
items.example: The opening fragment echoes melanin and its relatives.
items.exampleCN: 开头片段呼应 melanin 及其近亲。

items.example: The form appears in words for dark pigmentation.
items.exampleCN: 这个词素出现在表示深色色素的词里。

items.example: The ending follows the pattern of serotonin.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾沿用了 serotonin 的模式。

items.example: Serotonin shares the ending with melatonin.
items.exampleCN: serotonin 与 melatonin 共享词尾。

items.meaning: a body chemical that controls a process
items.example: Melatonin is one kind of hormone.
items.exampleCN: 褪黑素是众多激素中的一种。

items.meaning: relating to the small gland in the brain
items.example: The pineal gland makes melatonin.
items.exampleCN: 松果体分泌褪黑素。

items.example: Melatonin is sometimes discussed for insomnia.
items.exampleCN: 人们有时会讨论用褪黑素应对失眠。

items.meaning: a site where a hormone acts
items.example: Melatonin receptors sit in the brain.
items.exampleCN: 褪黑素受体位于脑中。

items.meaningCN: 由某种物质起作用的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ergic appears in melatoninergic.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ergic 出现在 melatoninergic 中。

definition_zh: 合并；融合；使混为一体；（牌戏中）摊牌；叠合
definition_en: to mix or join things so that they become one whole, especially sounds, ideas, or colours; in card games, to lay down a combination of cards
core_image: 两种不同的颜色在调色盘上被搅成一个新的颜色
scene: 音乐厅里，吉他、笛子和人声同时响起，渐渐听不出各自的边界。In the recording studio, the producer tried to meld the folk melody with electronic beats.
sceneCN: 这里 meld 是「融合、合为一体」（第 1 个义项：把不同事物合成为一件）；句意：在录音棚里，制作人试着把民谣旋律与电子节拍融合起来。

pos.zh: 合并体；融合物；（牌戏）摊出的一组牌

collocations.phrase: meld the old and the new

derivatives.zh: 由现在分词名词化，义为「融合；合并的过程」
过去分词形容词化，义为「被融合的；合并成的」

senses.title: To blend into one whole
senses.definition: to mix different things so closely that they seem to be one
senses.definitionCN: 把不同的事物紧密混合，使它们看起来成了一个整体
senses.example: The band melds jazz and folk music in every song.
senses.exampleCN: 这支乐队在每首歌里都把爵士与民谣融合在一起。
senses.why: The blend image comes from card players combining their separate cards into one table group, so the word pictures pieces that stop being separate.
senses.whyCN: 「融合」的画面来自牌手把各自分开的牌叠成桌上一组，所以这个词描绘的是不再彼此分开的部件。

senses.title: To blend gradually into surroundings
senses.titleCN: 渐渐消融于；与……融为一体
senses.definition: to pass so smoothly into something else that the border is no longer visible
senses.definitionCN: 平滑地过渡到另一事物之中，以致看不到分界
senses.example: The valley mist melds into the morning sky.
senses.exampleCN: 山谷的雾气渐渐消融进清晨的天空。
senses.why: If two things are melded, the line between them disappears, so the word naturally describes one thing dissolving into another.
senses.whyCN: 两物一旦融合，其间的界线就消失了，所以这个词顺理成章地用来描写一物消融于另一物。

senses.title: To merge formally or systematically
senses.definition: to combine separate parts, often companies, methods, or data, into a single organized unit
senses.definitionCN: 把分开的部分，常指公司、方法或数据，合并成一个有组织的整体
senses.example: The two departments will meld their records into one system.
senses.exampleCN: 两个部门将把各自的记录整合进同一套系统。
senses.why: Business and science borrow the card-table merging for formal combination, so the soft image of blending becomes a deliberate administrative merging.
senses.whyCN: 商业与科学借用了牌桌上的合牌义来表示正式合并，于是柔软的「交融」画面变成了有意的行政整合。

senses.title: A laid-down group of cards
senses.definition: in card games, a set or run of cards shown and played together
senses.definitionCN: 在牌戏中，一起亮出并打出的一组同点或同花的牌
senses.example: He laid down a meld of three kings.
senses.exampleCN: 他摊出了三张 K 组成的一组牌。
senses.why: This is the original gaming sense: players meld by placing matching cards face up as one combined set.
senses.whyCN: 这是最初的牌戏义项：玩家把相互匹配的牌正面朝上叠放成一组，这就是 meld。

senses.title: A blended product
senses.definition: something produced by combining different elements, such as a style or a dish
senses.definitionCN: 由不同元素组合而成的产物，如一种风格或一道菜
senses.example: Her cooking is a meld of French technique and Asian spices.
senses.exampleCN: 她的厨艺是法国技法与亚洲香料的融合体。
senses.why: When the action of melding is finished, the result takes the noun form, naming the blended thing itself.
senses.whyCN: 融合的动作完成之后，结果便用名词形式来表示，直指被融合出来的那个东西。

intro.en: Meld appears in English in the early twentieth century for laying cards on the table; its earlier origin is uncertain and may come from French or from the related words melt and weld.
intro.cn: meld 在二十世纪初的英语中表示「在牌桌上摊牌」，更早的来源不确定，可能来自法语，也可能与 melt、weld 有关。

items.en: The deeper origin of meld is uncertain; it may be French or an alteration of melt or weld.
items.cn: meld 更早的来源不确定，可能来自法语，也可能是 melt 或 weld 的变体。

items.en: In early poker and rummy circles, a meld is a set of cards placed on the table.
items.cn: 在早期的扑克与拉米牌圈子里，meld 指摊在桌上的一组牌。

items.en: The word first appears in print mainly around card-play reporting.
items.cn: 这个词最早主要见于牌局报道的印刷文字中。

items.en: The meaning widens from cards to any combination of parts into one group.
items.cn: 词义从纸牌扩展到任何把各部分组合为一组的做法。

items.en: Today meld ranges from blended music styles to merged company records and data.
items.cn: 今天 meld 涵盖从音乐风格的融合到公司记录与数据的合并。

note.en: Meld is close in spelling to melt, weld, and meld as a card term, and in meaning to blend and merge.
note.cn: meld 在拼写上接近 melt、weld 与作为牌戏术语的 meld，在意义上接近 blend 与 merge。

entries.definition: to join pieces of metal by heating them
entries.definitionCN: 焊接；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to change from solid to liquid through heat
entries.definitionCN: 熔化；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to interfere in something that is not your business
entries.definitionCN: 干涉；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to mix things so that they combine smoothly
to join two things into one
to join parts into a single whole, often formally

normalIntro.en: Meld is the card-table word for laying several cards down as one group, later widened to any joining into one.
normalIntro.cn: meld 原是牌桌上的词，指把几张牌叠放在一起当作一组，后来扩展到任何合成一体的做法。

normal.en: Meld into is the usual pattern when one style or sound dissolves into another.
normal.cn: 当一种风格或声音溶入另一种时，常用「meld into」这个结构。

normal.en: Meld with means two things join and keep some of their own colour.
normal.cn: 「meld with」表示两物结合，同时各自还保留一点本色。

normal.en: In card games a meld is a set of cards shown openly.
normal.cn: 在牌戏里，一个 meld 就是亮在桌上的一组牌。

normal.en: The noun a meld of styles names the blended result.
normal.cn: 名词短语 a meld of styles 指融合之后的那件成品。

normal.en: Compare merge: merge is neutral and businesslike, meld adds the idea of smooth blending.
normal.cn: 对比 merge：merge 中立、偏事务性，meld 多一层「平滑交融」的意味。

abstract.en: Picture two ribbons of paint turning into one colour on the palette.
abstract.cn: 想象两条颜料在调色盘上搅成同一种颜色。

abstract.en: Imagine a choir singing so tightly that no single voice stands out.
abstract.cn: 想象一个合唱团唱得如此紧密，听不出任何一个人的声音。

abstract.en: Think of two companies filing their papers into one shared folder.
abstract.cn: 想象两家公司把各自文件归进同一个共享文件夹。

examples.en: The new cafe melds old brick walls with modern glass.
examples.cn: 这家新咖啡馆把旧砖墙与现代玻璃融合在一起。

examples.en: Her voice slowly melds into the sound of the wind.
examples.cn: 她的歌声慢慢融进风声里。

examples.en: The committee must meld the two proposals into a single plan.
examples.cn: 委员会必须把两份提案整合成一个方案。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「没得」——两样东西一合并，「没得」差别了；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 来源不确定：meld 约二十世纪初见于英语，原为牌戏用语，指摊出的一组牌；可能与 melt、weld 有关，也可能来自法语，核心义「把分开的东西合成一体」。

sensesIntro.en: Meld starts as a card term for a set laid on the table, then widens to mixing things into one and to the blended result.
sensesIntro.cn: meld 最初是牌戏中「摊在桌上的一组牌」，后来扩展为把事物融合为一体，以及融合之后的成品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two colours stirred into one new colour.
core.cn: 核心意象：两种颜色被搅成一种新颜色。

branches.en: Blending things into one whole is the main modern sense.
branches.cn: 把不同事物融合为一个整体是最主要的现代义项。

branches.en: Gradual dissolving into surroundings is the softer picture.
branches.cn: 渐渐消融于周围环境是更柔和的画面。

branches.en: Formal merging of records or methods is an organized version of the same image.
branches.cn: 记录或方法的正式整合是同一意象的组织化版本。

branches.en: The card sense is the original gaming use of the word.
branches.cn: 牌戏义项是这个词最初的游戏用法。

branches.en: A meld as a product is the result left after blending.
branches.cn: 作为产物的 meld 是融合之后留下的结果。

intro.en: Meld has no clear productive affixes; it works as a simple verb and noun, with melding and melded forming around it.
intro.cn: meld 没有明确的构词词缀，它就是单纯的动词和名词，周围只衍生出 melding 与 melded。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin form can be reconstructed for meld, so mostly French and card-game vocabulary is listed.
latinIntro.cn: meld 无法可靠地追溯到某个拉丁语形式，所以这里主要列出法语与牌戏词汇。

items.example: Meld is the base verb.
items.exampleCN: meld 是基础动词。

items.example: The noun names a blended result.
items.exampleCN: 名词形式指融合出来的整体。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms melding.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 melding。

items.meaning: towards a state of being one
items.example: Meld into shows one thing dissolving into another.
items.exampleCN: meld into 表示一物溶入另一物。

items.example: Meld with keeps both sides in view.
items.exampleCN: meld with 让双方都还在视野里。

items.example: Meld together stresses the joining.
items.exampleCN: meld together 强调合到一起。

items.example: Weld is a spelling neighbour, not a relative.
items.exampleCN: weld 只是拼写相近，并非同源。

items.example: Blend is the closest meaning partner.
items.exampleCN: blend 是意义最接近的伙伴。

definition_zh: 旋律的；曲调的；旋律优美的；悦耳的
definition_en: relating to melody, or having a pleasant, easily remembered tune
core_image: 一个人跟着曲调轻轻哼唱，音高像台阶一样上下起伏
scene: 安静的琴房里，老师让初学者先不要加伴奏，只把调子唱准。She was praised for writing pieces with a strong melodic line.
sceneCN: 这里 melodic 是「旋律的、与曲调有关的」（第 1 个义项：与旋律这一音乐要素相关）；句意：她因写出旋律线条鲜明的小曲而受到称赞。

collocations.zh: 极具旋律性的；很好听的

derivatives.zh: 由 -ic 形容词加 -ally 构成副词，义为「在旋律上；从旋律方面」
同源近形词，义为「旋律优美的、悦耳的」
去掉 -ic 后的基础名词，义为「旋律；曲调」

senses.title: Relating to melody
senses.definition: connected with the tune rather than with rhythm, harmony, or words
senses.definitionCN: 与曲调相关的，而不是与节奏、和声或歌词相关
senses.example: The score shows a simple melodic line over a slow bass.
senses.exampleCN: 乐谱上是一条简单的旋律线配着缓慢的低音。
senses.why: The suffix -ic turns melody into an adjective of relation, so melodic simply means belonging to melody, the tune that goes up and down.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -ic 把 melody 变成表示「与……相关」的形容词，所以 melodic 直接指属于旋律、即上下起伏的那条曲调。

senses.title: Being full of a pleasant tune
senses.definition: containing a tune that is easy to follow and pleasant to hear
senses.definitionCN: 含有容易跟随、听起来悦耳的曲调
senses.example: Their new album is melodic and easy on the ear.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的新专辑旋律优美、很入耳。
senses.why: From merely relating to a tune, the word extends to having a good one, so melodic becomes a word of praise for music that sings.
senses.whyCN: 从「只是与曲调相关」扩展到「有一条好的曲调」，于是 melodic 成了赞美音乐「能唱出来」的词。

senses.title: Sounding like music in speech
senses.titleCN: （言语或声音）有韵律的、如歌的
senses.definition: used of speech or a natural sound that rises and falls in a tuneful way
senses.definitionCN: 形容言语或自然声音以抑扬有致的方式起伏，像唱歌一样
senses.example: Grandmother said goodnight in a soft melodic voice.
senses.exampleCN: 奶奶用柔和如歌的声音道了晚安。
senses.why: Speech has its own rise and fall of pitch, so the tune image transfers from music to voices and even to birdsong.
senses.whyCN: 说话本身就有音高的升降，于是旋律的画面从音乐迁移到人声，乃至鸟鸣。

intro.en: Melodic comes through French and Late Latin from Greek melōidia, meaning a singing together, formed from melos, a song, and aeidein, to sing.
intro.cn: melodic 经由法语与后期拉丁语，源自希腊语 melōidia（一同歌唱），由 melos（歌）与 aeidein（唱）组成。

items.en: Melos means a song or a limb of a song, and aeidein means to sing.
items.cn: melos 意为歌或歌的一段，aeidein 意为唱。

items.en: Melōidia means a singing together or a song.
items.cn: melōidia 意为一同歌唱或一首歌。

items.en: Melodia passes into Latin as the name of a tune.
items.cn: melodia 进入拉丁语，用来指曲调。

items.en: Melodie gives French its word for a song or tune.
items.cn: melodie 为法语提供了表示歌或曲调的词。

items.en: The English noun melody appears in this period; the adjective melodic is built on it much later.
items.cn: 英语名词 melody 在这一时期出现；形容词 melodic 则是更晚从它构出来的。

note.en: Melodic sits in the word family of melody alongside melodious and melodramatic, and in meaning beside harmonious and lyrical.
note.cn: melodic 与 melodious、melodramatic 同属 melody 的词族，在意义上与 harmonious、lyrical 相邻。

entries.definition: a tune, or the melody part of music
sweet and tuneful to hear
entries.definitionCN: 同源近形词，义为「旋律优美的」

entries.definition: showing exaggerated emotion
entries.definitionCN: 同根但意义远离，义为「戏剧化、夸张的」

entries.definition: pleasing because parts fit well together
having a pleasant tune
expressing strong feeling in a song-like way

normalIntro.en: Melodic means shaped like a melody: first as a plain relation to the tune, then as praise for a good tune, then for anything that rises and falls like song.
normalIntro.cn: melodic 意为「像旋律那样的」：先是单纯与曲调相关，再是赞美曲调好听，最后形容任何像唱歌般起伏的事物。

normal.en: A melodic line is the tune you hum after hearing it once.
normal.cn: melodic line 就是你听过一遍就能哼出来的那条曲调。

normal.en: A melodic instrument plays the tune rather than the beat.
normal.cn: 旋律乐器演奏的是曲调，而不是节拍。

normal.en: Highly melodic is a quick way to praise a song.
normal.cn: 「highly melodic」是夸奖一首歌的快捷说法。

normal.en: The adverb melodically means in a tuneful way.
normal.cn: 副词 melodically 表示以有曲调的方式。

normal.en: Compare melodious: melodious praises the sound itself, melodic stresses the structure of the tune.
normal.cn: 对比 melodious：melodious 夸的是声音本身，melodic 强调曲调的结构。

abstract.en: Picture notes stepping up and down like a staircase you can hum.
abstract.cn: 想象音符像一级级台阶上下起伏，你可以哼着走完。

abstract.en: Imagine a friend humming the same tune days later.
abstract.cn: 想象朋友几天后还在哼同一段调子。

abstract.en: Think of a mother speaking to a baby with a gentle rising voice.
abstract.cn: 想象母亲用轻柔上扬的声音对婴儿说话。

examples.en: Critics praised the film for its melodic score.
examples.cn: 评论家称赞这部电影的配乐旋律优美。

examples.en: Her poetry has a melodic quality, as if it were written for singing.
examples.cn: 她的诗有一种如歌的韵律，仿佛是为歌唱而写的。

examples.en: The piano part is largely melodic, while the drums keep the beat.
examples.cn: 钢琴声部主要由旋律构成，鼓则负责保持节拍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「没落第」——这段旋律优美的曲子让选手「没落第」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 melos（歌）+ aeidein（唱）→ melōidia（歌唱）→ 后期拉丁语 melodia → 古法语 melodie → 英语 melody，再加 -ic 构成 melodic，核心义「像歌一样起伏的曲调」。

sensesIntro.en: Melodic begins as a neutral adjective for the tune itself, then becomes praise for a good tune, and finally extends to voices and sounds that rise and fall like music.
sensesIntro.cn: melodic 最初只是中性地说「关于曲调的」，之后成为对好听曲调的赞美，最后扩展到像音乐一样起伏的嗓音与声音。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hummed tune stepping up and down.
core.cn: 核心意象：一段被哼唱的调子上上下下。

branches.en: The structural sense relates the adjective to melody as a musical element.
branches.cn: 结构义把形容词与作为音乐要素的旋律联系起来。

branches.en: The evaluative sense praises music with a good tune.
branches.cn: 评价义用于赞美旋律好听的音乐。

branches.en: The extended sense moves the tune image into speech and natural sound.
branches.cn: 引申义把旋律的画面移到言语与自然声中。

branches.en: Both a melodic line and a melodic voice follow a clear rise and fall of pitch.
branches.cn: 旋律线与如歌的嗓音都遵循清晰的音高起伏。

branches.en: Praise for a good tune easily transfers to any pleasing sound.
branches.cn: 对好曲调的赞美很容易迁移到任何悦耳的声音上。

intro.en: Melodic is the adjective built on melody with -ic, and it feeds words such as melodically and the related melodious.
intro.cn: melodic 是用 -ic 从 melody 构成的形容词，又衍生出 melodically，并与 melodious 相关联。

latinIntro.en: The Greek base melos and aeidein reached Latin as melodia, the tune from which melody and melodic both descend.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊词基 melos 与 aeidein 以 melodia 的形式进入拉丁语，指曲调，melody 与 melodic 都由它而来。

items.example: Melos is the Greek source of the first half.
items.exampleCN: melos 是这个词前半部分的希腊来源。

items.example: Aeidein gives the singing half of melody.
items.exampleCN: aeidein 为 melody 提供「唱」的部分。

items.example: Melody is the base noun.
items.exampleCN: melody 是基础名词。

items.example: The suffix -ic forms the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 构成形容词。

items.example: Melodic describes a tune directly.
items.exampleCN: melodic 直接描述曲调。

items.example: The suffix -ally forms the adverb melodically.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ally 构成副词 melodically。

items.example: The suffix -ious forms melodious.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ious 构成 melodious。

items.example: Melodious stresses the sweet sound.
items.exampleCN: melodious 强调声音甜美。

items.meaningCN: 情节夸张、配有音乐的戏剧
items.example: Melodrama once meant a musical drama.
items.exampleCN: melodrama 原指带音乐的戏剧。

items.example: Melodically shows how something is sung.
items.exampleCN: melodically 说明某物是怎样被唱的。

definition_zh: 旋律；曲调；主旋律；优美的乐曲
definition_en: a series of musical notes that form a tune, or the tune carried by the leading part of a piece
core_image: 一个人用手指在桌面上点出一段熟悉的曲调，音符一高一低连成线
scene: 咖啡馆里，钢琴师先弹出一个简短好记的调子，再在旁边添上和弦。The audience hummed the melody long after the concert ended.
sceneCN: 这里 melody 是「旋律、曲调」（第 1 个义项：能单独听出来的曲调）；句意：音乐会结束后很久，观众还在哼那段旋律。

derivatives.zh: 加 -ic 构成形容词，义为「旋律的；旋律优美的」
同源近形词，义为「悦耳的、像歌一样的」
加 -ist 构成，义为「作曲家；歌唱家」
由 melodic 加 -ally 构成，义为「在旋律上」

senses.title: A tune carried by notes
senses.definition: a series of notes arranged in time that forms a recognisable tune
senses.definitionCN: 按时间先后排列、形成可辨认曲调的一串音符
senses.example: The song has a simple melody that children can sing.
senses.exampleCN: 这首歌有一个孩子都会唱的简单旋律。
senses.why: The Greek word meant a song, so a melody is first the singable shape of notes, the part you whistle.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词本义就是「歌」，所以旋律首先是一串可以唱出来的音符形状，也就是你随口吹出的那一段。

senses.title: The leading part in music
senses.definition: the part of a piece that carries the tune, as opposed to harmony and accompaniment
senses.definitionCN: 承载曲调的那个声部，与和声和伴奏相对
senses.example: Pass the melody to the violins in the second movement.
senses.exampleCN: 在第二乐章里把主旋律交给小提琴。
senses.why: When several parts play at once, only one carries the tune, so melody comes to name that leading line.
senses.whyCN: 几个声部同时演奏时，只有一条在唱曲调，于是 melody 也用来指这条领奏的旋律线。

senses.title: Sweet and pleasing sound
senses.titleCN: 优美的乐声；悦耳的声音
senses.definition: a sequence of pleasant sounds, sometimes of speech or nature, that seems musical
senses.definitionCN: 一串悦耳的声音，有时指言语或自然之声，听起来像音乐
senses.example: In the quiet valley you hear the melody of birds and water.
senses.exampleCN: 在安静的山谷里，你能听见鸟与水交织成的声音。
senses.why: Because a melody pleases the ear, the word extends to any pleasing sequence of sound that rises and falls like song.
senses.whyCN: 因为旋律使耳朵愉悦，这个词就扩展到任何像歌声般起伏、令人愉悦的声音序列。

intro.en: Melody reaches English through Old French melodie and Latin melodia from Greek melōidia, a song, made of melos, a song or tune, and aeidein, to sing.
intro.cn: melody 经由古法语 melodie 与拉丁语 melodia，源自希腊语 melōidia（歌），由 melos（歌、曲调）与 aeidein（唱）组成。

items.en: Melos means a song, a tune, or a limb of a song; aeidein means to sing.
items.cn: melos 意为歌、曲调或歌的一段；aeidein 意为唱。

items.en: Melōidia means singing or a song, sometimes referring to music set to words.
items.cn: melōidia 意为歌唱或歌，有时指配有歌词的音乐。

items.en: Melodia enters Latin as the name of a tune.
items.cn: melodia 作为曲调的名称进入拉丁语。

items.en: Melodie carries the word forward in French.
items.cn: melodie 使这个词在法语中延续。

items.en: Melody is first used in English for sweet sound and song.
items.cn: melody 最初在英语中用来指甜美的声音与歌唱。

items.en: Music theory fixes melody as the tune in contrast with harmony.
items.cn: 在近现代音乐理论中，melody 固定指与和声相对的曲调。

note.en: Melody belongs to the family of melodic, melodious, and melodist, and sits near harmony, tune, and refrain.
note.cn: melody 属于 melodic、melodious、melodist 构成的词族，并与 harmony、tune、refrain 意义相邻。

entries.definition: relating to a tune
pleasingly tuneful
entries.definitionCN: 同源近形词，义为「悦耳的」

entries.definition: a singer or a writer of tunes
a series of notes that is pleasant to hear
notes sounded together to support a tune
the part of a song that repeats

normalIntro.en: Melody means a song and its singable shape; from that it names the leading line in music and any sweet run of sound.
normalIntro.cn: melody 本指歌与歌的可唱形状，由此又指音乐中的领奏旋律，以及任何甜美的声音序列。

normal.en: A catchy melody is one that stays in your head.
normal.cn: a catchy melody 就是会一直留在脑子里的旋律。

normal.en: The main melody is the line everyone recognises first.
normal.cn: 主旋律就是大家最先认出来的那条线。

normal.en: To compose a melody is to write that tuneful line.
normal.cn: compose a melody 就是写出那条有曲调的线。

normal.en: The plural is melodies, so two or more tunes.
normal.cn: 复数是 melodies，即两段或多段曲调。

normal.en: Compare tune: tune is everyday and chatty, melody is how music books talk.
normal.cn: 对比 tune：tune 日常随意，melody 是音乐书里的说法。

abstract.en: Picture fingers tapping a nursery tune on a table top.
abstract.cn: 想象手指在桌面上敲出一段儿歌的调子。

abstract.en: Imagine a single line drawn high and low across a music score.
abstract.cn: 想象乐谱上一条上下起伏的单独曲线。

abstract.en: Think of a bird repeating the same short tune at dawn.
abstract.cn: 想象黎明时一只鸟反复唱着同一小段调子。

examples.en: She wrote the lyrics first and then found a melody for them.
examples.cn: 她先写好了歌词，然后为歌词找了一段旋律。

examples.en: The melody rises in the chorus and falls at the end.
examples.cn: 旋律在副歌处上扬，又在结尾处回落。

examples.en: Some melodies are so famous that everyone can hum them.
examples.cn: 有些旋律太出名了，人人都能哼出来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「买劳迪」——「买」到好听的曲调，大家都叫「劳迪」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 melos（歌、曲调）+ aeidein（唱）→ melōidia（歌）→ 拉丁语 melodia → 古法语 melodie → 英语 melody，核心义「可以唱出来的一串音符」。

sensesIntro.en: Melody starts from the Greek idea of a song, narrows into the singable sequence of notes, then into the leading part of music, and widens again to any sweet run of sound.
sensesIntro.cn: melody 从希腊语「歌」的观念出发，收窄为可唱的音符序列，再专指音乐中的领奏声部，最后又扩展为任何甜美的声音序列。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a familiar tune hummed without words.
core.cn: 核心意象：一段不用歌词也能哼出的熟悉曲调。

branches.en: The tune sense is the direct heir of the Greek word for song.
branches.cn: 曲调义直接继承了希腊语「歌」的含义。

branches.en: The leading-part sense comes from polyphonic music, where only one line sings the tune.
branches.cn: 领奏义来自复调音乐，其中只有一条声部唱曲调。

branches.en: The sweet-sound sense extends the tune to pleasing non-musical sound.
branches.cn: 悦耳义把曲调扩展到非音乐的悦耳声音。

branches.en: Both the tune and the birdsong share a rising and falling line.
branches.cn: 曲调与鸟鸣共享一条上下起伏的线。

branches.en: A recognisable melody is what lets listeners pick out the leading part.
branches.cn: 一条可辨认的旋律正是听众分辨出领奏声部的依据。

intro.en: Melody is a Greek compound of song and singing, and it has gathered a large family of English words around it.
intro.cn: melody 是希腊语中「歌」与「唱」的复合词，周围聚集了一大批英语同族词。

latinIntro.en: Greek melōidia passed into Latin as melodia and Old French as melodie before English took it up.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 melōidia 先以 melodia 进入拉丁语，再成为古法语的 melodie，之后才被英语吸收。

items.example: Melos supplies the tune part of the word.
items.exampleCN: melos 提供这个词中「曲调」的部分。

items.example: Aeidein supplies the singing action.
items.exampleCN: aeidein 提供「唱」这个动作。

items.example: Melodia is the Latin stepping stone.
items.exampleCN: melodia 是过渡的拉丁语形式。

items.example: Melody is the modern noun.
items.exampleCN: melody 是现代名词。

items.example: The suffix -ic forms melodic.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 构成 melodic。

items.example: The suffix -ious forms melodious.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ious 构成 melodious。

items.example: The suffix -ist forms melodist.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ist 构成 melodist。

items.example: The suffix -ally forms melodically.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ally 构成 melodically。

items.example: Melodic is the adjective of relation.
items.exampleCN: melodic 是表示关联的形容词。

items.example: Melodrama keeps the song element in its name.
items.exampleCN: melodrama 的名字里仍保留着「歌」的成分。

definition_zh: 值得记住的；难忘的；令人印象深刻的
definition_en: worth remembering because it is unusual, important, or strongly felt
core_image: 一张老照片被指腹反复摩挲，边角发白，可画面依旧清晰
scene: 多年后，老人从相册里抽出一张海边合影，指腹摩着发白的边角说那天风大得说不出话。It was a memorable evening on the coast.
sceneCN: 这里 memorable 是「难忘的」（第 2 个义项：带来强烈个人感受而留在记忆里）；句意：那是海岸边一个难忘的夜晚。

pos.zh: 值得记住的；难忘的；令人印象深刻的

collocations.zh: 令人印象深刻的台词；名句

derivatives.zh: 令人难忘地（形容词加 -ly 成副词，强调动作被记住的方式）
记忆；记忆力（同出拉丁 memoria）
纪念碑；纪念物（以拉丁 -alis 构成，由「记忆」转为「用于纪念的事物」）
记住；背熟（同一词根加动词后缀，由「记住」转为「使进入记忆」的动作）
备忘录（拉丁 gerundive，字面为「应被记住之事」）

senses.title: Worth being remembered
senses.definition: good or interesting enough to deserve being kept in mind
senses.definitionCN: 足够好或足够有趣，因而值得留在记忆里
senses.example: The guide gave a memorable account of the ruins.
senses.exampleCN: 导游对这片遗址的讲述令人难忘。
senses.why: The suffix -able means worthy of being, so the word literally says worth remembering.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -able 意为「值得被……」，所以这个词字面上就是「值得被记住」。

senses.title: Strongly felt, hard to forget
senses.definition: so strongly felt that it stays in the mind long after the event
senses.definitionCN: 感受如此强烈，事件过去很久仍留在心里
senses.example: Their welcome was memorable for its warmth.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的迎接因那份热情而令人难忘。
senses.why: From being worth remembering it grows into being unforgettable in practice.
senses.whyCN: 从「值得记住」发展到实际上「忘不掉」。

senses.title: Unusually talked about
senses.definition: notably unusual or impressive, often used of a line, an idea, or a phrase
senses.definitionCN: 格外特别或出色，常用于句子、想法、词语
senses.example: The novel opens with a memorable sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说以一个令人难忘的句子开篇。
senses.why: What people cannot stop repeating is what the mind keeps, so the word marks quotable things.
senses.whyCN: 人们不停复述的东西正是心里存下的东西，于是这个词被用来标记值得被引用的东西。

senses.title: Used of an occasion
senses.definition: said of an evening, a trip, or a ceremony that will be looked back on with pleasure
senses.definitionCN: 指回想起来会感到愉快的夜晚、旅程或仪式
senses.example: They marked the opening with a memorable dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用一顿难忘的晚宴庆祝开幕。
senses.why: Rites are designed to be stored, so the adjective settles naturally on occasions.
senses.whyCN: 仪式本来就是为被记住而设计的，所以这个形容词很自然地落在场合上。

senses.title: Easy to keep in mind
senses.definition: easily retained by mind, often because it is simple, catchy, or well made
senses.definitionCN: 由于简单、好记或做得好而容易被记住
senses.example: A memorable logo is one you can draw from memory.
senses.exampleCN: 好的标志是你仅凭记忆就能画出来的那种。
senses.why: Recall follows design: what is shaped simply slips into long-term memory.
senses.whyCN: 回想取决于设计：造型简单的东西容易滑进长期记忆。

senses.title: Worthy of note
senses.definition: deserving to be mentioned or recorded after an event
senses.definitionCN: 在事后值得被提及或记录
senses.example: Only two outcomes were memorable enough to report.
senses.exampleCN: 只有两种结果值得报告。
senses.why: The same root names the act of bringing to mind, so memorable also means worth calling up in words.
senses.whyCN: 同一词根也指「把事唤回心里」，所以 memorable 也能指值得被用语言唤回的东西。

senses.title: Memorable as a polite verdict
senses.definition: used politely of something odd or awkward that happened, when a blunt word would offend
senses.definitionCN: 委婉地形容发生过的古怪或尴尬之事，直说会冒犯人
senses.example: The presentation was memorable, if not entirely clear.
senses.exampleCN: 那次汇报令人印象深刻，虽然不完全清晰。
senses.why: A courteous speaker avoids judgment by pointing instead at how well it stuck.
senses.whyCN: 讲礼貌的人不评判好坏，只指出它印象有多深。

senses.title: Memorable in business use
senses.titleCN: （商业用语）令人记住的品牌信息
senses.definition: in marketing, describing a message or a brand that people can recall without prompting
senses.definitionCN: 营销中指人们不提示就能回想起来的讯息或品牌
senses.example: The campaign was measured by how memorable it was.
senses.exampleCN: 这次宣传以它给人留下的记忆深浅来衡量。
senses.why: Advertising asks if the message is remembered without help, which turns the adjective into a metric.
senses.whyCN: 广告要问讯息能否在无人提示时被想起，这就把这个形容词变成了一个指标。

senses.title: Memorable in exams and study skill
senses.definition: describing a method or a note that makes material stick in the mind
senses.definitionCN: 形容让材料牢牢进入记忆的方法或笔记
senses.example: Visual maps make dates more memorable for many students.
senses.exampleCN: 对许多学生来说，图示让年代更容易记住。
senses.why: Study advice judges methods by what they leave behind, so the adjective becomes a quality of technique.
senses.whyCN: 学习建议按「留下什么」来评判方法，于是这个形容词成了技巧的属性。

intro.en: Memorable is Latin memor「mindful, remembering」 plus the adjective suffix -able, which says worthy of being, so the word means worthy of being remembered. The deeper origin of memor is not settled.
intro.cn: memorable 由拉丁 memor「留心的、记得的」加形容词后缀 -able 构成，后者表示「值得被……」，所以词义是「值得被记住的」。memor 的更深来源未有定论。

items.en: Memor meant mindful or remembering. Its deeper origin is uncertain, and any older root form offered for it is a reconstruction rather than a proven derivation.
items.cn: memor 意为「留心的、记得的」。它的更深来源不确定，为其设想的更早词根形式只是重构，不是已证实的派生。

items.en: Memorare, a verb from memor, meant to bring to mind or recount, and memorialis meant recorded for remembrance.
items.cn: 由 memor 派生的动词 memorare 意为「使想起、讲述」，形容词 memorialis 意为「留作纪念的」。

items.en: Memorabilis, meaning that may be remembered, joined memor with the suffix -abilis, the ancestor of English -able.
items.cn: memorabilis（可被记住的）把 memor 与后缀 -abilis 结合，后者是英语 -able 的前身。

items.en: Old French memorable and the Latin form both fed English; the French spelling dropped the final -bilis ending.
items.cn: 古法语 memorable 与拉丁形式都进入英语；法语拼写把词尾 -bilis 简省了。

items.en: Memorable is recorded in English from the fifteenth century, at first meaning fitted to be remembered or worthy of record.
items.cn: memorable 在十五世纪已有英语记录，最初意为「适合被记住的、值得记录的」。

items.en: The modern sense widens from worthy of record to striking, exceptional, or merely polite praise.
items.cn: 现代义从「值得记录」扩展到「引人注目的、出色的」，乃至仅仅表示客气的称赞。

note.en: The first group holds words that share the root of remembering, from memor to memorial; the second holds adjectives that also praise something as striking or excellent.
note.cn: 第一组是共享「记住」词根的词，从 memor 到 memorial；第二组是同样用来称赞某物突出或出色的形容词。

entries.definition: something set up to keep a person or event in memory
entries.definitionCN: 旨在令人记住某人或某事的纪念物

entries.definition: to learn by heart on purpose
the faculty of remembering, or a past event that is recalled
entries.definitionCN: 记忆能力，或所回想的往事

entries.definition: a short written note or message in an office
entries.definitionCN: 办公室里简短的书面便条

entries.definition: so striking that it can never be forgotten
entries.definitionCN: 深刻得永远无法忘记的

entries.definition: unusual enough to be noticed and talked about
entries.definitionCN: 不同寻常到值得注意和谈论的

entries.definition: important enough to be recorded or mentioned
entries.definitionCN: 重要得值得记录或提及的

entries.definition: attracting attention at once, especially by its appearance
entries.definitionCN: 尤指因外表而立即吸引注意的

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real suffix, the true word family, and fixed phrases that show what the adjective is usually used for.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的后缀、真实的词族，以及显示这个形容词常用在什么对象上的固定搭配。

normal.en: Memor is mindful and -able says worthy of being, so the word spells out worth remembering.
normal.cn: memor 是「留心」，-able 是「值得被……」，所以这个词直接拼出「值得被记住」。

normal.en: The family runs memory, memorize, memorial and memorandum, all built on the noun of remembering.
normal.cn: 同族词有 memory、memorize、memorial、memorandum，都建立在「记住」这一名词之上。

normal.en: Fixed objects: a memorable experience, a memorable occasion, a memorable performance, memorable lines.
normal.cn: 固定对象：难忘的经历、值得纪念的场合、难忘的表演、令人印象深刻的台词。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with memorial, the thing built, and with memorized, the act completed in the past.
normal.cn: 别与 memorial（建起来的纪念物）以及 memorized（过去完成的动作）混淆。

normal.en: Compare unforgettable: unforgettable insists on permanence, while memorable leaves room for degrees.
normal.cn: 对比 unforgettable：unforgettable 强调永久，memorable 则留有程度差别。

abstract.en: Picture a photograph worn pale at the corners by a thumb, the picture still sharp.
abstract.cn: 想象一张照片边角被拇指摩得发白，画面却依然清晰。

abstract.en: Picture a single line of a play that the whole audience repeats on the way home.
abstract.cn: 想象散场路上，满场观众都在重复戏里同一句台词。

abstract.en: Picture a hand writing a date on the inside of a drawer, where it will be seen every day.
abstract.cn: 想象有人把一个日子写在抽屉内侧，每天都看得见。

examples.en: The trip was memorable for the people we met, not the places we saw.
examples.cn: 这次旅行令人难忘，是因为遇到的人，而不是看过的景。

examples.en: She delivered a memorable answer in fewer than ten words.
examples.cn: 她用不到十个词给出了一个令人难忘的回答。

examples.en: Good teachers turn dull dates into memorable stories.
examples.cn: 好老师能把枯燥的年代变成难忘的故事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「么么若宝」——够宝贝、够珍贵的东西，才值得被记在心里；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 memor（留心的、记得的）+ 形容词后缀 -abilis（值得被……）→ memorabilis（可被记住的）→ 古法语 memorable → 英语 memorable，核心义「值得被记住」。memor 更深来源不确定，属「一般认为」层面。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses grow from one judgement: something is worth keeping in mind. That judgement narrows to a personal feeling, to quotable language, to occasions, to ease of recall, to notice, to polite hedging, and to the practical measures of marketing and study.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都从一个判断生长出来：某物值得留在心里。这个判断依次收窄为个人感受、可被引用的语言、特定场合、易记程度、值得提及，再到委婉用语，以及营销与学习中的实用指标。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old photograph worn pale at the corners, kept because every look brings the scene back whole.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张边角磨白的老照片，之所以留着，是因为每次看都能把那个场景原样唤回。

branches.en: WORTH AND MENTION: worthy of being remembered first, then worth naming afterwards.
branches.cn: 值得与被提及：先是值得记住，再是事后值得被说起。

branches.en: STICKING POWER: felt so strongly that it stays, and designed so simply that it returns.
branches.cn: 留存之力：感受强烈因而留下，设计简单因而能再被唤起。

branches.en: THINGS THAT HOLD: memorable lines in a text and memorable occasions in a life.
branches.cn: 承载之物：文本里的难忘句子，生活里的难忘场合。

branches.en: POLITE COVER: saying memorable when unforgettable would be too kind.
branches.cn: 客气的遮盖：当 unforgettable 说出来太客气时，改说 memorable。

branches.en: MEASURED USE: marketing and study counsel both ask what people can recall unaided.
branches.cn: 被度量的用法：营销与学习建议都在问人能独立回想起多少。

intro.en: Memorable is a clean two part word: the Latin stem memor of remembering, and the suffix -able of worthiness.
intro.cn: memorable 是干净的两段式词：表示「记住」的拉丁词干 memor，以及表示「值得」的后缀 -able。

latinIntro.en: Latin memor and memoria give memory, memorize, memorial and memorandum; the suffix -abilis, through French -able, gives readable, visible and durable.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 memor 与 memoria 衍生 memory、memorize、memorial、memorandum；后缀 -abilis 经法语 -able 衍生 readable、visible、durable。

items.example: Memor is the stem of every word in the family.
items.exampleCN: memor 是这一整族词的词干。

items.example: Memorabilis is the direct Latin parent.
items.exampleCN: memorabilis 是直接的拉丁语母词。

items.meaning: worthy of being, able to be
items.example: The suffix -able turns memorize into memorable.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -able 把 memorize 变成 memorable。

items.meaning: in a way that has that quality
items.example: The adverb memorably keeps the judgement in motion.
items.exampleCN: 副词 memorably 让这个判断落到动作上。

items.meaning: the faculty or store of remembering
items.example: Memory names what memorable is worth entering.
items.exampleCN: memory 指的是 memorable 值得进入的那个地方。

items.example: A memorial is built rather than felt.
items.exampleCN: memorial 是被建起来的，而不是被感受到的。

items.example: Memorize names the act, memorable the quality.
items.exampleCN: memorize 指动作，memorable 指性质。

items.example: A memorandum is a note written to be remembered.
items.exampleCN: 备忘录是为了被记住而写下的字条。

items.example: She memorably opened with one question.
items.exampleCN: 她令人难忘地以一个提问开场。

definition_zh: 备忘录；备忘便条；〈法律〉交易备忘录
definition_en: a short written note or document that records something so that it will not be forgotten
core_image: 便签夹里夹着一张薄纸，开头印着一行字：此事须记住
scene: 会议散了，大家还在走廊里说话，助理回到座位补写一张薄纸，开头是「请各部门于周五前回复」。The manager sent a short memorandum to every department.
sceneCN: 这里 memorandum 是「备忘录」（第 1 个义项：机构内部为传达事项而写的简短文件）；句意：经理给每个部门发了一份简短的备忘录。

pos.zh: 备忘录；备忘便条；交易备忘录

derivatives.zh: 便条；备忘录（memorandum 的截短形式，多用于口语与办公场合）
备忘录的复数（保留拉丁语中性复数词尾）
难忘程度；值得记住的品质（源自同族形容词 memorable）
记忆；记忆力（同出拉丁 memoria）
纪念碑；纪念物（拉丁 -alis 构词，义为用于纪念之物）

senses.title: A short official note
senses.definition: a short written message circulated inside an organization to pass on policy, information, or instructions
senses.definitionCN: 机构内部传阅的简短书面讯息，用以传达政策、信息或指示
senses.example: A memorandum confirmed the new start time.
senses.exampleCN: 一份备忘录确认了新的上班时间。
senses.why: A written record outlives memory, so the Latin phrase for a thing to be remembered becomes the paper itself.
senses.whyCN: 书面记录比记忆活得更久，于是拉丁语的「应被记住之事」变成了那张纸本身。

senses.title: A reminder note
senses.definition: an informal note made only to help oneself remember a detail later
senses.definitionCN: 只为帮助自己日后记住某个细节而写的非正式便条
senses.example: He kept a memorandum beside the door listing what to take.
senses.exampleCN: 他在门边放了一张便条，列着要带的东西。
senses.why: The oldest sense is the personal reminder, one mind writing to its future self.
senses.whyCN: 最早的义项就是个人的备忘，是一个头脑写给将来的自己。

senses.title: A record of an agreement
senses.definition: a document that records what was discussed or agreed, often before a binding contract is signed
senses.definitionCN: 记录已讨论或已议定事项的文件，常在正式合同签订之前
senses.example: Both sides signed a memorandum of understanding.
senses.exampleCN: 双方签署了一份谅解备忘录。
senses.why: Agreement rests on memory too, so diplomats and partners use a memorandum to fix what was said.
senses.whyCN: 协议同样依赖记忆，因此外交官与合作方用备忘录把说过的话固定下来。

senses.title: A diplomatic communication
senses.definition: in diplomacy, a summary of facts or a statement of position handed between states
senses.definitionCN: 外交场合国家之间递交的事实摘要或立场陈述
senses.example: The embassy delivered a memorandum on the border talks.
senses.exampleCN: 使馆递交了一份关于边境谈判的备忘录。
senses.why: Diplomacy needs a record that is formal but not a treaty, which is exactly what a note in writing gives.
senses.whyCN: 外交需要一个正式但不必是条约的记录，而这正是书面备忘所提供的东西。

senses.title: A published statement of policy
senses.definition: a written statement issued by a government or a corporation to set out a policy or a position
senses.definitionCN: 政府或公司为阐明政策或立场而发布的书面声明
senses.example: The department issued a memorandum on data handling.
senses.exampleCN: 该部门发布了一份关于数据处理的备忘录。
senses.why: Organizations need the same note to reach everyone at once, so it grows from reminder into policy.
senses.whyCN: 组织需要同一张便条同时到达所有人，于是它从备忘长成了政策。

senses.title: A legal short form
senses.definition: in law and finance, a short document setting out terms, shares offered, or the purpose of a company
senses.definitionCN: 法律与金融中列明条款、发行股份或公司宗旨的简短文件
senses.example: The memorandum listed the shares the company may issue.
senses.exampleCN: 这份备忘录列明了公司可发行的股份。
senses.why: A legal document is a record others will consult, so the reminder note becomes a fixed term of art.
senses.whyCN: 法律文件是供他人查阅的记录，于是备忘便条固定成了一个专业术语。

senses.title: The abbreviation memo
senses.definition: the short everyday form memo, standing for the same office note
senses.definitionCN: 日常口语中的短形 memo，指同一种办公便条
senses.example: Read the memo before the meeting starts.
senses.exampleCN: 会议开始前先读一下这份便条。
senses.why: An office writes so many notes that the long word is clipped to five letters.
senses.whyCN: 办公室写的便条太多，长词被截成了五个字母。

senses.title: A record of terms for later negotiation
senses.titleCN: 谈判提纲；记录备忘文件
senses.definition: in commerce, a written summary of price, terms, or offers given to a buyer or seller as a basis for negotiation
senses.definitionCN: 商业中交给买方或卖方、作为谈判基础的报价、条款或条件摘要
senses.example: The broker emailed a memorandum with the asking price.
senses.exampleCN: 经纪人电邮了一份写明要价的备忘录。
senses.why: Negotiation grows from what each side remembers having offered, so the note becomes a working document.
senses.whyCN: 谈判从各方记得自己提出过什么开始，于是这张便条成了工作文件。

senses.title: Memorandum as a prefixed heading
senses.definition: the word printed at the head of a note or letter to mark its official purpose
senses.definitionCN: 印在便条或信件开头的字样，用以标明其正式用途
senses.example: The sheet carried the heading memorandum, date, and subject line.
senses.exampleCN: 这张纸的抬头写着备忘录、日期和主题行。
senses.why: Once the word had become a document type, it could also be a printed label.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词成了文种，它也可以直接作为印刷标签。

intro.en: Memorandum is not an English invention: it is a Latin gerundive meaning a thing to be remembered, freely used in Latin and, since the sixteenth century, as a heading for notes in English.
intro.cn: memorandum 不是英语的新造词，而是拉丁语的「将来被动分词」，意为「应被记住之事」；它在拉丁语中广泛使用，自十六世纪起又作为便条的抬头进入英语。

items.en: Memor meant mindful or remembering. Its deeper origin is uncertain, and any earlier stem proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: memor 意为「留心的、记得的」。它的更深来源不确定，为它设想的更早词干都属于重构。

items.en: Memorare, to bring to mind, formed a gerundive memorandum, literally that which is to be remembered, plural memoranda.
items.cn: 动词 memorare（使想起）构成将来被动分词 memorandum，字面为「应被记住之事」，复数为 memoranda。

items.en: Latin kept memorandum in standing phrases, such as memorandae rei causa, for the sake of a thing to be remembered.
items.cn: 拉丁语把 memorandum 放在固定短语里，如 memorandae rei causa，意为「为了这件须记住的事」。

items.en: Memorandum enters English as an ornamental Latin word at the head of documents, a warning to read on.
items.cn: memorandum 先在十五世纪作为装饰性的拉丁语，印在文件开头，提醒读者继续读下去。

items.en: It settles as a noun for a note of matters to be remembered, and plural memoranda is soon in use.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，它固定为名词，指记录须记住之事的便条，复数 memoranda 也很快通行。

items.en: Office practice and diplomacy extend it to short policy notes, and it is clipped to memo, with the plural memorandums also common.
items.cn: 办公与外交的实践把它的范围扩展到简短的政策说明，并把它截短为 memo，复数 memorandums 也很常见。

note.en: The first group holds words built on the same root of remembering, from memo to memorial; the second holds the written records a memorandum is often confused with.
note.cn: 第一组是由「记住」这一词根构成的词，从 memo 到 memorial；第二组常是与备忘录容易混淆的书面记录。

entries.definition: a list of matters to be dealt with at a meeting, literally things to be done
entries.definitionCN: 会上待办事项的清单，字面为「必须被做之事」；与 memorandum 共享拉丁语将来被动分词词尾，只是词干不同。

entries.definition: the Latin plural of the word, kept alongside memorandums
entries.definitionCN: 保留拉丁语中性复数词尾的复数形式，与 memorandums 并用。

entries.definition: the everyday clipping used in offices
entries.definitionCN: 办公室里日常使用的截短形式。

entries.definition: a monument or fund kept in the memory of a person
entries.definitionCN: 为纪念某人而设立的纪念物或基金。

entries.definition: to commit to memory deliberately
entries.definitionCN: 有意地把材料记进记忆。

entries.definition: a board or sheet posted where many people will read it
entries.definitionCN: 张贴在众人可见之处的告示或纸张

entries.definition: a letter sent to many people at once with the same content
entries.definitionCN: 内容相同、一次寄给许多人的信件

entries.definition: a legal summary of the facts and law of a case
entries.definitionCN: 案件事实与法律要点的书面摘要

entries.definition: a set of papers collected on one person or one case
entries.definitionCN: 围绕某个人或某案件收集起来的一叠材料

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin gerundive ending, the real plural forms, and the office phrases in which the word actually occurs.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语的将来被动分词词尾、真实的复数形式，以及这个词真正出现的办公搭配。

normal.en: The ending -um is Latin for a thing that must be done, so the word says this is to be remembered.
normal.cn: 词尾 -um 是拉丁语「必须被做之事」的形式，所以这个词是说「这是要被记住的」。

normal.en: The plural is both memorandums and memoranda, the second keeping the Latin form.
normal.cn: 复数既可以是 memorandums，也可以是保留拉丁形式的 memoranda。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: a memorandum of understanding, an internal memorandum, circulate a memorandum.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：谅解备忘录、内部备忘录、传阅备忘录。

normal.en: In an office it is cut to memo, which is why a memo is a memorandum and never a letter.
normal.cn: 在办公室里它被截成 memo，所以便条是备忘录的简写，而不是信件。

normal.en: Compare memory: memory is the store, and a memorandum is the paper that spares the store.
normal.cn: 对比 memory：memory 是储藏，memorandum 是省下这份储藏的那张纸。

abstract.en: Picture a thin sheet clipped in a file, the first line printed so that nobody can forget it.
abstract.cn: 想象一张夹在档案里的薄纸，开头一行印得清楚，谁也不会忘。

abstract.en: Picture a note taped inside a door listing what must not be left behind.
abstract.cn: 想象一张贴在门内侧的纸条，列着千万不能忘带的东西。

abstract.en: Picture two signatures at the foot of one sheet, agreeing to remember the same terms.
abstract.cn: 想象同一张纸底部有两个签名，表示记得同一套条款。

examples.en: The office circulated a memorandum explaining the new hours.
examples.cn: 办公室传阅了一份说明新工作时间的备忘录。

examples.en: She wrote a memorandum to herself about the call.
examples.cn: 她给自己写了一张关于那通电话的备忘便条。

examples.en: Ministers signed a memorandum of understanding on water.
examples.cn: 各国部长签署了一份关于水资源的谅解备忘录。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「memor」是「记忆」，「andum」提示「须做之事」——合起来就是一张写着「此事须记住」的纸；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 memor（留心的、记得的）→ memorare（使想起）→ 将来被动分词 memorandum（应被记住之事，复数 memoranda）→ 英语 memorandum，核心义「写下以免忘记的东西」。memor 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses run from a private reminder to an instrument of diplomacy and law. The same sheet of paper first helps one mind, then an office, then an organization, and finally a state speak to another state.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从一张私人备忘的纸条，一路走到外交与法律的文件。同一张纸先帮助一个人，再帮助一个办公室，再帮助一个机构，最后让一个国家向另一个国家说话。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin sheet clipped in a file with one thing to say at the top, so that it will be remembered by everyone who must act.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张夹在档案里的薄纸，开头只写一件要说的事，好让所有需要照办的人都记住。

branches.en: THE OFFICE NOTE: the full word and its clipped form memo name the same everyday sheet.
branches.cn: 办公便条：完整形式与截短的 memo 指的是同一张日常纸条。

branches.en: THE PRIVATE REMINDER: the earliest use, one mind writing to its own future.
branches.cn: 私人备忘：最早的用法，一个头脑写给自己的将来。

branches.en: TERMS ON PAPER: an agreement recorded, and a summary of terms used as a base for bargaining.
branches.cn: 纸上的条款：被记录的协议，以及作为议价基础的条款摘要。

branches.en: SPEAKING FOR A BODY: a diplomatic note, and a published statement of policy.
branches.cn: 代表机构发言：外交备忘录与公开发布的政策声明。

branches.en: TECHNICAL FORM: a legal instrument, and the printed heading that marks a note as this kind of document.
branches.cn: 技术形态：法律文件，以及把便条标为此类文件的印刷抬头。

intro.en: Memorandum needs no affix added in English, because it arrives complete from Latin; its parts are memor, the verb stem, and -andum, the ending of a thing that must be done.
intro.cn: memorandum 在英语里不需要再加词缀，因为它从拉丁语整词借入；它的组成是表示记忆的 memor、动词词干，以及表示「必须被做之事」的词尾 -andum。

latinIntro.en: Latin memor and memoria, with the verb memorare, give the whole family; the gerundive ending -andum forms words such as memorandum, agenda and addendum.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 memor、memoria 与动词 memorare 衍生出整族词；将来被动分词词尾 -andum 构成 memorandum、agenda、addendum 等词。

items.example: Memor is the stem behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: memor 是整族词共同的词干。

items.example: Memorare turns the adjective into an action.
items.exampleCN: memorare 把这个形容词变成了动作。

items.example: The ending -andum marks duty in memorandum.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -andum 在 memorandum 中标记了「应该」。

items.example: The whole word is borrowed complete.
items.exampleCN: 整个词是整词借入的。

items.example: The plural memoranda keeps the Latin -a.
items.exampleCN: 复数 memoranda 保留了拉丁语词尾 -a。

items.meaningCN: 办公用语中的截短形式
items.example: Memo is clipped after three syllables.
items.exampleCN: memo 裁掉了后面的音节。

items.example: A memorandum spares memory is not the claim; it spares the need.
items.exampleCN: 备忘录省下的是「要记住的必要」，而不是记忆本身。

items.example: Memorial and memorandum split early into object and paper.
items.exampleCN: memorial 与 memorandum 很早就分成实物与纸张两路。

items.example: Agenda shares the gerundive ending with memorandum.
items.exampleCN: agenda 与 memorandum 共享同一将来被动分词词尾。

definition_zh: 记住；背熟；熟记
definition_en: to learn something so exactly that it can be recalled without looking at the text
core_image: 合上书本，闭着眼把一段台词从第一句念到最后一句
scene: 下课铃响前，学生合上剧本，把台词从头到尾默念了一遍，一句也没看纸。The cast had to memorise the whole script before the first rehearsal.
sceneCN: 这里 memorise 是「背熟」（第 1 个义项：有意识地把材料记进记忆）；句意：第一次排练前，全体演员必须把整部剧本背熟。

derivatives.zh: 记忆的过程；背诵（动词加 -ion 构成动作名词，英式拼写作 -isation）
记忆；记忆力（同出拉丁 memoria）
值得记住的；难忘的（词根加 -able，由「记住」转为「值得被记住」）
备忘录（拉丁将来被动分词，字面为「应被记住之事」）
纪念（前缀具「共同」义，由「记住」转为「众人共同记住」）

senses.title: Fix in the mind on purpose
