senses.definition: to commit facts or words to memory by deliberate effort so that they can be recalled later
senses.definitionCN: 有意识地努力把事实或文字送进记忆，以便日后回想
senses.example: She memorises ten new characters every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 她每天早上记十个新字。
senses.why: The suffix turns a noun of memory into an action, so the word names the act of filling memory.
senses.whyCN: 后缀把「记忆」的名词变成了动作，所以这个词指的是往记忆里填充的动作。

senses.title: Learn a text word for word
senses.definition: to learn a speech, a poem, or a part so exactly that every word can be said in the right order
senses.definitionCN: 把讲稿、诗歌或角色台词学到一字不差、次序不乱的程度
senses.example: The actor memorised the monologue in two days.
senses.exampleCN: 这位演员两天里背熟了那段独白。
senses.why: Where memory must reproduce exact words, the verb means word for word rather than in substance.
senses.whyCN: 当记忆必须复现确切字句时，这个动词指一字不差，而不是大意对了就行。

senses.title: Remember a route or a sequence
senses.definition: to learn the order of places, steps, or names well enough to follow it without help
senses.definitionCN: 把地点、步骤或名称的次序学到无须帮助也能照做
senses.example: Drivers memorise the delivery route before winter closes the passes.
senses.exampleCN: 司机们在冬季封山之前就记住了送货路线。
senses.why: A route is a sequence, and a sequence is held by order, so memory here is spatial and ordered.
senses.whyCN: 路线是一个次序，次序靠顺序被握住，所以这里的记忆是空间性的、有序的。

senses.title: Learn by repetition without understanding
senses.definition: to retain material through drills and repetition, often with little grasp of what it means
senses.definitionCN: 靠操练与重复记住材料，往往并不真正理解其含义
senses.example: Previous classes memorised the tables without ever using them.
senses.exampleCN: 以前的班级只是把表格背下来，却从没真正用过。
senses.why: The word itself is neutral, but schooling gives it the criticism that repetition replaces understanding.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本身中性，但学校语境让它带上了「重复取代理解」的批评。

senses.title: Store a result in computing
senses.definition: in computing, to store a computed result so that later calls need not repeat the work
senses.definitionCN: 计算机中指把计算好的结果存起来，使之后的调用不必重算
senses.example: The program memorises results of slow calls.
senses.exampleCN: 程序会把耗时调用的结果存下来。
senses.why: A machine keeps what it has been given, so the human verb is borrowed for writing into its store.
senses.whyCN: 机器会把给它的东西留着，于是人的动词被借去表示写入机器的存储。

senses.title: Take note of a detail
senses.definition: to make a deliberate mental note of a name, a face, or a number for later use
senses.definitionCN: 对姓名、面孔或数字特意留心并记住，以备后用
senses.example: The guard memorised the number plate as the car left.
senses.exampleCN: 车开走时，门卫把车牌号记了下来。
senses.why: Attention without rehearsal still counts, which shows how wide the verb is.
senses.whyCN: 只靠注意而不反复练习也算，可见这个动词的范围很宽。

senses.title: Perform without the text
senses.definition: to learn a piece or a speech so well that it can be delivered without notes or music
senses.definitionCN: 把曲子或讲稿学到不看谱、不看稿也能完成
senses.example: She memorised the sonata one page at a time.
senses.exampleCN: 她一页一页地把那首奏鸣曲背了下来。
senses.why: Performing without the script is the proof that the exact form is held inside.
senses.whyCN: 脱稿完成是「确切的形式已被握在心里」的证据。

senses.title: Memorise as a study habit
senses.definition: used in study advice about methods that repeat material until it sticks, often before an examination
senses.definitionCN: 在学习建议中指把材料反复练习到记住的方法，常发生在考试之前
senses.example: Students who memorise the day before forget within a week.
senses.exampleCN: 考前一天才强记的学生，一周之内就忘了。
senses.why: Advice needs a plain verb for the habit, so the act becomes the name of a study routine.
senses.whyCN: 学习建议需要用朴素的动词指称这个习惯，于是动作成了某种学习套路的名称。

senses.title: Memorise a set of words or symbols
senses.definition: to learn a fixed set such as a vocabulary list, a code, or a formula, learned as units
senses.definitionCN: 把词表、密码或公式等固定的组合当成一个整体来记住
senses.example: He memorised the phone number in two groups.
senses.exampleCN: 他把电话号码分成两组记了下来。
senses.why: Sets are remembered in chunks, so the verb often takes a countable list as its object.
senses.whyCN: 成套的东西按组块记忆，所以这个动词常带一个可数的清单作宾语。

intro.en: Memorise is Latin memoria, meaning memory, plus the verb ending -ise, the British spelling of a suffix that came to English through French from Latin -izare and Greek -izein. The American form memorize is spelled with -ize.
intro.cn: memorise 是拉丁语 memoria「记忆」加动词词尾 -ise 构成；这个后缀经法语、上溯拉丁 -izare 与希腊 -izein 进入英语，英式拼作 -ise，美式拼作 -ize。

items.en: Memor meant mindful or remembering. The deeper origin of the stem is uncertain, and earlier forms offered for it are reconstructions.
items.cn: memor 意为「留心的、记得的」。这个词干的更深来源不确定，为它设想的更早形式都是重构。

items.en: Memoria named memory both as the ability and as the thing remembered, and gave the whole family its stem.
items.cn: memoria 既指记忆能力，也指被记住之事，并为整族词提供了词干。

items.en: The verb ending goes back to Greek -izein, makers of doing, through Latin -izare and French -iser.
items.cn: 这个动词词尾上溯希腊语 -izein（表「做」），再经拉丁 -izare 与法语 -iser 进入英语。

items.en: The verb is first recorded in the sixteenth century, at first in the sense of putting something into writing.
items.cn: 这个动词在十六世纪已有记录，最初意为「把某事写下来」。

items.en: The sense of learning by heart is recorded from the nineteenth century, when schooling began to teach fixed texts by repetition.
items.cn: 「背熟」这一义项自十九世纪起才有记录，当时学校教育开始靠重复教授固定的文本。

items.en: Both spellings now circulate: -ise is standard in British usage, and -ize in American usage, with the same pronunciation.
items.cn: 如今两种拼写并行：英式通行 -ise，美式通行 -ize，读音完全相同。

note.en: The first group holds the spellings and the root relatives this verb is most often mixed with; the second holds other verbs for getting something into the mind.
note.cn: 第一组是这个词最容易被混淆的拼写形式与同根词；第二组是其他表示「把东西弄进头脑」的动词。

entries.definition: the same verb written with the American -ize ending
entries.definitionCN: 同一个词的另一种写法，用美式 -ize 词尾。

entries.definition: the past tense and past participle of the same verb
entries.definitionCN: 同一个词的过去式与过去分词形式。

entries.definition: the noun for the act or process of learning by heart
entries.definitionCN: 表示「背熟这一动作或过程」的名词。

entries.definition: the store or faculty that the verb fills
entries.definitionCN: 被这个动词填充的储藏处或能力，即记忆。

entries.definition: a thing built or kept to preserve remembrance
entries.definitionCN: 为保存纪念而建起或留下的实物；只是写法相近，实为名词而非动词。

entries.definition: to gain knowledge or skill, including understanding how something works
entries.definitionCN: 获得知识或技能，包含理解其运作方式

entries.definition: to give over formally; in the phrase commit to memory, to lodge in the mind
entries.definitionCN: 正式交付；在 commit to memory 一语中指送进记忆

entries.definition: to keep what has already been taken in, over time
entries.definitionCN: 把已经吸收的东西长时间保持住

entries.definition: to bring stored information back into the mind
entries.definitionCN: 把存起来的信息重新唤回头脑

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real suffix, the real spelling pair, and the fixed objects the verb usually takes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的词尾、真实的两种拼写，以及这个动词常接的固定宾语。

normal.en: Memoria is memory and the ending makes a verb, so memorise means to make a thing into memory.
normal.cn: memoria 是「记忆」，词尾使它成为动词，所以 memorise 意为「使某物成为记忆」。

normal.en: British spelling uses -ise, American spelling uses -ize; both are pronounced the same.
normal.cn: 英式拼作 -ise，美式拼作 -ize，两者读音相同。

normal.en: Fixed objects: memorise a passage, memorise lines, memorise a route, memorise for an exam.
normal.cn: 固定宾语：背一段文字、背台词、记路线、为考试强记。

normal.en: The family runs memory, memorable, memorandum and commemorate, and all of them start from the same noun.
normal.cn: 同族词有 memory、memorable、memorandum、commemorate，全都从同一个名词出发。

normal.en: The word names the putting in, not the keeping: recall and retain happen afterwards.
normal.cn: 这个词指「装进去」，不指「保持」；recall 与 retain 都发生在之后。

abstract.en: Picture a script closing on the table while the mouth keeps moving without it.
abstract.cn: 想象剧本在桌上合起，嘴唇却仍在没有书的情况下继续动。

abstract.en: Picture a route walked twice with eyes shut, every turn already known.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路闭着眼走过两遍，每个转弯都已知道。

abstract.en: Picture a phone number broken into three blocks and stored that way.
abstract.cn: 想象一个电话号码被切成三段，并以此方式存进脑中。

examples.en: Pupils must memorise the irregular verbs by Friday.
examples.cn: 学生们必须在周五前背熟不规则动词。

examples.en: He memorised the map of the metro in a week.
examples.cn: 他一周就把地铁线路图记住了。

examples.en: Better to understand the rule than to memorise ten exceptions.
examples.cn: 弄懂规则比背下十个例外更好。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「记忆」加「使成为」——把材料做成记忆；背台词、记路线、存进机器，都是同一个动作换了落点。这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 memoria（记忆）→ 动词词尾 -ise（经法语 -iser、拉丁 -izare，上溯希腊 -izein，表「使成为、做」）→ 英语 memorise，核心义「使某物进入记忆」。memoria 出自 memor（留心的），memor 更深来源不确定，属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one act, putting something into memory on purpose. It lands on facts, on an exact text, on a route, on drilling, on a machine store, on a noticed detail, on performance without notes, on a study habit, and on a list of words.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿着同一个动作展开：有意把某物送进记忆。它依次落在事实、确切的文本、一条路线、机械操练、机器的存储、被刻意留意的一个细节、无稿的表演、一种学习习惯，以及一份词语清单上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a script closed on the table and a voice still going on, word after word, without looking.
core.cn: 核心意象：剧本合放在桌上，而声音仍不看稿地一句接一句往下走。

branches.en: TAKING IN: the general act, and the smaller act of marking one detail on purpose.
branches.cn: 收入：泛称的动作，以及刻意标记某一个细节的较小动作。

branches.en: EXACT UNITS: a text word for word, and a fixed set of words or symbols.
branches.cn: 确切单位：逐字的一段文本，以及一组固定的词或符号。

branches.en: ORDERED SPACE: a route kept as a sequence of turns.
branches.cn: 有序空间：一条作为转弯序列被记住的路线。

branches.en: REPEAT OR PRACTISE: drilling without understanding, and the study habit named after it.
branches.cn: 重复或练习：不求理解的操练，以及由此得名的那种学习习惯。

branches.en: NOTES REMOVED: a machine storing results, and a player performing from memory.
branches.cn: 去掉稿本：存下结果的机器，以及凭记忆演奏的表演者。

intro.en: Memorise is a Latin noun of memory with a verb ending added, so the two halves can be read: the storage, and the act of putting something in it.
intro.cn: memorise 是「记忆」的拉丁名词加上动词词尾，两半都可读：储藏的地方，以及把东西放进去的动作。

latinIntro.en: Latin memor and memoria give the nouns and adjectives of the family; the verb ending, Latin -izare from Greek -izein, also forms realise, organise and modernise.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 memor 与 memoria 构成这一族的名称与形容词；动词词尾源自希腊 -izein 的拉丁 -izare，也构成 realise、organise、modernise。

items.example: Memor is the stem shared by the whole family.
items.exampleCN: memor 是整族词共有的词干。

items.example: Memoria names the store the verb fills.
items.exampleCN: memoria 指的是这个动词所填充的储藏处。

items.example: The suffix -ise turns the noun of memory into a verb.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ise 把「记忆」的名词变成动词。

items.example: American usage writes memorize with the -ize ending.
items.exampleCN: 美式用法把 memorize 写成 -ize 词尾。

items.example: The suffix -tion forms memorisation.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -tion 构成 memorisation。

items.example: The suffix -able forms memorable.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -able 构成 memorable。

items.example: The prefix com- forms commemorate.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 com- 构成 commemorate。

items.example: Memory is what memorise works on.
items.exampleCN: memory 是 memorise 所作用的对象。

items.meaning: the act of learning by heart
items.example: Memorisation needs repetition, recall does not.
items.exampleCN: 背熟需要重复，回想则不需要。

definition_zh: 威胁；危险的人或物；威胁性；使受威胁
definition_en: something or someone dangerous that threatens people, or the state of being threatened
core_image: 举起的拳头悬在头顶，投下的阴影压过来
scene: 夜里回家的路上，路灯坏了，巷子深处有人在喊叫。A stranger shouting in the dark alley was a real menace to anyone walking home late.
sceneCN: 这里 menace 是「威胁性的人或物」（第 1 个义项：造成危险、令人害怕的人或东西）；句意：暗巷里大喊的陌生人，对每个深夜回家的人都是实实在在的危险。

collocations.zh: 公害；对公众的危险人物

derivatives.zh: 由 menace 加 -ing 构成，义为「威胁的；险恶的」
由 menacing 加 -ly 构成，义为「充满威胁地」
由过去分词转作形容词，义为「受到威胁的」

senses.title: A dangerous person or thing
senses.definition: a person, group, or thing that is likely to cause harm
senses.definitionCN: 可能造成伤害的人、群体或事物
senses.example: Abandoned factories are a menace to local wildlife.
senses.exampleCN: 废弃的工厂对当地野生动物是一种危害。
senses.why: The Latin minacia meant a projecting threat, so what projects danger outward becomes a menace itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 minacia 指「伸出来的威胁」，因此把危险向外投射出去的人或物本身就成了 menace。

senses.title: A spoken or intended threat
senses.definition: a warning that harm will be done to someone, often meant to frighten
senses.definitionCN: 宣告将加害于人的警告，多意在吓唬对方
senses.example: He fixed the neighbours with a cold menace in his voice.
senses.exampleCN: 他用冷冰冰的威胁语气盯着邻居们。
senses.why: The threatening gesture of the core image is heard in words, and the menace becomes a warning aimed at a person.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象中那个威胁性的手势从嘴里说出来，menace 就变成了针对某人的警告。

senses.title: The quality of being threatening
senses.definition: a threatening quality felt in a person, a place, or an atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 从人、地方或气氛中感到的威胁性质
senses.example: A quiet menace hung over the empty street.
senses.exampleCN: 空荡的街道上笼罩着一种无声的威胁。
senses.why: Once the threat stops naming a danger and only hovers in the air, it turns into a suggestive quality rather than a thing.
senses.whyCN: 当威胁不再指名某个危险物、而只是弥漫在空气中时，它就变成了某种暗示性的氛围质地，而不再是一个实体。

senses.title: To threaten or endanger
senses.definition: to put someone or something in danger, or to warn of harm
senses.definitionCN: 使某人或某物陷入危险，或警告将加害
senses.example: Rising seas menace low-lying coastal towns.
senses.exampleCN: 不断上升的海平面威胁着低洼的沿海城镇。
senses.why: The noun image of a raised fist passes into the verb, where the threatening shadow is cast over a target.
senses.whyCN: 名词中那只举起的拳头过渡成动词，威胁的阴影直接笼罩在某个对象身上。

senses.title: An annoying nuisance
senses.titleCN: 讨人烦的家伙；碍事的东西
senses.definition: a person or thing that irritates people, used informally and often half jokingly
senses.definitionCN: 惹人烦的人或东西，非正式说法，常带半开玩笑的语气
senses.example: That little brother of hers is a real menace with a water pistol.
senses.exampleCN: 她那个小弟弟拿着水枪，真是个讨人嫌的家伙。
senses.why: The strong word for danger is softened for small everyday harm, so a playful pest inherits the same word in a joking tone.
senses.whyCN: 表示危险的强词被用来形容日常的小麻烦，于是爱捣乱的人就带着玩笑口吻沿用了这个词。

intro.en: Menace comes from Latin minacia, a threatening, from minax, overhanging or threatening, which grew out of minae, the jutting points of walls or the threats in a face.
intro.cn: menace 来自拉丁语 minacia（威胁），源自 minax（突出悬垂的、威胁的），而 minax 又出自 minae（城墙突出的尖端，或脸上威胁的神色）。

items.en: Minae names jutting points and, by extension, threats; minax describes what hangs over a person.
items.cn: minae 指突出的尖角，引申为威胁；minax 形容悬在某人头顶的东西。

items.en: Minacia, a threatening or the state of being threatened, is recorded in later Latin.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语中 minacia 已表示「威胁」或「受威胁状态」。

items.en: Menaçe carries the word into French with the meaning of a threat or threatening conduct.
items.cn: 古法语 menaçe 把这个词带入法语，义为威胁或威胁性的举动。

items.en: From around the fourteenth century the noun names a threat in English, and the verb appears alongside it.
items.cn: 大约自十四世纪起，这个词在英语中作名词表示威胁，动词也随之出现。

items.en: The word widens from personal threats to dangers to social order, public health, and nature.
items.cn: 它的范围从针对个人的威胁扩展到对社会秩序、公共卫生与自然环境的危害。

note.en: Menace is the noun of threatening, related by form to menacing and by meaning to threat, danger, and peril.
note.cn: menace 是表示「威胁」的名词，形式上与 menacing 相邻，意义上与 threat、danger、peril 相邻。

entries.definition: seeming likely to cause harm
entries.definitionCN: 由 menace 加 -ing 构成，义为「凶险的；威胁的」

entries.definition: willing to be led or persuaded, with a similar-looking ending
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近，词源不同，义为「顺从的；愿意接受的」

entries.definition: threatening, in a rare literary use
entries.definitionCN: 与目标词同出拉丁语 minax，是罕见的书面形容词，义为「威胁的」

entries.definition: a statement or sign that harm will come
entries.definitionCN: 近义词，指将造成伤害的言辞或迹象，范围比 menace 更日常

entries.definition: the possibility of harm
entries.definitionCN: 近义词，指受伤害的可能性，比 menace 更中性

entries.definition: serious and immediate danger
entries.definitionCN: 近义词，指严重而迫近的危险，语气正式

normalIntro.en: Menace keeps the image of something hanging over a person, a threat that juts out and casts a shadow.
normalIntro.cn: menace 保留着「悬在人头顶的东西」这一意象，一种伸出来的、投下阴影的威胁。

normal.en: A menace is what poses a menace to others, so the word names both the threat and the thing that threatens.
normal.cn: 造成 menace 的东西本身也被叫作 menace，所以这个词既指威胁，也指带来威胁的人或物。

normal.en: The common phrase pose a menace to marks danger directed at a target.
normal.cn: 常见搭配 pose a menace to 表示危险正指向某个对象。

normal.en: Menacing is the everyday adjective, as in a menacing look.
normal.cn: menacing 是日常形容词，例如「一脸凶相」。

normal.en: Compare threat: a threat is usually spoken, while a menace is more often a presence that frightens.
normal.cn: 对比 threat：threat 多指说出来的威胁，menace 更常指令人害怕的存在。

normal.en: The verb shares the spelling of the noun, as in floods that menace a village.
normal.cn: 动词与名词拼写相同，如洪水威胁村庄。

abstract.en: Picture a raised fist that never comes down, only hovers.
abstract.cn: 想象一只举起的拳头始终不落下，只是悬在那里。

abstract.en: Hear a low voice saying you will be sorry.
abstract.cn: 听见一个压低的声音对你说「你会后悔的」。

abstract.en: Feel a curtain of cold air pressing on your back.
abstract.cn: 感觉一层冷空气贴着后背压过来。

examples.en: Drunk drivers are a menace to everyone on the road.
examples.cn: 醉酒司机对路上的每个人都是威胁。

examples.en: The old warehouse has been menaced by fire for years.
examples.cn: 这座旧仓库多年来一直受到火灾的威胁。

examples.en: There was a quiet menace in the way she smiled.
examples.cn: 她微笑的方式里透着一股不动声色的威胁。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「没呢事」——有人冲你挥着拳头说「别以为没呢事」，就是在威胁你；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 minae（突出的尖角；威胁）→ minax（突出悬垂的、威胁的）→ minacia（威胁）→ 古法语 menaçe → 英语 menace，核心义「悬在头顶的威胁」。

sensesIntro.en: Menace starts from the concrete danger that threatens others, moves to the spoken threat, then to the threatening atmosphere, the verb of endangering, and finally the joking pest.
sensesIntro.cn: menace 先从具体威胁他人的危险物出发，过渡到说出口的威胁，再指弥漫的威胁气氛、作动词表示危及，最后落到玩笑式的「捣蛋鬼」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a raised fist that hangs over a person and casts a shadow.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只举起的拳头悬在人头顶，投下阴影。

branches.en: The danger itself is named by the overhanging image at its most concrete.
branches.cn: 危险之物是悬垂意象最具体的落点，义项集中指向名词。

branches.en: A threat spoken aloud turns the overhang into words aimed at a listener.
branches.cn: 说出口的威胁把悬垂的动作变成针对听者的话语。

branches.en: A threatening air keeps the shape but loses the named object.
branches.cn: 威胁性气氛保留了形状，却不再指向具体的对象。

branches.en: The verb moves the shadow from the fist onto the target.
branches.cn: 动词把阴影从拳头移到被威胁的目标身上。

branches.en: The same word shrinks from social danger to everyday nuisance.
branches.cn: 同一个词从社会性危险缩小到日常小麻烦。

intro.en: Menace is a Latin noun of threat that has added a verb and the adjectives menacing and menaced in English.
intro.cn: menace 是拉丁语中表示威胁的名词，英语中又发展出动词以及 menacing、menaced 两个形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin minae means jutting points or threats, minax means overhanging or threatening, and minacia means a threat.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 minae 意为突出的尖角或威胁，minax 意为悬垂的、威胁的，minacia 意为威胁。

items.example: Minae gives the image of points jutting out.
items.exampleCN: minae 提供尖端突出的意象。

items.example: Minax describes what hangs over a person.
items.exampleCN: minax 描述悬在人头顶的东西。

items.example: Minacia is the direct source of the French word.
items.exampleCN: minacia 是法语词的直接来源。

items.example: The Old French noun carries the cedilla that English later loses.
items.exampleCN: 古法语名词带有英语后来舍弃的软音符。

items.meaning: a dangerous person or thing; a threat
items.example: The noun names a danger that threatens others.
items.exampleCN: 名词指威胁他人的危险物。

items.example: The verb needs no change of spelling from the noun.
items.exampleCN: 动词拼写与名词完全相同。

items.meaning: forming an adjective from a verb
items.meaningCN: 由动词构成形容词的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ing forms menacing.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 menacing。

items.example: Menacing describes a look or a cry.
items.exampleCN: menacing 形容神色或叫声。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms menacingly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 menacingly。

items.example: Menaced is the past participle used adjectivally.
items.exampleCN: menaced 是由过去分词转成的形容词。
